title: SEO in 2026: White-Hat Growth, Smart Backlinks, and Why the Old Tricks Are Dying
summary: SEO in 2026: White-Hat Growth, Smart Backlinks, and Why the Old Tricks Are Dying
text:
SEO in 2026: White-Hat Growth, Smart Backlinks, and Why the Old Tricks Are Dying

Share

2026-05-23

Search engine optimization in 2026 looks very different from the SEO most marketers learned five years ago.

The era of:

mass spam backlinks

keyword stuffing

AI-generated garbage pages

fake authority sites

“10,000 backlinks for $5” Fiverr miracles

is collapsing fast.

Search engines got smarter.

AI search changed discovery.

Users became less patient.

And trust became the new ranking signal.

Today, the websites winning organic traffic are not necessarily the biggest brands.

They are the brands that:

publish consistently

build real topical authority

earn trust signals

create discoverable content

distribute intelligently

understand audience intent better than competitors

White-hat SEO is no longer the “slow boring method.”

In 2026, it is actually the most scalable strategy.

What White-Hat SEO Really Means in 2026

White-hat SEO simply means:

optimizing for humans first while staying aligned with search engine guidelines.

That sounds obvious.

But many marketers still optimize for algorithms instead of audiences.

Modern SEO is now deeply connected to:

user behavior

engagement quality

branded searches

content satisfaction

creator authority

entity recognition

cross-platform visibility

Google, AI search engines, YouTube, Reddit, TikTok, and even social algorithms now reinforce each other.

SEO is no longer isolated.

It became part of a larger “attention ecosystem.”

The Biggest SEO Shift Happening Right Now

In the past:

backlinks alone could rank weak content

Now:

weak content with strong backlinks often collapses over time

Search engines increasingly measure:

content usefulness

originality

user retention

engagement patterns

brand mentions

expertise consistency

This is why many “SEO-only websites” disappeared after recent updates.

Meanwhile:

niche creators

personal brands

genuine businesses

communities

expert-driven blogs

are gaining visibility.

Authenticity became algorithmically valuable.

Which is honestly hilarious considering the internet spent 15 years rewarding the exact opposite.

Backlinks Still Matter — But Differently

Backlinks are still important in 2026.

Very important.

But the definition of a “good backlink” changed dramatically.

A strong backlink today is:

contextually relevant

placed naturally

surrounded by meaningful content

coming from a trusted source

capable of generating actual clicks

Google increasingly values:

relevance over volume

trust over manipulation

engagement over raw link count

One relevant mention from a respected niche site can outperform hundreds of low-quality backlinks.

That is a massive shift.

The White-Hat Backlink Strategy That Actually Works

Here is what smart marketers are doing in 2026.

1. Build Linkable Assets

People link to:

original research

statistics

case studies

tools

calculators

templates

controversial opinions

useful guides

Nobody wants to link to:

“Top 7 Social Media Tips You Need Today!!!”

The internet already has 900 million of those.

Create something worth referencing.

Examples:

industry benchmarks

AI workflow tutorials

automation experiments

ranking studies

platform growth reports

marketing frameworks

2. Use Content Distribution Aggressively

Publishing alone is dead.

Distribution is now half the SEO game.

Good SEO marketers distribute content through:

X/Twitter

Reddit

LinkedIn

Facebook groups

niche communities

YouTube Shorts

newsletters

Discord servers

The goal is not just traffic.

The goal is:

visibility

mentions

citations

natural backlinks

branded searches

Search engines increasingly notice when people actively discuss your brand online.

SEO and Social Media Are Now Connected

This is one of the most important realities of 2026.

A blog post can gain rankings because:

a Reddit thread discussed it

creators shared it

YouTube mentioned it

X users quoted it

communities bookmarked it

Search visibility and social visibility are merging.

This is why automation tools like

JarveePro

are becoming useful for white-hat marketers.

Not for spam.

But for:

distribution workflows

scheduling

multi-platform consistency

content amplification

audience management

Modern SEO rewards visibility momentum.

How to Build Backlinks Without Looking Like a Spammer

Here is the realistic approach.

Focus on:

relationships

relevance

expertise

consistency

Good methods:

guest posting on real sites

collaborating with creators

publishing unique data

becoming quotable

joining niche communities

answering questions publicly

building free tools/resources

digital PR campaigns

Bad methods:

mass blog comments

PBN farms

AI spam sites

irrelevant directory blasts

automated forum spam

fake outreach emails

If your backlink strategy feels like a scam operation from a movie involving burner phones and energy drinks, it is probably not white-hat.

AI Content Is Not the Enemy

Low-quality content is.

AI-assisted writing is now normal.

Almost every major marketing team uses AI in some form.

The problem is when marketers:

publish unedited AI spam

produce generic content

chase volume over value

create pages nobody actually wants

The winning formula is:

AI-assisted creation + human insight + original experience

That combination scales extremely well.

The Smart SEO Formula for 2026

Here is the practical framework:

Step 1 — Pick a Real Niche

Avoid broad generic topics.

Become known for something specific.

Step 2 — Build Topic Clusters

Create interconnected content around one expertise area.

Search engines reward topical depth.

Step 3 — Publish Consistently

Momentum matters more than perfection.

Step 4 — Distribute Everywhere

Content should travel.

Step 5 — Earn Mentions Naturally

Be useful enough to reference.

Step 6 — Build Brand Searches

People searching your name directly is now a major trust signal.

Step 7 — Optimize User Experience

Fast site.

Readable content.

Clear structure.

No ad apocalypse destroying usability.

SEO in 2026 Is More Human Than Ever

Ironically, after years of manipulation, search engines are now moving back toward rewarding genuinely useful content.

The marketers winning today are not necessarily gaming the algorithm.

They are:

understanding attention

publishing strategically

building trust

creating memorable content

becoming recognizable entities online

White-hat SEO is no longer “safe but slow.”

Done correctly, it is one of the strongest long-term growth assets a business can build.

And unlike spam tactics:

it compounds.

That is the real difference.

Black-hat SEO chases shortcuts.

White-hat SEO builds momentum that survives updates, platform shifts, and AI-driven search changes.

In 2026, that durability matters more than ever.

High engagement

Algorithmic preference

The issue is： does buying Instagram followers

really

For buying Instagram followers and likes, here is the community guideline：

“Foster meaningful and genuine interactions. Help us stay spam-free by not artificially collecting likes, followers, or shares, posting repetitive comments or content, or repeatedly contacting people for commercial purposes without their consent.

Don’t offer money or giveaways of money in exchange for likes, followers, comments or other engagement.

Don’t post content that engages in, promotes, encourages, facilitates, or admits to the offering, solicitation or trade of fake and misleading user reviews or ratings.”

What will happen when if you break the rules：

According to Instagram,

We can remove any content or information you share on the Service if we believe that it violates these Terms of Use, our policies (including our Instagram Community Guidelines), or we are permitted or required to do so by law.

Here’s an example of a service that sells Instagram likes for as little as $1.47.

accounts

summary: SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING TRENDS AND PREDICTIONS FOR 2022
text:
SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING TRENDS AND PREDICTIONS FOR 2022

Share

2021-11-15

We are fast approaching the end of another year marred by COVID, and while many will be glad to see the end of 2021 now that normalcy is about to return, we still have a ways to go before the full economic impact of the pandemic may play out in different ways for decades.

So what can you expect to see from Facebook, Twitter and the rest in 2022? We need to know: which social media trends are going to change the game in 2022?

TikTok will become the most important social network for marketing (??!)

The popular video-sharing social networking platform TikTok allows users to create and share various musical content for the amusement of themselves and others through short musical videos. More than just an entertaining distraction, the app spurs creativity and helps users showcase their talents through music.

TikTok surpassed the 1 billion user mark in September 2021. That made it the 7th most popular social network in the world.

Instagram is the most important channel for influencer marketing, newcomer TikTok has quickly become one of the most popular platforms in the world in less than two years and a rising platform for influencers.

Tips

Create a TikTok account for your branding

Explore TikTok so you can start feeling fluent on the platform and find some ideas

Adapt your TikTok social strategy

Customers will expect to buy items directly on social media

Now, as social media networks continue to expand on in-platform shopping tools, it's clear that social media eCommerce is gaining steam. But, as with any new marketing trend, you might wonder, "Are consumers actually buying products while surfing social media?"

81% of shoppers were already using social media to discover new brands and research products. Many businesses have figured out that letting these users checkout in the same app just makes sense.

There are now more ways than ever to buy products on social media.

Experiment with shoppable posts, or even ads! This will allow customers to see your products in context—and then place an order in just a few taps.

You can also optimize your Instagram product content to show up in the Shopping tab of Instagram's app.

Youtube recently announced its “Shorts” feature for users of the Youtube app. Shorts are 15-seconds long and allow users to compile multiple video clips together, adjust video speeds, and record alongside music hands-free.

text:
Target Your Competitor’s Followers on Instagram with JarveePro: Full Setup & Strategy

Share

2025-07-21

Why Are So Many People Asking the Same Question?”

A few months ago, I found myself in a loop — answering the same client question over and over again.

“Wait… what’s the difference between

Number of Profiles to Follow

and

Number of Followings to Follow

?”

“How do I follow people from my competitor’s page?”

“Why isn’t the delay working?”

I’d explain it 10 different ways, send screenshots, even jump on calls. Still, confusion lingered. But behind that confusion, there was something else —

huge potential

Because this wasn’t just about fixing a setting.

It was about finding out one of the most

underrated, overlooked growth strategies

on Instagram — one that could quietly and consistently drive real followers, without spending a dollar on ads.

And the best part?

It was sitting inside JarveePro all along, waiting to be used the right way.

This post isn’t just a how-to. It’s a breakdown of

why this strategy works

, how to set it up right, and how a small feature turned into a serious advantage for our clients.

Why Targeting Your Competitor’s Followers Just Works

Let’s start with the

psychology

When you follow someone randomly on Instagram, you’re a stranger.

But when you follow someone who already follows a page

like yours

— maybe your competitor, maybe a niche creator — you’re familiar. You fit into the world they’ve already chosen.

That’s what makes this strategy powerful:

The users are already active.

They already like similar content.

They’re far more likely to

follow back

, engage, or click through to your page.

It’s

warm traffic

, not cold.

And with the right tool — JarveePro — you can reach hundreds or thousands of these people

without lifting a finger

, as long as your settings are right.

Breaking Down the JarveePro Strategy

JarveePro’s task system includes something called

FollowHisFollowings

— a feature that sounds simple, but packs serious depth.

Here’s what it does:

You input Instagram profiles (your competitors, influencers, brands in your niche).

JarveePro visits those profiles, goes to their “Following” list (the accounts

they

follow).

Then it starts following a set number of those users — quietly, automatically.

But here’s where it gets tricky — and where most users (and clients) got stuck.

Let’s break it down clearly.

The 3 Core Settings You Must Understand

1.

Target Profiles to Extract From (Per Account)

“Number Of Profile To Follow”

This isn’t about the number of people to follow.

This tells JarveePro:

How many source profiles should we use for this account?

Say you added 10 competitors.

If this is set to

, JarveePro will randomly pick 5 of them per account, and extract followers from them.

Pro Tip

: Stick with 3–5 to keep the data pool fresh and avoid scraping limits.

2.

How Many Users to Follow From Each Profile

“Number Of Followings To Follow”

This is where the action happens.

If set to

20

, it means JarveePro will grab 20 users from each of the 5 source profiles you chose above.

5 profiles × 20 users =

100 follows per task cycle

These are the actual people who’ll be followed.

3.

Delay Between Accounts (in Seconds)

“Account Use Interval(s)”

Here’s the most misunderstood setting.

Many assumed this was in minutes.

It’s not. It’s in

seconds

Set it to

60

for a 1-minute gap between accounts performing the task.

This reduces footprint, makes actions look natural, and avoids triggering Instagram’s rate limits.

Common Mistakes That Hurt Your Results

Even experienced marketers miss these. Here’s what to avoid:

Using Too Many Source Profiles

Instagram may throttle scraping if you bounce through 10+ sources without proper intervals. Keep it to 3–5 per account.

Forgetting Delays

Running tasks back-to-back with 0s delay looks robotic. You’ll burn trust — and your accounts.

Mixing Up “Followers” and “Followings”

You want to extract

followings

— the people your competitors are following. It’s different from their followers.

Not Warming Up New Accounts

Brand-new accounts can’t start with aggressive follow activity. Start slow. Gradually increase volume.

Real Use Case: Turning Confusion Into Conversion

We had a client in the fashion space — managing 10 Instagram accounts targeting streetwear fans.

They were manually following people from competitor pages, getting maybe 50–60 follows per day. It was taking hours.

They switched to JarveePro’s FollowHisFollowings task.

At first, it was chaos. Settings were wrong. Delays were off. Follows weren’t sticking.

So we sat down, optimized the settings:

5 competitor profiles per account

20 followings per profile

60–120 seconds delay

Rotation every 3 hours

Daily limits set to 150–200

Within a week:

Follows per day jumped to 1000+ across accounts

Engagement went up 25%

The client stopped calling with questions

Better yet — we turned that setup into a template used across 12 other clients. Time saved: dozens of hours per week.

Advanced Tips to Use JarveePro Instagram Tool

Use Spintax in Bios/DMs

Make your follow-up messages (if any) dynamic. Randomized messages = higher response rate, lower spam score.

Rotate Between Different Source Profiles Daily

Switch up your competitor input every 2–3 days to avoid saturation.

Combine with Auto-Engagement

JarveePro lets you like a post or story after follow. It increases visibility and follow-back rate.

Use Multiple Accounts with Smart Limits

Instead of blasting 1000 follows on one account, split it across 5–10 accounts for better trust and safety.

Automation Only Works When You Understand the Strategy

Most people use automation tools like brute force.

But Instagram rewards nuance — subtlety, behavior that mimics real users, actions done with intention.

When you understand

why

“FollowHisFollowings” works — and how to structure it the right way — tools like JarveePro become more than software.

They become strategy multipliers.

You don’t need a team of 10 VAs.

You just need a well-oiled setup, a clear targeting plan, and a tool that does the hard work — consistently, quietly, and safely.

Ready to Try It?

Use our optimized

FollowHisFollowings Template

Or set it up yourself with the guide above.

And next time someone asks:

“Wait… what does that setting mean?”

Just send them this post.

The effects of social media on public opinion, What tools shouldn't I miss out?

Share

2024-07-25

The Effects of Social Media on Public Opinion

The influence of social media on public opinion is profound and multifaceted. As platforms like Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and TikTok have become integral to daily life, they have also emerged as powerful tools that shape the way we perceive the world. This blog dig deep into the effects of social media on public opinion, the role of advanced tools like JarveePro in managing social media presence, and the trends shaping social media in 2024, particularly the rise of AI.

The Power of Social Media in Shaping Public Opinion

Social media platforms have democratized the flow of information, allowing anyone with an internet connection to share their views, news, and content with a global audience. This democratization has several significant impacts on public opinion:

Amplification of Voices

: Social media gives a voice to individuals who might otherwise be unheard. Movements like #BlackLivesMatter and #MeToo gained global traction through social media, highlighting issues of racial injustice and sexual harassment.

Echo Chambers

: Algorithms on platforms like Facebook and Twitter often show users content that aligns with their existing beliefs. This can lead to echo chambers, where users are only exposed to opinions similar to their own, reinforcing their beliefs and potentially polarizing public opinion.

Fake News and Misinformation

: The rapid spread of misinformation on social media can shape public opinion based on false or misleading information. This is particularly concerning in contexts like elections or public health crises.

Influence of Influencers

: Social media influencers have significant sway over their followers' opinions and behaviors. Their endorsements can affect public perception of products, brands, and even political issues.

The Role of JarveePro in Managing Social Media Presence

In the complex landscape of social media, tools like JarveePro are essential for effectively managing and optimizing social media strategies. JarveePro is a powerful social media automation software that helps businesses and individuals streamline their social media efforts.

Here’s how JarveePro can be instrumental:

Automating Posts

: Consistency is key in social media marketing. JarveePro allows users to schedule posts across multiple platforms, ensuring a steady flow of content without the need for constant manual updates.

Targeting Audiences

: With JarveePro, users can target specific demographics and interests, ensuring their content reaches the most relevant audiences. This is crucial for shaping public opinion effectively.

Engaging with Followers

: JarveePro automates interactions such as likes, comments, and follows, helping to build a community and engage with followers without overwhelming manual effort.

Analyzing Performance

: JarveePro provides detailed analytics on social media performance, allowing users to track the effectiveness of their strategies and adjust accordingly.

Managing Multiple Accounts

: For businesses and influencers managing multiple social media accounts, JarveePro simplifies the process, allowing for seamless coordination and management from a single dashboard.

Trends in Social Media in 2024

As we move through 2024, several key trends are shaping the social media landscape. These trends are driven largely by advances in technology, particularly artificial intelligence (AI).

AI-Driven Content Creation

: AI is increasingly being used to create content. Tools like OpenAI's GPT-4 can generate text for posts, articles, and even scripts, allowing for more efficient content creation. This can help businesses maintain a robust online presence without dedicating extensive time and resources.

Enhanced Personalization

: AI algorithms are becoming more sophisticated in analyzing user data to provide personalized content. This means users will see more content tailored to their interests, increasing engagement and the effectiveness of social media campaigns.

Improved Customer Service

: AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants are enhancing customer service on social media. These tools can handle inquiries, provide information, and even resolve issues in real-time, improving user experience and satisfaction.

Social Commerce

: The integration of e-commerce with social media platforms is growing. Users can now make purchases directly through social media apps, streamlining the shopping experience and driving sales.

Increased Focus on Privacy

: With growing concerns about data privacy, social media platforms are implementing stricter privacy measures. This includes more transparent data usage policies and better controls for users over their data.

Short-Form Video Content

: The popularity of platforms like TikTok has highlighted the effectiveness of short-form video content. This trend is likely to continue, with more brands and individuals using short videos to capture attention and convey messages quickly.

Rise of Micro-Influencers

: Micro-influencers, with smaller but highly engaged followings, are becoming more valuable to brands. Their authenticity and close connections with their audience make them effective for niche marketing.

Using JarveePro to Catch Up with These Trends

JarveePro’s features align well with these trends, making it an invaluable tool for those looking to get the most out the power of social media in 2024.

Enhanced Personalization

: JarveePro’s advanced targeting capabilities allow users to personalize their content for different audience segments. By analyzing performance data, users can refine their strategies to better meet the interests and preferences of their followers.

Improved Customer Service

: JarveePro can automate responses to common inquiries, ensuring timely engagement with followers. This, combined with AI chatbots, can significantly enhance customer service on social media.

Social Commerce

: JarveePro can automate posts and promotions for products directly linked to e-commerce platforms, facilitating seamless social commerce experiences for users.

Privacy Compliance

: JarveePro’s robust data management features ensure that user data is handled responsibly, aligning with the increased focus on privacy in social media.

Short-Form Video Content

: JarveePro can schedule and automate the posting of short-form videos, ensuring they reach the audience at optimal times. This can help maximize the impact of video content in marketing campaigns.

Micro-Influencer Campaigns

: JarveePro can manage multiple influencer partnerships, automating interactions and tracking performance. This makes it easier to leverage the power of micro-influencers for targeted marketing efforts.

Conclusion

The impact of social media on public opinion is undeniable.

As we look towards 2024, the trends in social media—driven largely by AI—are set to further revolutionize the landscape. From AI-driven content creation and enhanced personalization to AR/VR integration and social commerce, these trends offer exciting opportunities for those willing to embrace them.

With the help of JarveePro, users can stay ahead of these trends, ensuring their social media efforts are both effective and efficient.

Incorporating JarveePro into your social media strategy not only streamlines the management process but also positions you to capitalize on the latest trends, ultimately shaping public opinion in favor of your brand or cause. As social media continues to evolve, tools like JarveePro will remain indispensable for navigating this ever-changing digital frontier.

The Future of LinkedIn Automation: Smarter Networking in 2025

Share

2025-09-08

LinkedIn has grown far beyond its original role as a professional networking site. In 2025, it has become the go-to platform for B2B marketing, career building, and thought leadership. With over one billion members worldwide, the competition for attention is fierce, and businesses are finding it harder to reach the right people manually. This is where automation is reshaping the way professionals use LinkedIn.

Instead of spending countless hours sending connection requests, managing multiple accounts, or tracking campaigns, LinkedIn automation tools allow marketers to scale their efforts while staying efficient and consistent. But the future of automation isn’t just about speed—it’s about smarter networking, personalization, and safe account management.

Why LinkedIn Automation Matters in 2025

LinkedIn is unique compared to other social platforms. While Instagram and TikTok focus on entertainment and lifestyle content, LinkedIn is where professionals and businesses make real connections that often lead to sales, partnerships, or career opportunities.

However, this also makes it one of the hardest platforms to manage manually. Some of the biggest challenges include:

Time-consuming outreach

: Sending personalized messages and follow-ups at scale takes hours.

Multi-account management

: Agencies and B2B teams often juggle multiple LinkedIn profiles.

Consistency issues

: Without regular activity, profiles lose visibility in the feed.

Risk of account restrictions

: Aggressive activity or logging in from the same IP across multiple accounts often leads to bans.

Automation solves these problems by allowing professionals to focus on building meaningful relationships while the tool handles the repetitive work.

The Evolution of LinkedIn Automation

In the early days, automation on LinkedIn was limited to simple connection requests and bulk messaging. But in 2025, automation tools have evolved into sophisticated platforms that can:

Personalize outreach with AI-driven templates.

Schedule posts across multiple accounts for consistent visibility.

Analyze engagement data to improve campaign performance.

Protect accounts with safer login environments and proxy management.

This evolution reflects a shift in the mindset of marketers. Instead of spamming thousands of users, the goal is now

quality over quantity

—engaging with the right audience using the right strategy.

How JarveePro Enables Smarter LinkedIn Networking

JarveePro is designed to meet the modern demands of LinkedIn marketers. Unlike basic automation tools, it combines scale with safety, helping professionals and agencies grow their networks without risking bans.

Here’s how JarveePro supports smarter LinkedIn automation in 2025:

Proxy Binding for Each Account

Every LinkedIn profile can be connected to a unique proxy, creating a secure environment and reducing the risk of detection.

Category Management

Easily group accounts by project, client, or campaign. Agencies managing multiple clients can organize everything in one place.

Automated Outreach

Send connection requests, follow-ups, and messages automatically, while still keeping them personalized and human-like.

Bulk Scheduling

Plan and schedule content across multiple LinkedIn accounts. This ensures profiles stay active without constant manual effort.

Human-Like Behavior

JarveePro mimics real user activity with randomized timing, making automation safe and natural.

With these features, businesses no longer need to choose between safety and efficiency—they get both.

How To Run LinkedIn Automation Better in 2025

Automation isn’t a magic button—it works best when you use it with a clear strategy. Here are a few things that really make the difference:

Keep it human.

Nobody likes getting spammy copy-paste messages. If you’re using automation, make sure your templates sound natural and add small personal touches, like referencing someone’s role or industry.

Don’t push too hard.

Sending hundreds of connection requests a day is the fastest way to get flagged. A steady, consistent pace feels more natural and keeps your account safe.

Pay attention to results.

Automation gives you data—use it. See what kind of messages get replies, what content drives engagement, and double down on what’s working.

Mix automation with real interaction.

The best connections usually come from genuine conversations. Let automation handle the repetitive stuff, but jump in personally when someone shows interest.

Protect your accounts.

Always separate accounts with proxies and unique setups. LinkedIn is strict, so a little caution goes a long way.

title: The New X-Strategy: How Modern Brands Win on Twitter/X Through Conversation, Agility, and Authentic Voice
summary: The New X-Strategy: How Modern Brands Win on Twitter/X Through Conversation, Agility, and Authentic Voice
text:
The New X-Strategy: How Modern Brands Win on Twitter/X Through Conversation, Agility, and Authentic Voice

Share

2025-11-18

1. The Twitter/X Landscape in 2025: A Platform Defined by Rapid Change

No social media platform has undergone more change in the last two years than Twitter/X. From feature rollouts to algorithm rewrites to interface redesigns, the platform moves at a pace that leaves competitors looking slow and predictable.

Leadership decisions are executed quickly, often without lengthy public testing, creating an environment where nothing stays static for long. This has produced two major effects:

The volatility discourages slow-moving brands

Businesses reliant on rigid content calendars, multi-week review processes, and corporate tone guidelines often struggle here. By the time a tweet is approved internally, the trend it references might already be obsolete.

The volatility empowers agile marketers

Marketers who can adapt fast — whether through automation tools, flexible workflows, or agency-style responsiveness — can capitalize on opportunities that others miss. Changes that seem chaotic to casual users often become strategic advantages for those who monitor platform shifts closely.

In other words, Twitter/X rewards those who play dynamically, not defensively.

2. The Algorithm Shift: Why Conversations Outperform Broadcasts

One of the most notable transformations in 2025 is X’s increasing emphasis on conversational engagement over traditional posting. While tweets that announce products or share static images still have value, they no longer anchor the algorithm the way replies and discussions do.

Replies Are the New Reach Engine

The platform now heavily amplifies:

thoughtful replies

humorous responses

expert commentary under trending threads

conversational engagements with followers

participation in popular discussions

Posts in the form of replies — especially to high-authority accounts — often outperform standalone tweets.

This shift is reshaping brand strategies fundamentally.

Why X Prefers Conversations

There are three major reasons behind this priority:

A. Users stay longer when they join discussions

Conversation threads keep people on the platform, and longer session times increase ad revenue.

B. Replies reveal identity and voice

X aims to reward accounts that behave like individuals — expressive, reactive, and social.

C. Replies generate network effects

One reply may be viewed by thousands of users who follow the original poster, even if they don’t follow the account replying.

This makes replies one of the highest-leverage actions on the platform.

3. The Rise of Human-Like Brands: Why Personality Wins in 2025

In previous years, brands could get away with polished messaging and scheduled posts. But in 2025, authenticity is no longer optional.

Brands that thrive on X today demonstrate characteristics once reserved for creators:

humor

personality

distinct opinions

emotional tone

contextual awareness

conversational presence

The Decline of Corporate Tone

Corporate-sounding posts struggle to generate engagement because they feel impersonal and passive. Users scroll past them as if they belong to another era — because they do.

Modern audiences want brands that speak like humans. They want personality, not perfection.

The Human Voice Advantage

A human-like voice delivers measurable benefits:

higher engagement rates

more retweets and quote posts

stronger audience loyalty

improved perception of relatability

better top-of-funnel brand awareness

increased visibility in conversation-driven algorithms

Today, the brands that win aren’t the ones who speak the loudest but the ones who speak the

most naturally

4. Speed as a Strategic Advantage

On X, speed is a superpower. From trend participation to customer responses, rapid movement is often the difference between visibility and obscurity.

Trend Windows Are Shorter Than Ever

Trends now peak and decline in hours — sometimes minutes. Brands that wait for approval cycles frequently miss opportunities entirely.

Timely Replies Amplify Reach

Replying quickly to audience comments or industry discussions increases visibility dramatically due to how the algorithm prioritizes recency.

Customer Conversations Are Public

Every customer interaction becomes public record, making speed and tone publicly measurable. Fast, helpful replies strengthen reputation. Slow or mechanical replies damage it.

5. Visual Content: Professional Quality, Conversational Tone

Despite the rise of conversational posts, visual elements still matter. High-quality graphics, clean layouts, and short-form video clips can multiply engagement.

But on X, visual content must be paired with conversational messaging — not polished corporate language.

What Works Visually on X in 2025

short “explainers”

chart-based insights

meme-style formats adapted professionally

quote graphics

animated text snippets

vertical video optimized for mobile

simple but bold branding elements

Visual + Conversation = Maximum Impact

Posts that pair compelling visuals with human-like commentary outperform visuals alone. Users are drawn to posts that feel like a person speaking, not a campaign asset delivered from a marketing department.

6. Why Marketers Still Love Twitter/X

Despite volatility, X remains essential for marketing for several reasons:

Industry News Moves Faster Here

Trends start on X before they appear on other platforms. Marketers use X as the pulse of real-time culture.

You Can Reach Decision-Makers Directly

Executives, founders, investors, creators, journalists — they all use X daily.

Organic Reach Potential Is Higher Than on Most Platforms

While many platforms limit visibility heavily, X continues to reward relevant engagement naturally.

Multi-Account Strategies Are Still Viable

Brands can run multiple personas, communities, and campaigns — especially when supported by automation tools like JarveePro.

Messaging Styles Are More Flexible

A brand can be educational, humorous, authoritative, conversational, or controversial — and still succeed if done authentically.

7. Practical Strategies for Winning on X in 2025

This is the actionable section marketers care about. Below are the proven tactics that consistently deliver results on X today.

Strategy 1: Build a Distinctive Brand Voice

Your voice must be:

clear

human

expressive

recognizable

Avoid generic phrasing like:

“Stay tuned for updates.”

“We are excited to announce…”

“These features will enhance your experience…”

Users scroll past these instantly.

Instead, aim for:

clarity

engagement

relatability

opinion

Your voice should feel like a real person who understands the culture of the platform.

Strategy 2: Invest Heavily in Replies

Replies drive exponential reach. Use them to:

comment under trending posts

respond to industry leaders

join community discussions

reply to customer feedback

provide expertise

insert humor when appropriate

A single well-crafted reply can outperform 10 standalone tweets.

Strategy 3: Use High-Frequency Posting (Without Spamming)

The sweet spot for many brands in 2025:

3–6 original posts per day

15–50 replies depending on the niche

2–5 retweets or quote tweets

High-frequency posting increases visibility and provides more opportunities to reach sub-audiences.

Strategy 4: Capitalize on Micro-Trends and Cultural Moments

Micro-trends now matter as much as macro-trends. These include:

niche jokes

community memes

industry-specific conversations

viral screenshots

news cycles

trending keywords

A brand that responds quickly to these gains relevance rapidly.

Strategy 5: AI-Assisted Content (The Smart Way)

AI isn’t for replacing brand voice — it’s for accelerating:

drafting

brainstorming

idea generation

trend summarization

data analysis

post variations

audience segmentation

Tools like JarveePro enable marketers to produce high-volume content without sacrificing quality.

Strategy 6: Build Conversations, Not Announcements

Announcement-style posts have declining performance. Instead:

ask questions

request feedback

encourage debate

share opinions

comment on industry changes

provide quick insights

The more your posts feel like conversations, the better the algorithm treats them.

Strategy 7: Use Multi-Account Personas Strategically

Smart marketers now manage multiple accounts representing:

different product lines

different content angles

different audience segments

different brand voices

different communities

This allows for broader reach and more creative experimentation.

8. Where Twitter/X Is Going Next (2025–2026 Outlook)

While platform unpredictability remains, several directional trends are clear.

More Creator Tools

Expect enhanced features for:

monetization

analytics

video distribution

fan communities

More AI Integration

AI will increasingly shape:

post recommendations

content ranking

audience matching

feed personalization

More Emphasis on Public Debate and Conversation

Discussion-driven posts will continue to outperform broadcast posts.

Greater Adoption by Global Markets

Twitter/X usage is growing internationally, making multi-language strategies more important.

Conclusion: The New Rules for Succeeding on Twitter/X

Twitter/X in 2025 is defined by five realities:

Rapid change is the norm.

Conversations outperform broadcasts.

Human-like brands win.

Speed beats perfection.

Agility is the marketer’s competitive advantage.

Brands that approach X with flexibility, personality, and conversational focus will continue to see exceptional results — far beyond what static content strategies can achieve.

For marketers who embrace its ever-changing nature, X is not a chaotic environment; it is a high-reward platform with limitless potential.

summary: The Proxy Puzzle: Real Lessons from Running 30 to 2000 Accounts with JarveePro
text:
The Proxy Puzzle: Real Lessons from Running 30 to 2000 Accounts with JarveePro

Share

2025-09-24

Why Proxies Decide Your Survival in Multi-Account Marketing

Every day, I hear the same questions from clients: “Do I need to bind proxies one by one?” “Why are my accounts posting the same content?” or even “Can I run JarveePro in RDP?” These may sound like minor technical details, but they decide whether your accounts live or die.

If you’re managing just a few social accounts, you can get away with sloppy setups. But the moment you move from 30 accounts to 200, or even 2000, those small mistakes can snowball into massive problems: banned accounts, wasted time and money, duplicate posts that kill engagement, or bandwidth inefficiencies that quietly eat into margins.

This isn’t a basic “what is a proxy” post. It’s a collection of

real lessons from real client questions

—the kind that land in my inbox daily—and the practical insights I’ve learned running JarveePro at scale. If you’ve ever been confused about proxies, RDP, or how to prevent duplicate content, this is written for you.

The First Big Confusion: Binding Proxies

A client recently asked:

“With a list of 100 accounts, I import 30 into JarveePro. When I press ‘Bind Proxy,’ will the proxies I purchased be randomly assigned to each account correctly? Or do I have to assign proxies one by one?”

This is the heart of the proxy puzzle. Do you let automation assign randomly, or do you manually link proxies to accounts?

Here’s the practical truth:

Random binding

is fast and works well for newcomers. JarveePro will spread your purchased proxies across accounts to avoid obvious duplication. It’s the quickest way to get started.

Ordered binding

is for control and scaling. If you want certain accounts tied to specific regions, clients, or niches — or you’re running many accounts for a single brand —binding them in order gives you predictable behavior.

Which should you use? It depends on where you are in your journey. If you’re running 30 accounts, random binding keeps things simple. If you manage hundreds or thousands, you’ll want deliberate proxy allocation as part of your standard operating procedure.

The Hidden Cost of Mismanaging Proxies

Most new users think proxies are only for “hiding IPs.” That’s a tiny part of the story. Proxies affect:

Account safety

— They separate accounts, making them appear as distinct users.

Task reliability

— Good proxies reduce login failures and timeouts.

Operational cost

— Cheap proxies can cause higher retry rates and wasted task runs.

I’ve seen teams invest in JarveePro Monitor and still lose ground because proxies were misallocated. But I’ve also seen teams buy quality residential proxies, manage them carefully, and scale safely for months.

When someone asks “what’s the best proxy for multiple social media accounts?” the correct response isn’t a brand name — it’s a checklist: residential vs. datacenter, per-proxy account limits, regional alignment, and provider reliability.

Scaling: From 30 Accounts to 2000 — What Changes

People often assume scaling is just “more accounts = more work.” That’s true, but it misses the point: the rules change as you scale.

30 accounts

— a testing ground. Mistakes are fixable.

200 accounts

— a business. Small mistakes cost money and time.

2000 accounts

— an operation. You need systems, monitoring, and discipline.

Here’s what shifts at each stage:

Proxy assignment

shifts from “let it run” to “strategy-driven allocation.”

Content strategy

shifts from “one post” to “variations, spintax, and rotation.”

Infrastructure

shifts from running locally to VPS/RDP and distributed setups.

Monitoring

shifts from manual checks to automated campaign monitoring (JarveePro Monitor).

In short: you don’t just multiply what you do at 30 — you change how you do it.

The Duplicate Post Problem (Real Client Case)

A client (AshTrade Ukraine) sent screenshots and wrote:

“JarveePro posts the same post on all accounts — needs to be fixed with the settings. I’m still setting something up incorrectly. I need help.”

This is one of the most common mistakes. People automate without variation. Platforms see identical posts across many accounts and flag that pattern as spam.

Fix:

use

spintax

and content variation. Don’t treat automation as “copy-paste at scale.” Treat it as “create variations that look genuine.”

Example:

Base message: “Buy our product now!”

Spintax:

{Grab|Get|Order} yours {today|now|before they’re gone}! {Shop|Visit our store|See mor

JarveePro supports this natively. Combine spintax with scheduled posting windows and different media assets per account group, and you’ll see engagement hold steady while risk drops.

The RDP / VPS Question — Why It Matters Beyond Convenience

Another user asked: “Is it possible to run JarveePro inside RDP?”

Yes — and here’s why many pros choose RDP/VPS:

Uptime

: You can keep tasks running 24/7 without relying on your personal PC.

Isolation

: Separate workspaces reduce risk (less chance of cross-contamination between personal and client accounts).

Scaling

: A well-configured VPS handles many browsers reliably; your local machine often can't.

Security

: Properly managed servers, with limited access and backups, reduce single-point failure.

But RDP is not magic. It’s infrastructure. You still need quality proxies and smart scheduling. RDP gives you stability; it doesn’t fix bad proxy setups or duplicate content.

Take a look at JarveePro VPS Version

Real-Time Search + Automated Engagement — How to Make It Work

A client wanted to know why search results only saved links and didn’t feed actions directly into tasks. That friction is what separates hobbyist automation from professional-grade operations.

The ideal flow:

Real-time discovery

finds new posts or trends right when they appear.

Automated tasks

(likes, retweets, comments) are queued and applied to fresh results.

Monitoring

tracks action success and flags drop-offs for human review.

JarveePro’s real-time search can feed actions directly into campaigns, but the setup matters: you must link search outputs to active campaign templates and enable campaign monitoring (JarveePro Monitor) so results are tracked and adjustments are automated.

Tip:

always build a feedback loop. Let results guide the next round of targeting. If a search term produces poor-quality posts, tweak the keyword or adjust filters.

The Enterprise Angle: $2000 for JarveePro Monitor (Campaign Monitoring)

What does JarveePro Monitor really deliver, and why do advanced teams invest in it?

At its core,

JarveePro Monitor

uses the

Advanced Content Explorer

to continuously track, filter, and surface the most relevant content across multiple platforms — Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, YouTube, Reddit, Pinterest, as well as sources like RSS feeds, Reuters, and Stocktwits.

Instead of blindly automating posts, campaigns are now guided by

real-time signals from the market and social media trends

. That means:

Continuous Industry Monitoring:

Track breaking news, trending discussions, or emerging memes in your niche.

Content Generation on the Fly:

Auto-generate posts and comments aligned with the latest developments, so campaigns never feel outdated.

Cross-Platform Intelligence:

Get insights from multiple networks in one dashboard, ensuring your strategy isn’t siloed.

Trend-Connected Engagement:

Ensure that what you post or comment resonates because it’s tied directly to what audiences are currently talking about.

Strategic Advantage:

Being first (or early) to act on news or conversations often means higher reach, more engagement, and stronger positioning.

For small operators, $2000 might feel steep. But for enterprises running

large-scale social campaigns

, this isn’t just another tool — it’s

a trend intelligence engine

that fuels relevance. Missing the pulse of your industry for even a day can mean losing momentum, engagement, or even credibility. With JarveePro Monitor, you’re always informed, always aligned, and always ahead.

What the Proxy Puzzle Teaches You (Practical Rules)

From those client Q&As, here’s what actually works — not theory, but the rules the pros follow:

Start simple, then systematize

Use random binding to get going, but build a plan for manual allocation once you scale.

Avoid one-post-fits-all

Spintax and asset rotation are mandatory for multi-account posting.

Treat infrastructure as a lever

RDP and VPS are not optional when your account count grows past hobby-range.

Monitor like it’s your business

If you’re serious, buy monitoring. JarveePro Monitor gives you the visibility

to act on news or conversations

hat fuels relevance.

Distribute risk

Don’t put many accounts behind one proxy. Per-proxy account limits are a real safeguard.

Measure voice, not volume

Engagement patterns matter more than raw output. A single well-targeted campaign that gets responses is better than hundreds of shallow interactions.

A Short Checklist for Scaling Safely

If you’re moving from 30 to 200+ accounts, run through this checklist:

Choose proxies with a proven reputation for social platforms.

Decide on binding strategy (random for load-in, manual for production).

Set up spintax and rotate media assets.

Move to RDP or VPS for stability.

Enable campaign monitoring (consider JarveePro Monitor).

Run incremental increases in activity — don’t blast everything on day one.

Monitor for IP blocks or repeat failures and quiesce accounts when needed.

Real Use Cases: Mini Case Studies from the Q&A

Case 1 — The 30-account agency

An agency imported 30 accounts to test a new product campaign. Random binding worked, they used spintax, and they made incremental increases.

Result: low friction, steady engagement, no bans.

Case 2 — The 300-account operator

A mid-sized operator ran into repeated login errors because proxies were overloaded. They moved to manual binding, increased proxy pool, and added campaign monitoring.

Result: fewer retries, lower costs per action, and stable deliverability.

Case 3 — The 2000-account operator

A larger team invested in JarveePro Monitor and built SOPs around proxy assignment and content rotation. The monitoring package paid for itself by catching a cross-region proxy issue that would have otherwise impacted hundreds of accounts.

Why JarveePro’s Features Matter (Not as Hype, but as Tools)

When I describe JarveePro’s proxy manager, campaign monitor, or VPS integrations, this isn’t about marketing blurbs. These are hard features solving hard problems:

Proxy Management

: lets you bind in bulk, bind in order, or set per-account preferences. This reduces accidental overlap.

Spintax & Content Rotation

: prevents duplication and keeps posts genuine.

VPS and RDP support

: gives persistent, controlled runtime environments for large-scale runs.

Campaign Monitoring (JarveePro Monitor)

: turns raw automation into a manageable, visible operation.

Every time we release an update — dashboard tweaks, export fixes, login improvements for YouTube/TikTok — it’s because a user hit a real pain point. Those updates aren’t features for feature’s sake; they’re shortcuts that keep your operation running.

Conclusion— The Puzzle Is Solvable

The proxy puzzle looks scary when you’re starting, but it’s solvable with a few practical moves:

Start with safe defaults (random binding, small proxy pools).

Build SOPs for content variation (spintax + rotation).

Move to RDP/VPS when you need stability.

Invest in campaign monitoring before small issues become catastrophes.

Proxies, binding, RDP, and content variation are not optional technicalities — they are the infrastructure of reliable growth. Whether you’re at 30 accounts or 2000, the goal is the same:

keep the accounts healthy, keep content varied, and keep learning

JarveePro exists to make that easier — from bulk binding to campaign monitoring — so you spend your time on strategy, not firefighting.

Things you need to know about the Facebook Spam Policy

Share

2022-01-29

As the world’s most popular social media platform,Facebook has a billion active users per month.By issuing an advertisement in such a platform,you can easily find the right audience,attracting the audiences’ attention and get results.But if you want to grow your business on Facebook,you need to know about the Facebook Spam policy well.If you are interested in this topic,keep reading,you’ll find it worthy.

What is spam?

Spam involves contacting people with unwanted content or requests. This includes sending bulk messages, excessively posting links or images to people's timelines and sending friend requests to people you don't know personally,etc.

You might say for businessmen and marketers,this seems to be a common thing.Because they often do this in order to grow their business.However,doing this can easily be regarded as spam,which can make your content not be seen by more users,and your account also has the risk to be blocked.When we know the Facebook policy well,we can avoid these problems and grow our account and business with ease.

Let’s take a look at the Policy Rationale of Facebook

As Facebook put it,they has always worked hard to limit the spread of spam because they do not want to allow content that is designed to deceive, or that attempts to mislead users, to increase viewership.

This kind of content creates a negative user experience, detracts from people's ability to engage authentically in online communities and can threaten the security, stability and usability of Facebook services.

They also aim to prevent people from abusing their platform, products or features to artificially increase viewership or distribute content for commercial gain.

What kind of content will be defined as spam?

1.Post, share, engage with content or create accounts, Groups, Pages, Events or other assets, either manually or automatically, at very high frequencies.

2.Attempt to or successfully sell, buy or exchange site privileges or product features, such as accounts, admin roles, permission to post, Pages, Groups, likes, etc., except in the case of clearly identified branded content, as defined by our Branded Content Policies.

3.Require or claim that users are required to engage with content (e.g. liking, sharing) before they are able to view or interact with promised content.

What actions has Facebook taken when confronting spam?

It takes a three-part approach to content enforcement: remove, reduce and inform.

1.Remove

The Facebook Community Standards outline what is and isn't allowed on Facebook. They remove content that goes against their policies as soon as they become aware of it.

2.Reduce

Some problematic content can create a negative experience for people on Facebook. So they'll often reduce the distribution of this content, even when it doesn’t quite meet the standard for removal under their policies.

3.Inform

When content is potentially sensitive or misleading, they sometimes add a warning or share additional information from independent fact-checkers.

Avoid spam with

JarveePro

After reading,we can find out that the frequency of our operation is vital.To avoid too high frequency operations, I recommend you to use JarveePro scheduling feature.You can set a specific running time for your task and your account,which is helpful to avoid spam.Besides, you can create multiple accounts instead of using one account too actively. And multi-accounts management can also be successfully done by JarveePro.

All in all,you need to pay close attention to the following matters:

1.Use the specific proxy and user agent to run your account each time.

2.Do not run many tasks at the same time with one account. For example, use account A to do the follow task and unfollow task at the same time.

3.If you want to run many tasks with one account, please set a specific running time for each task.(which can be done perfectly by the scheduling feature of JarveePro.)

4.Do not follow so many people per time, just make your task like the real people are doing it. (It is also about the frequency of your task.What’s more,try to make your operations like a general user.)

In conclusion,Facebook has always worked hard to limit the spread of spam.They have the same policies around the world, for everyone on Facebook.When you have a better knowledge about their policies ,you may benefit a lot,no matter for your account and your business.

,you can grow your account and your business on Facebook more easily,while obey to their laws at the same time.Get started with

text:
This is how YouTube algorithm works

Share

2021-10-14

Since its launch in 2005, YouTube’s growth has been really impressive. In 2006, YouTube was purchased by Google, skyrocketing the platform into its role as one of the biggest websites on the internet. As of the second quarter of 2021, the YouTube mobile app was counting 774.6 million monthly active users (MAU) worldwide on iPhone and iPad combined. By comparison, monthly active YouTube users on the Android app were roughly 17.6 million worldwide. It’s now the second-largest search engine in the world—and a valuable tool for brands and creators alike.

It’s well known that many social media platforms use algorithms to determine what content people see. YouTube uses its algorithms to serve up a never-ending list of relevant content, and always seems to know exactly what users want to watch next.YouTube uses its algorithms to serve up a never-ending list of relevant content, and always seems to know exactly what users want to watch next.

According to YouTube, 70 percent of the videos that viewers watch are recommended to them by the algorithm. Since marketers are at the mercy of algorithms on nearly every publishing channel, knowing how each of these unique algorithms work is crucial to attracting and maintaining an audience.

What is the algorithm？

The point of the algorithm is that it aims to reflect what viewers like.

YouTube’s algorithm serves the most relevant, personalized videos to their users on five different parts of their platform: Search, Home, Suggested Videos, Trending, Subscriptions, and Notifications.

The algorithm has two primary goals: to suggest videos that suit viewers and to keep viewers watching more videos.

A brief history of the YouTube algorithm

2005 to 2012: Optimizing views

The YouTube algorithm recommended the videos that attracted the most views or clicks since day one. In this way, The YouTube algorithm only placed the most popular videos in front of the audience eyeballs. It became very sloppy with repetitive content.

2012: Optimizing for watch time

Since view count was not clear enough, YouTube jiggled up its algorithms a bit. Now, YouTube SEO depended on the watch time (view duration) of videos and the total time spent on the overall platform (session time). in this way, creators should create high-quality content to attract the audience. Many new creators were able to reach out to larger masses.

2016：AI deep learning

Thanks to Google’s acquisition of Youtube in 2006, YouTube was able to become the second largest search engine. Youtube now takes this same approach through machine learning by relying on a multitude of factors to rank content.

2017-2020: Optimizing for Video Quality

As Instagram continues to be a platform that billions of people use on a daily basis the necessity for quality content is paramount.

The YouTube algorithm began to measure satisfaction with metrics like Shares, Likes and Dislikes (and, of course, the especially brutal “not interested” button.)

How does the YouTube algorithm work in 2021？

Ranking on the YouTube home page is based on:

Performance: Using click-through rate and average view duration, YouTube measures how well a video engaged other viewers when they saw it on their home page.

Personalization: YouTube personalizes a user’s video recommendations based on their watch history and how often they engage with a specific channel or topic.

There are some metrics that YouTube algorithm will take.

Search

YouTube takes into account how well your title, description and content match each user's query. They also consider how many videos users have watched from your channel and how long ago they last watched another video on the same topic as yours.

When users visit the homepage, they first see the videos they've subscribed to, and then recommended videos based on their previous viewing history and the video's performance. While you may want to try and grab a coveted spot on the page, YouTube encourages creators to simply create quality content that people want to watch and click on.

Description

In YouTube Analytics, take the Traffic Sources section to find out which words viewers use in the search bar to find your channel and videos. It is best to consider popular keywords for your title, or at least your description, as they have been tried and tested and have been proven to drive traffic to your channel. However, please do this in moderation. You don't want to use random words that have nothing to do with the topic.

Beyond that, please consider the length of your description. Ideally, you should have 1-2 paragraphs of relevant content. If you can't come up with that many, we recommend relevance in length. If you just include social media or a few sentences in your description, then you're really missing out on content that will help the algorithm a lot - don't skip this step!

By the way - your first sentence is the most important. It's what the viewer sees before they click on your video in search. Experiment with the social media campaigns with JarveePro. Try JarveePro free today.

text:
Tips and Tricks for Facebook Marketplace

Share

2021-10-21

Facebook Marketplace is Facebook’s built in buy and sell channel. It allows Facebook users to sell items directly to each other. According to Facebook data, more than one in three US Facebook users buy and sell on Marketplace each month. Facebook Marketplace used to be a peer-to-peer shopping marketplace, but has expanded to include merchant selling.

Do some research

Before you start selling, look around the Facebook Marketplace and see what people are selling in your area. Do you want to sell locally, regionally or nationally? Differentiate yourself by selling items that are not similar to other items. Medium to large sized items are popular on the Facebook Marketplace. General household items such as furniture, electronics and microwaves are common.

Take good pictures

Pictures have a long way to go. Don't use stock images as this is often seen as fraudulent. Present your items in the way you want to see them in the shop. Take multiple, clear photos in good lighting with plain backgrounds. Avoid filters and be sure to capture the item at multiple angles.

Include an accurate and detailed description in addition to time and availability. In addition to any warranty information, make sure your photos also show any potential defects. In this way, customers know they are dealing with a serious seller who has taken the time to display the item for sale. Use a plain white or black background when taking photos. This eliminates distractions.

Be consistent

Sellers who try to sell everything they can on marketplaces are rarely successful. Consistency will give you control over pricing, listing, and delivery expertise. It will also build you a following across your social media channels because you will be known as the subject matter expert on your items.

List Brand names

Include brand names in all of my listings. If it’s an item that is still available in stores, you could link the manufacturer’s listing and description. It is believed that this helps people to get a feel for what they may have to pay if they have to buy a new car.

Sell on Facebook like retail stores

This is retail arbitrage, a business model that works well on Amazon. In fact, 19% of Amazon sellers engage in retail arbitrage, with over half of them making $1,000 or more in sales per month.

It also works well on eBay, so there's no reason why you can't succeed on Facebook. If there are local people in your area looking for the same products, then you will have customers.

Spread the word

Facebook owns Instagram and you can easily cross-post your listings. This means more eyes will see your items. You can also automatically cross-post your listing in other Facebook groups you belong to. This also means that you will get more seen and potential buyers.

Explain why you are selling

You could clearly explain why I'm selling an item (to clean up a room, to change the style) so that people understand that there is nothing wrong with the listing (especially if the item is in good condition). Explain how you use it. Show items that have been used in your home to inspire people！

Andrew Pires, the owner of eCommerce from New York, The Maskie, says:

Facebook Marketplace allows for businesses to nurture a relationship with your customers, which is extremely important for brand name and consumer retention. Your goal should be to have your customers see you as a person rather than a business and feel comfortable reaching out to you about your products. As time goes on, you will see that this connection makes your customer pool grow, and more loyal customers will arise as well.

It’s time to join the business bandwagon!

You can also marketing your own brand！

These features can help users build and maintain a fan base on social media platforms, increasing their exposure and influence.

In addition, when Jarvee closed its service permanently, JarveePro was the best alternative. JarveePro not only has similar automation features but also has more comprehensive and flexible automation options. Users can set their own automation rules according to their needs and preferences, making it more in line with their marketing and promotion strategies.

JarveePro also provides some useful statistical and analytical features that can help users understand the performance of their social media accounts and user behavior, to better formulate marketing and promotion strategies. Users can use this statistical and analytical data to understand the growth trends of their social media accounts, audience demographics, and user feedback.

In summary, JarveePro is a powerful social media automation tool that can help users efficiently and intelligently manage and operate their accounts on social media platforms. It is the best alternative after Jarvee closed and can free up users’ hands, allowing them to focus more on content creation and marketing. If you are looking for an efficient and reliable social media automation tool, then JarveePro is a worthy consideration.

Top #2 Jarvee Alternative : FollowingLike

FollowingLike is like a wholesale social media growth company. This is because they offer similar features to other brands out there – but they do so for multiple Instagram/Facebook accounts.

Advertisement

These guys are so serious about their Instagram features that they’ve divided their price points into how many accounts they can help you grow. This is why they’re ideal if your brand has multiple Instagram accounts, or if you work for an agency and a big part of your job is keeping up with social media.

Following Like has three different packages. Their first package can help you with one account, while their second package can help you with five. Their last and biggest package can help you with unlimited accounts, which is quite a jump from the middle option.

FollowingLike takes their Instagram engagement very seriously, so you can rest assured that you’re in good hands with them.

MeetEdgar focuses on automating social media scheduling by allowing you to create a library of evergreen content that can be shared repeatedly. It offers category-based scheduling and content recycling, along with basic analytics and reporting.

Top #4 Jarvee Alternative: Later

Later is a popular social media scheduling tool and can be considered a potential alternative to Jarvee. It primarily focuses on visual content scheduling for platforms like Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and Pinterest. Later allows you to plan and schedule your social media posts in advance, organize your content with a visual content calendar, and preview how your posts will appear on your social media profiles. It also offers features like hashtag suggestions, analytics, and user-generated content management. While Later may not have the same extensive automation capabilities as Jarvee, it excels in visual content management and scheduling for social media.

summary: Twitter Algorithm in 2021：ALL You Should Know
text:
Twitter Algorithm in 2021：ALL You Should Know

Share

2021-11-02

Twitter is a real-time microblogging platform, publicly launched in July 2006. At launch, its defining features were the tight limits placed on each post, known at a tweet.

First, let's clarify one thing. Twitter is powered by a variety of algorithms that determine all aspects of how content is served on the platform. This includes everything from suggested accounts to popular tweets. As with most social media algorithms, Twitter's algorithms are all about personalisation. The Twitter feed algorithm does not affect the main timeline for those using the Latest Tweets view, which is a simple list of tweets from followed topics and accounts. It does, however, build a timeline for those using the home page view.

Here is a quick break down of twitter algorithm：

When Twitter was launched in 2006, the algorithm was built in reverse chronological order; that is, users had to scroll through tweets from the most recent to the older ones. The tweets they saw were only from followed accounts.

But in 2014, they began to see tweets from followers as well as recommended tweets and topics. In 2015, Twitter helped users keep an eye on tweets they might have missed when they exited the platform with the 'While you're away' feature.

In 2016-2017, Twitter started ranking what they thought were the best tweets to the top of users' feeds. They also brought in the 'In case you missed it' feature in 2017 to replace 'When you leave'.

In 2018, Twitter allowed users to choose between an algorithmically organised feed and a regular feed. This means they can now choose whether to not view popular tweets or the latest ones.

Features in 2021

Top Tweets: As they will always be following users, Twitter will always include top tweets to ensure users get the most out of the platform.

They rank the best tweets from people you follow and content from people you don't follow. They also suggest people to follow based on who you already follow.

Latest Tweets: They show users the most recent tweets in reverse chronological order.

ICYMI: This shows the top tweets on the user's feed. However, the longer the user spends on the app, the less popular tweets they will see.

Happening: This can appear at the top of the feed, showing the latest events or topics of interest to the user.

Twitter Algorithm Ranking Signals

1. Recency：How recently was the tweet published?

2. Relevancy：How relevant are the keywords used in the tweet?

How many people are engaging with the same keywords used by other creators?

Accounts you often engage with

Topics you follow and engage with most

3. Engagement： How many likes, comments, and retweets the tweet has received?

How many users are engaging with other tweets of the same user?

How many users regularly connect with the tweet author?

4. Graphics： The type of graphics used in a tweet (GIF, images, videos, polls, or plain text tweet)

The type of graphic with which most of the users interact.

5. Other Factors： The number of followers of the account.

The location of the account relative to the other users.

Customisable timelines

Twitter users also have the option to create custom timelines using Twitter lists.

You can fix up to five lists for easy access. In them, you can switch between the latest tweets and popular tweets, just like in the main timeline.

Twitter for Business： What You Should Know

Share

2021-10-13

Twitter is a social media and online news platform where people communicate in short messages – up to 280 characters long – called tweets. It is a channel that can help you reach your target audience.

Founded in 2006, Twitter is now one of the most popular social media platforms in the world. With millions of daily users, Twitter can be a powerful tool to raise awareness about your business, engage with customers and develop leads.

Tweeter profile

It's easy to customize your profile by selecting the unique profile and header images, adding a name, bio, location, birth date, and website. You can also choose a theme colour, and pin a Tweet that other people will see when they visit your profile.

Your header photo should be an ever-changing billboard showcasing what’s new. This can be an upcoming launch or campaign, or a new photoshoot that nails your current vibe.

Profile page

▪ Business location: Listed directly in the profile and displayed visually on a small map. People can tap on the location map/listing to open Google Maps and get directions. This helps you reach and connect with local followers.

Hours of operation (optional): Showcase the days and times people can reach your business at a physical location.

Methods of contact: Enable options for customers to contact your business through any or all of the following methods:

▪ Phone call

▪ Text message

▪ Twitter Direct Message

▪ Email

Add a direct link to your website. Include a link to what you want people to see now.

Twitter terms

DM

A "DM," or "direct message," is a private message between two Twitter users. It’s different from a public @mention because, in order to send a DM, the recipient must follow you.

@ Sign

The @ sign is an important code on Twitter, used to refer to individuals on Twitter. It is combined with a username and inserted into tweets to refer to that person or send them a public message. (Example: @username.) When @ precedes a username, it automatically gets linked to that user's profile page.

Handle, Username

A Twitter handle is a username selected by anyone using Twitter and must contain fewer than 15 characters — this can be changed at any time. Each Twitter handle has a unique URL, with the handle added after twitter.com. Example: http://twitter.com/username.

FF or #FF

#FollowFriday started as a way to recommend other Twitter users to your followers. It happens on Fridays, and you can search Twitter for the hashtag on Fridays to watch the kudos pour in.

Tweet content

Planning your content takes a little bit of time upfront, but ultimately saves you effort and stress later on. But you’ll be glad when you post the origin tweet finally. It is useful for aligning the content you’re posting on all your channels. They’re on Twitter to find content that is VALUABLE to them.

Think about the following options:

· Videos

· Pictures

· Articles

· Infographics

Your pinned Tweet

This is what you want your followers to focus on — your biggest, latest news.

In addition, FREQUENCY should be an important part of your Twitter strategy.

summary: Twitter is a frequently cited marketing tool, but it's usually quite different from articles discussing your SERPs ranking. Twitter can increase your audience, provide you with customer service channels, and improve audience engagement. It’s not generally considered something that will raise your Google ranking.
text:
Twitter SEO Tips

Share

2021-03-11

Twitter is a frequently cited marketing tool, but it's usually quite different from articles discussing your SERPs ranking. Twitter can increase your audience, provide you with customer service channels, and improve audience engagement. It’s not generally considered something that will raise your Google ranking.

The primary reason for this, I assume, is because Google doesn’t have wholesale access to Twitter for indexation purposes. They have to crawl it just like they crawl everything else. They tried integration once, with the so-called firehose, but that fell through. Since then, Google has been leery about using third-party data streams for their apps, and instead, just use their own scraping and crawling engine.

That said, you can still get quite a bit of SEO value out of Twitter if you know what to do. Or, coincidentally, if someone presents to you an article of tips for what to do.

The Art of Using Keywords

Try to maintain consistent communication and include similar keywords you use on your website. Remember that hashtags play the role of keywords for Twitter; they improve your searchability and help people find your content. Therefore, turn your essential keywords into hashtags because thanks to them, each one of your tweets will appear in the Twitter search for a specific topic and in Twitter’s Trends Feed. However, avoid overusing hashtags for a single update as this might look spammy and discourage your potential followers. It’s optimal to use up to 3 hashtags for a single tweet. Feel free to add them at the end of a link to an article explaining its field or category.

Once in a while, analyze which hashtags bring you the most engagement: clicks, retweets, likes. Then, optimize your profile by focusing on the more effective ones. Review your results using Twitter analytics and find out what works best for your business.

Bio

Your Twitter bio is your one chance to romance Twitter’s search engine and the visits to your profile in 160 characters or less. Use super relevant keywords and hashtags.

When considering which hashtags to use be aware that the hashtags you use in your bio will be clickable and could also be a distraction from your bio. If someone does click through the hashtag be mindful you are not driving them to your competitors if you are using an industry hashtag. Stick with branded hashtags or ones where the pros outweigh the cons.

Images

For business brands, use a version of your logo that is easily recognizable and representative of your brand. Think about color, image size, and how it will look from a mobile device.

Compare your header image to a magazine cover. Change it monthly to match your monthly editorial calendar.

Feature promotions or a visual that tells a story about what’s happening that month with your brand. For example, your team, a trade show, book launch, new product release, a featured story, or even tiring in a holiday or special event.

Be sure to optimize all images by saving the image file name with branded keywords to increase the chances of being found in an image search.

Open up Your Twitter DM

If you want to make your brand more approachable on Twitter and optimize your accessibility, take the privacy off your direct messages. How do you do this?

Go to the Twitter settings page and click on the Privacy and Security tab. Scroll down the page, go to the direct message option, and checkmark the “Receive Direct Messages from anyone.”

Link to Your Website

Including a link to your official website is a strong call to action. Consider which page would be most appropriate and where you want to send your followers. There are plenty of options, however, by SEO standards, most authority usually belongs to the main page of your company’s website, so this is going to be the most reasonable choice. In the case of any temporary campaign or event, you can always link to a special landing page.

Make sure that your websites like Facebook, Instagram, YouTube... link back to the Twitter account. Mutual linking not only brings more valuable traffic but also gives your profile more credibility in the eyes of Google.

Customer Service Twitter Tools

Since 80 percent of customer service requests happen on Twitter, there’s a compelling reason why brands are leaning into optimizing customer service with Twitter.

In the past year, brands can choose from customer service tools including direct message deep links, customer survey messaging, profile notifications signifying a brand’s response time, and also whether the profile is the correct username to provide support.
