text:
How JarveePro Advanced Content Explorer Works for Modern Social Media Data Collection

2026-05-12

Introduction

Social media marketing has changed dramatically in recent years.

In the past, marketers focused mostly on follower counts and basic scraping tools. But in 2026, successful social media growth relies far more on understanding audience behavior, engagement patterns, content performance, and niche activity.

This is why modern marketers increasingly use data intelligence systems instead of simple scraping software.

JarveePro Advanced Content Explorer

was built specifically for this new generation of social media research.

Instead of only collecting raw profile data, the system helps users discover:

trending content

active audiences

engagement-heavy posts

creator ecosystems

viral discussions

behavioral signals

niche-specific opportunities

This article explains how Advanced Content Explorer works, what type of data it can collect, how filtering operates, and why behavioral targeting is becoming more important than traditional demographic scraping.

What Is JarveePro Advanced Content Explorer?

Advanced Content Explorer is the dedicated social media data collection and audience intelligence system inside

JarveePro.

The platform is designed to help users collect and analyze publicly accessible social media information across supported platforms.

Depending on the platform and workflow, users can gather:

public post data

engagement metrics

creator activity

audience interaction data

hashtag-related content

niche discussions

follower-related datasets

content performance signals

Unlike traditional scrapers that simply export raw data, Advanced Content Explorer focuses heavily on filtering and engagement analysis.

The goal is not only to collect data — but to identify useful patterns inside social media ecosystems.

How Advanced Content Explorer Collects Social Media Data

The system works by analyzing publicly accessible platform activity and engagement structures.

Depending on the selected workflow, Advanced Content Explorer can monitor and collect information related to:

Content Activity

This includes:

posts

captions

hashtags

public comments

repost activity

engagement volume

interaction frequency

This helps users identify what type of content performs best within specific niches.

Creator and Influencer Activity

Users can also analyze creator ecosystems by collecting:

creator engagement metrics

posting activity

niche relevance

audience interaction patterns

content performance behavior

This is useful for influencer research, partnership discovery, and competitor analysis.

Audience Interaction Signals

Advanced Content Explorer can also collect publicly accessible audience-related datasets from:

post engagement

creator communities

niche discussions

interaction audiences

This allows marketers to identify highly active communities around specific topics, creators, or industries.

How Filtering Works Inside Advanced Content Explorer

One of the platform’s most valuable capabilities is engagement-based filtering.

Instead of collecting massive amounts of low-quality data, users can narrow datasets using engagement and behavioral conditions.

Filtering examples may include:

likes

comments

repost counts

share activity

language

content length

activity level

engagement volume

This helps users isolate:

highly engaged posts

viral content

active creators

trending discussions

niche-specific audiences

For example, instead of scraping every post under a hashtag, users can focus only on posts generating meaningful interaction.

This dramatically improves research quality and targeting precision.

Why Modern Social Media Scraping Focuses on Behavior Instead of Demographics

A common misconception is that modern scraping systems primarily collect demographic information like:

age

gender

identity classification

In reality, social platforms increasingly restrict access to reliable demographic data due to:

privacy protections

platform security systems

anti-scraping technologies

API limitations

behavioral detection systems

Because of this, modern automation platforms increasingly prioritize behavioral intelligence instead.

Behavioral signals often provide stronger marketing value anyway.

For example:

A user consistently interacting with fitness creators, cryptocurrency content, gaming communities, or luxury travel posts often provides more actionable targeting information than estimated age or gender alone.

This is one of the biggest shifts happening across the automation industry in 2026.

What Makes Behavioral Targeting More Effective

Behavioral targeting focuses on what users actually do rather than assumed identity traits.

This includes analyzing:

what content users engage with

how frequently they interact

which creators they follow

which discussions they participate in

which content formats generate stronger reactions

This type of analysis helps marketers identify:

purchase intent

niche interests

audience quality

engagement likelihood

trend participation

As social media platforms continue evolving, engagement-based intelligence is becoming one of the most important forms of audience research.

Common Use Cases for Advanced Content Explorer

Advanced Content Explorer is widely used for:

Influencer Discovery

Finding creators with active and engaged audiences.

Competitor Research

Analyzing how competing brands structure content and generate engagement.

Viral Trend Monitoring

Tracking which topics and content formats spread rapidly within specific niches.

Audience Intelligence

Studying engagement behavior around creators, industries, and hashtags.

Content Research

Identifying high-performing content structures before creating campaigns.

Lead Generation Research

Building targeted audience datasets around public engagement activity.

Can Advanced Content Explorer Support Custom Workflows?

Yes.

Custom workflow development may be possible depending on platform limitations and technical requirements.

Some businesses request advanced systems for:

niche-specific filtering

audience classification

custom collection pipelines

AI-assisted analysis

advanced behavioral segmentation

However, modern social platforms evolve rapidly, which means advanced systems often require continuous adaptation and maintenance.

Conclusion

Modern social media intelligence is no longer about collecting the largest amount of raw data possible.

The real value now comes from understanding:

engagement behavior

audience activity

creator ecosystems

niche trends

content performance patterns

JarveePro Advanced Content Explorer

was designed specifically for this modern approach to social media research.

By combining large-scale collection systems with engagement-based filtering and behavioral analysis, the platform helps marketers and agencies identify higher-quality opportunities across today’s increasingly competitive social media landscape.

summary: How the Instagram Repost Tool Works in JarveePro (Large-Scale Campaign Guide)
text:
How the Instagram Repost Tool Works in JarveePro (Large-Scale Campaign Guide)

2026-03-07

Introduction

The

Instagram Repost Tool in JarveePro

is designed to help marketers automatically find, collect, and repost content from targeted sources.

For users running

large numbers of accounts or campaigns

, understanding how the repost workflow operates behind the scenes can help avoid confusion and ensure campaigns run smoothly.

This guide explains how the repost system works, why scraping is required, and how JarveePro manages repost campaigns across multiple accounts at scale.

How the Instagram Repost Tool Works

The repost process in JarveePro is a

multi-step automation workflow

rather than a single action. When a repost campaign runs, the system performs the following steps:

Scrapes posts from the selected source

The account gathers eligible posts from post url sources configured in the campaign.

Downloads the media locally

The scraped media is temporarily stored on the server so it can be scheduled for posting.

Automatically creates a Post campaign

Each collected post is queued into a

Post campaign

, which will publish the repost according to your posting schedule.

Publishes the content gradually

JarveePro publishes the reposts based on the configured timing and safety limits.

This workflow ensures reposted content is handled safely and organized properly across multiple accounts.

Why Scraping Is Required

Before an account can repost content, it must first

scrape the post data from Instagram

This process relies on:

valid session cookies

active account login

the ability to access and scrape content from the source

If an account cannot scrape posts (for example due to expired cookies or login issues), the repost campaign will not start.

For this reason, it is always recommended to

check account status before launching large repost campaigns

Running Repost Campaigns at Scale

JarveePro is designed to support

large-scale automation environments

, including servers running hundreds or even thousands of accounts.

However, actions are

not executed simultaneously across all campaigns

Instead, the system distributes tasks over time in order to:

reduce platform risk

maintain safer automation behavior

balance server resources

avoid excessive simultaneous scraping

For example:

Starting

100 repost campaigns

does not mean they will all scrape at the same second.

JarveePro will

queue and spread actions across time automatically

This allows campaigns to run continuously without overwhelming the server or the social platform.

How Many Posts Will Be Reposted?

When you configure a repost campaign to collect a specific number of posts (for example

20 posts

), the tool will:

scrape up to the configured number of posts

create post entries in the queue

publish them through the automatically generated Post campaign

The repost tool does

not repost everything instantly

Instead, it builds a

posting queue that is executed according to the campaign schedule

Storage Usage When Running Repost Campaigns

During the scraping process, JarveePro temporarily saves downloaded media files on the server.

This allows the system to:

publish the repost later

prevent duplicate reposting

track already-used content in the database

If you are running

very large repost campaigns

, the amount of stored media may grow over time. Periodic monitoring or cleanup may be recommended depending on your campaign size.

Best Practices for Large Campaigns

To ensure repost campaigns run smoothly at scale, consider the following recommendations:

Always

verify account login status

before starting campaigns

Start with

small tests

before launching hundreds of campaigns

Monitor server resources when running large automation setups

Use realistic timing settings to mimic natural posting behavior

These practices help maintain stable automation performance and reduce potential issues.

Full Setup Guide

For step-by-step configuration instructions, see the detailed tutorial:

https://blog.jarveepro.com/knowledge/JarveePro-4-Instagram-Campaigns/Instagram-Repost-Settings-Troubleshooting/5651

Conclusion

The Instagram Repost Tool in JarveePro is a powerful automation feature designed for marketers managing large numbers of accounts. By understanding how the repost workflow operates—scraping content, generating post campaigns, and scheduling posts—you can run repost campaigns more efficiently and at scale.

With proper configuration and active accounts, JarveePro can reliably manage repost automation across hundreds or even thousands of campaigns.

How to Assign and Configure Proxies in JarveePro Account Manager (Complete Guide)

2026-02-25

Overview

The Account Manager and Proxy Manager in JarveePro allow you to assign individual proxies to each social media account. Proper proxy configuration is essential for account safety, platform compliance, and scalable automation.

JarveePro provides two methods to assign proxies:

Assign proxy directly inside Account Manager

Assign and manage proxies centrally using Proxy Manager

Both methods ensure accounts operate through dedicated IP addresses.

Why Proxies Are Required

Using proxies provides several important benefits:

Prevents multiple accounts from sharing the same IP address

Reduces the risk of account restrictions or detection

Enables safe scaling across multiple accounts

Allows geo-targeting using location-specific proxies

Improves account stability and trust score

Best practice: Assign one proxy per account.

Supported Proxy Types

JarveePro supports:

HTTP

HTTPS

SOCKS4

SOCKS5 (Recommended)

SOCKS5 is strongly recommended for residential and mobile proxies due to better compatibility and stability.

Method 1: Assign Proxy via Account Manager

This method is ideal when adding or configuring individual accounts.

Step 1: Open Account Manager

Go to JarveePro Dashboard

Click

Account Manager

Select the platform (Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok, etc.)

Step 2: Edit Account

Select the account

Click the

Edit (pencil icon)

Locate the

Proxy Settings

section

Step 3: Enter Proxy Details

Enter the following:

Proxy Type: HTTP

Host: Proxy IP address

Port: Proxy port

Username: Proxy username

Password: Proxy password

Example:

Host: 193.228.193.86

Port: 12321

Username: your_username

Password: your_password

Step 4: Save and Verify

Click OK

JarveePro will verify the proxy automatically

Ensure proxy shows in the Proxy Column

The account will now operate through the assigned proxy.

Method 2: Assign and Manage Proxies via Proxy Manager (Recommended)

This method provides centralized proxy management and is recommended for managing multiple accounts.

Step 1: Open Proxy Manager

Go to JarveePro Dashboard

Click

Proxy Manager

Select or create a category

You will see a list of all imported proxies.

Step 2: Check Proxy Usage

Proxy Manager shows:

Proxy availability status

Number of accounts bound to each proxy

Platform assignment

Proxy connection status

This helps prevent assigning the same proxy to multiple accounts unintentionally.

Step 3: Bind Proxy to Account

To assign a proxy:

Locate the proxy

Select or assign the account(s) to bind

Click

Save

The proxy will now be assigned to the selected account.

Step 4: Verify Proxy Binding

Confirm the following:

Proxy status shows

Available

Proxy shows correct number of bound accounts

Account is successfully connected using the proxy

Bulk Proxy Import Format

JarveePro supports bulk proxy import using this format:

IP:PORT:USERNAME:PASSWORD

Example:

193.228.193.86:12321:user:password

Best Practices

Follow these recommendations for optimal performance:

Use one proxy per account

Avoid sharing proxies between accounts on the same platform.

Use SOCKS5 residential or mobile proxies

These provide higher trust and better performance.

Match proxy location to account location

Improves account stability and reduces verification triggers.

Use Proxy Manager for bulk management

Provides full visibility and centralized control.

Always verify proxy connectivity before use

Ensures proper configuration.

Common Issues and Solutions

Issue: Proxy shows unavailable

Solution:

Verify proxy credentials

Ensure proxy is active with provider

Select correct proxy type (SOCKS5 recommended)

Issue: Multiple accounts using same proxy

Open Proxy Manager

Check proxy binding count

Assign dedicated proxies per account

Issue: Account connection problems

Reassign proxy

Verify proxy availability

Restart JarveePro if needed

Summary

JarveePro allows proxy assignment through both Account Manager and Proxy Manager. Account Manager is ideal for individual account setup, while Proxy Manager provides centralized proxy control, usage visibility, and bulk assignment capabilities.

Using SOCKS5 residential or mobile proxies, assigning one proxy per account, and verifying proxy connectivity ensures safe, stable, and scalable automation.

Proper proxy management is essential for maintaining long-term account health and automation reliability.

How to Avoid Duplicate Content for Facebook Group Posts

2026-03-20

Introduction

When posting to multiple Facebook groups using JarveePro, duplicate content is one of the most common issues users face. However, this is not caused by the software—it’s a direct result of how content and campaign limits are configured. Understanding how text distribution works is essential to ensure clean and unique posting.

Q 1: Why does duplicate content happen in Facebook group campaigns?

Answer:

Duplicate content occurs when the same text is allowed to be reused across multiple groups or accounts. JarveePro will reuse available texts unless strict limits are applied. Without proper configuration, multiple accounts or posting cycles may repeat the same message across different groups.

Q 2: How do I prevent duplicate posts across Facebook groups?

To ensure each group receives unique content, configure the following:

Set

Times Allowed per Text

to

1–1

Times Allowed per Text by Account

Max uses per target

Use

Sequential mode

This guarantees that each text is only used once.

Q 3: What happens if I have more groups than texts?

Answer:

If the number of groups exceeds the number of available texts, JarveePro will only post as many times as there are unique texts.

👉 Example:

106 groups

102 texts

➡️ Only

102 groups will receive posts

The remaining groups will be skipped because no unused content is available. This is expected behavior and ensures no duplication occurs.

Q 4: Should I use random or sequential mode?

Sequential mode is recommended when avoiding duplicates. It ensures texts are used one by one without repetition. Random mode increases the risk of uneven usage and potential duplication.

Summary

Avoiding duplicate content in JarveePro depends on two key factors: correct usage limits and having enough unique texts. When limits are set to 1–1 and sequential mode is used, each text is posted only once. If there are more groups than texts, only the available unique content will be used, ensuring clean and non-repetitive posting.

Many older JarveePro knowledge base articles were originally written for Full Version, Business Version, or Enterprise users running multiple Facebook accounts at the same time.

Because of that, many tutorials focused heavily on:

Preventing the same account from repeatedly messaging users

Rotating messages across multiple accounts

Limiting duplicate outreach behavior

Distributing campaigns between dozens or hundreds of accounts

1 Facebook account

1 sending profile

Only have 1 Facebook account

Want to send messages to many profile URLs

1–100

1–50

1–10

for:

Times Allowed per Profile by Account

Times Allowed per Message

Times Allowed per Message by Account

The problem is:

These are

ranges

, not fixed values.

So if the setting is:

JarveePro may randomly choose:

25

or any value inside that range.

This is exactly why some campaigns suddenly stop after sending only:

3 messages

5 messages

8 messages

even when there are still dozens of profile URLs remaining.

The software is following the configured range correctly.

The Correct Configuration for Individual Version Users

If you only have:

1 Facebook account

1 message template

Many target profile URLs

then you should use

fixed values

, not random ranges.

For example:

If you want to message:

100 Facebook profile URLs

then all related limits should be configured as:

100 – 100

NOT:

1 – 100

This forces JarveePro to consistently allow the full campaign completion instead of randomly stopping early.

tab:

Times Allowed per Profile

Set:

1 – 1

This ensures:

Each target profile receives the message only once

No duplicate messaging occurs

Times Allowed per Profile by Account

Why?

Because:

You only have one sending account

That single account must be allowed to process all 100 profiles

Correct “Messages” Tab Settings

Inside the

Messages

tab, all limits should also use fixed values.

If your campaign targets:

100 profile URLs

then configure:

Times Allowed per Message

100 – 100

Times Allowed per Message by Account

(bottom section)

This ensures:

Your one message template can be reused across all 100 targets

The single account is allowed to fully complete the campaign

No random early stopping happens

Why Older Tutorials May Confuse Individual Users

Most older tutorials were designed for:

Full Version users

Agency users

Multi-account environments

Enterprise automation setups

Those users usually wanted:

Different accounts sending different messages

Strict anti-duplication limits

Account rotation behavior

Large-scale distribution systems

But Individual Version users have a very different workflow.

With only one connected Facebook account:

You are not distributing work across accounts

You are not rotating messages

You simply want one account to finish the entire profile list

That means your settings should focus on:

Fixed allocation

Stable completion

No randomization

Recommended Setup Summary

If you have:

1 Facebook account

1 message template

100 target profiles

then use:

Profile URLs Tab

Times Allowed per Profile → 1 – 1

Times Allowed per Profile by Account → 1 – 1

Messages Tab

Times Allowed per Message → 100 – 100

Times Allowed per Message by Account → 100 – 100

Bottom Times Allowed per Message → 100 – 100

This configuration allows:

One unique message per user

No duplicate messaging

Full campaign completion

Stable behavior for Individual Version users

Conclusion

JarveePro is highly flexible because it supports both:

Single-account users

Enterprise-scale automation users

However, using the wrong configuration style for your account type can easily create unexpected campaign behavior.

If you are using the Individual Version, avoid random ranges for messaging limits unless you intentionally want randomized stopping behavior.

For single-account outreach campaigns, fixed values like:

100 – 100

are the safest and most reliable approach for completing the full target profile list successfully.

How to Deploy OpenClaw with Docker (Step-by-Step Guide)

2026-03-20

Introduction

As AI-driven automation becomes more advanced, tools like OpenClaw are emerging as powerful execution layers behind platforms like JarveePro. To unlock its full potential, proper deployment is essential. In this guide, we walk through how to deploy OpenClaw using Docker, ensuring a stable and scalable setup for automation workflows.

Why Use Docker for OpenClaw?

Docker simplifies deployment by packaging OpenClaw with all its dependencies. This eliminates compatibility issues and allows you to run it consistently across local machines or VPS environments.

Key benefits include:

Easy setup and deployment

Isolated environment for stability

Scalability for larger automation operations

Prerequisites

Before starting, make sure you have:

A system with Docker installed

A valid OpenAI-compatible API key

Basic access to terminal or SSH (for VPS users)

Step 1: Run OpenClaw with Docker

Use the following command to deploy OpenClaw:

docker run -d \

--name op \

--cap-add=CHOWN \

--cap-add=SETUID \

--cap-add=SETGID \

--cap-add=DAC_OVERRIDE \

-e MODEL_ID=gpt-5.1 \

-e BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 \

-e API_KEY=YOUR KEY \

-e OPENAI_API_KEY=YOUR KEY \

-e API_PROTOCOL=openai-responses \

-e CONTEXT_WINDOW=200000 \

-e MAX_TOKENS=4096 \

-e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_BIND=lan \

-e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18789 \

-e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=YOUR TRUST IP:PORT \

-e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_ALLOW_INSECURE_AUTH=true \

-e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_DANGEROUSLY_DISABLE_DEVICE_AUTH=true \

-e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_AUTH_MODE=token \

-e OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=none \

-e WORKSPACE=/home/node/.openclaw/workspace \

-e OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_ENABLED=fs,bash,shell,curl \

-v /opt/openclaw:/home/node/.openclaw \

-v /opt/openclaw/workspace:/home/node/.openclaw/workspace \

-p 18789:18789 \

-p 18790:18790 \

--restart unless-stopped \

justlikemaki/openclaw-docker-cn-im:latest

Step 2: Configure Your Environment

Before running, update the following:

Replace

YOUR KEY

with your actual API key

Set

OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

to your trusted IP and port

Adjust ports if needed for your infrastructure

Step 3: Verify the Deployment

After running the container:

Check if it’s running:

docker ps

Access the gateway:

http://YOUR_SERVER_IP:18789

If everything is correct, OpenClaw should now be active and ready to receive tasks.

Step 4: Connect to JarveePro

Once OpenClaw is running:

Use the gateway URL inside JarveePro

Configure API communication

Start sending automation workflows

This creates a full pipeline where JarveePro handles execution logic and OpenClaw processes AI-driven decisions.

Best Practices

Use a VPS instead of a local machine for better uptime

Avoid insecure authentication in production

Monitor resource usage (CPU/RAM) for scaling

Separate automation environments for different projects

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Forgetting to replace API keys

Misconfiguring allowed origins

Running everything on one machine (limits scalability)

Using unsupported AI models

Summary

Deploying OpenClaw with Docker provides a reliable foundation for AI-powered automation. When combined with JarveePro and a capable model like gpt-5.1, it enables scalable, intelligent workflows that go far beyond traditional automation tools.

JarveePro offers several flexible ways to export account data, allowing marketers and automation users to back up, migrate, or share their setup safely. You can export usernames, passwords, proxies, cookies, and even browser cache to ensure a seamless transition between systems or VPS environments.

Below are the

three main export methods

available inside the JarveePro Accounts section.

Method 1: Export Accounts via Toolbar (Full Account Data)

This is the most detailed and customizable method to export all your account information.

Steps:

Go to the

Accounts

section.

Click the

Export

button in the top toolbar.

In the export window, select which

columns

to include:

Platform

– Platform name (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, etc.).

Category

– Group or project label.

Status

– Account status (Normal, Failed, etc.).

Account (Username/Email)

– Account login name.

Password

– Encrypted account password.

Proxy

– Proxy address assigned to the account.

Cookie

– Browser cookies for session restoration.

2FA

– Two-factor authentication code.

Token

– API or session token.

Choose file type:

.csv

– Ideal for spreadsheets or database imports.

.xlsx

– For Excel compatibility.

.txt

– For quick backups or scripts.

Adjust optional settings (Row/Column separators, include headers).

Click

Export

to save the file.

Use Case:

Export usernames, passwords, proxies, and cookies for account migration or backup.

Method 2: Export to ZIP (Includes Browser Cache)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kNus016LHk8

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GtIWreUgSTo

This method creates a complete backup that includes each account’s

browser cache

, making it ideal when transferring accounts between devices or VPSs without needing to re-login.

Steps:

Go to

Accounts → More (⋯)

on the toolbar.

Select

“Export to zip (includes browser cache)”

Choose where to save the ZIP file.

The exported ZIP will include:

Account credentials

Session cookies

Browser fingerprints and cache

Use Case:

Transfer accounts to another computer or VPS and continue automation without verification issues.

Method 3: Export Browser Cache Only (For JarveePro VPS Version)

This method is designed for the

JarveePro VPS version

, allowing users to

send the browser cache

directly to the VPS that the accounts are bound to. The accounts themselves are still

managed through the main JarveePro dashboard

, but their cache and sessions are maintained on the VPS for stability and security.

Steps:

Navigate to

Accounts → More (⋯)

in the toolbar.

Click

“Export browser cache to zip.”

Send or map the exported browser cache to the corresponding

VPS

where the account is hosted.

Once mapped, accounts continue to run and be managed through the

main JarveePro dashboard

, while the VPS handles login sessions and automation tasks.

Use Case:

For VPS-based setups where browser cache and session management are performed remotely, ensuring seamless operation without exposing account credentials.

Summary

JarveePro makes it easy to export your accounts in three different ways:

Full Account Export (.CSV/.XLSX/.TXT)

– export all details including username, password, proxy, and token.

Export to ZIP (with Browser Cache)

– create a complete backup for quick account migration.

Export Browser Cache Only

– Sends only the browser cache to the VPS; accounts still managed on the main dashboard.

By using the right export method, you can ensure your accounts, sessions, and proxies are safely preserved and easily restored when needed.

How to Group Accounts in JarveePro for Better Social Media Automation Management

2026-03-10

Introduction

When managing large numbers of social media accounts, organization becomes extremely important. Many automation users operate dozens or even hundreds of accounts across multiple platforms, making it difficult to control campaigns without a clear structure.

JarveePro allows users to organize accounts into logical groups so that campaigns, automation actions, and workflows can be managed more efficiently.

Account grouping helps marketers assign specific accounts to specific tasks, clients, or geographic markets, making large-scale automation much easier to control.

Why Grouping Accounts Matters

Grouping accounts provides several benefits for automation users:

Better campaign organization

Easier management of large numbers of accounts

More targeted automation strategies

Improved control over engagement distribution

Instead of managing hundreds of accounts individually, grouping allows marketers to run campaigns on

specific sets of accounts based on defined criteria

Common Ways to Group Accounts in JarveePro

Below are several practical ways users organize their automation accounts.

1. Grouping by Account Provider

Many users purchase or source accounts from different providers.

Grouping by provider helps track:

account quality

account reliability

performance differences between providers

Example groups:

Provider A accounts

Provider B accounts

aged accounts provider

phone verified accounts

This makes it easier to identify which account sources perform best.

2. Grouping by Import Date

Accounts can also be grouped based on when they were added to the system.

Imported this month

Imported last quarter

Recently added accounts

Older warmed-up accounts

This is useful for

account warm-up strategies

, where newly added accounts run lighter automation tasks first.

3. Grouping by Client

Agencies managing multiple clients often assign different account pools to different clients.

Example:

Client A promotion accounts

Client B engagement accounts

Client C marketing accounts

This prevents accounts from mixing across campaigns.

4. Grouping by Location

Some marketing campaigns require accounts from specific regions.

Examples:

US accounts

UAE accounts

UK accounts

Europe accounts

This is especially useful for:

regional marketing campaigns

localized engagement

country-specific audiences

5. Grouping by Gender

Certain marketing campaigns require comments or engagement from specific demographics.

US Male accounts

US Female accounts

Female lifestyle accounts

Male sports accounts

Some SMM panel campaigns specifically request this type of segmentation.

6. Grouping by Campaign Type

Accounts can be dedicated to specific automation tasks.

Example groups:

like campaign accounts

comment campaign accounts

follow campaign accounts

story view accounts

Separating accounts by campaign helps distribute actions more naturally.

7. Grouping by Platform

Users managing multiple platforms may group accounts like:

Instagram automation accounts

Facebook marketing accounts

TikTok growth accounts

Twitter engagement accounts

This simplifies campaign configuration across different social networks.

8. Grouping by Risk Level

Automation users sometimes categorize accounts by risk tolerance.

Example groups:

high activity accounts

low activity accounts

testing accounts

backup accounts

This helps prevent losing high-value accounts during experimentation.

9. Grouping by Proxy or Network

Accounts can also be grouped based on the proxy infrastructure they use.

residential proxy accounts

mobile proxy accounts

datacenter proxy accounts

This helps manage network distribution and troubleshoot connection issues.

10. Grouping by Purpose

Some accounts serve very specific roles within automation strategies.

Examples:

engagement accounts

boosting accounts

content posting accounts

scraping accounts

Separating roles helps maintain cleaner automation workflows.

11. Grouping by VPS or Device

Users running automation at scale often operate multiple servers or devices. Grouping accounts by

VPS, server, or device

makes it easier to track where accounts are hosted and managed.

This is especially useful when using dedicated automation servers such as a

JarveePro VPS environment

Example groups:

VPS 1 – Instagram Accounts

VPS 2 – TikTok Accounts

VPS 3 – Warm-up Accounts

Server A – Client Campaigns

Server B – Testing Accounts

Grouping accounts by VPS helps users:

quickly identify which accounts belong to which server

balance automation load across multiple machines

troubleshoot issues related to specific servers

avoid mixing accounts across different environments

For example, if a user operates

300 automation accounts across three VPS servers

, grouping them by server allows the user to immediately see which accounts are running on

VPS 1, VPS 2, or VPS 3

This becomes particularly useful when performing maintenance, scaling infrastructure, or migrating accounts between servers.

Example Automation Strategy Using Groups

For example, a marketer managing 100 accounts might organize them like this:

Group 1:

US Male accounts (comment campaigns)

Group 2:

US Female accounts (engagement campaigns)

Group 3:

UAE accounts (regional marketing campaigns)

Group 4:

Warm-up accounts (low activity automation)

Group 5:

High trust aged accounts (main campaigns)

This structured approach makes it much easier to control large automation operations.

Summary

Grouping accounts is one of the simplest but most powerful ways to organize large-scale social media automation.

By grouping accounts based on factors such as provider, import date, location, gender, campaign type, or client, marketers can run more targeted campaigns and manage large numbers of accounts efficiently.

JarveePro provides the flexibility needed to structure automation workflows in ways that match real-world marketing operations.

title: How to Prevent Duplicate Actions Using the JarveePro Scheduler
summary: How to Prevent Duplicate Actions Using the JarveePro Scheduler
text:
How to Prevent Duplicate Actions Using the JarveePro Scheduler

2026-01-12

Introduction

Duplicate actions are one of the most common issues users face when running scheduled campaigns in JarveePro—especially when looping tasks like

Facebook friend requests

Instagram comments

, or

content-based actions

Many users assume the scheduler should “remember” where it left off. In reality,

the new JarveePro Scheduler works based on task records

, not sequence memory.

This article explains

why duplicates happen

, how the

new scheduler logic works

, and

exactly how to configure it

to prevent repeated actions.

Why Duplicate Actions Happen

JarveePro does

not create duplicate actions by default

Duplicates only occur when the user enables

Reset/Cleanup

mode, which is designed for looping campaigns such as story views or video watches.

By default:

The scheduler restarts the campaign

Previously completed targets won't be reprocessed

This behavior is

intentional

, not a bug

The key lies in

task record handling

Understanding the New JarveePro Scheduler Logic

In the new scheduler UI, each campaign run creates

task records

These records determine:

Which actions were completed

Which targets were already processed

Whether the campaign starts fresh or continues logically

Critical Option: Task Record Cleanup

Inside the scheduler settings, you’ll see this option:

☐ Clean up completed task records when starting a task

This checkbox controls duplicate behavior.

How the “Clean Up Completed Task Records” Option Works

✅ When ENABLED

All previous task records are deleted

Campaign starts from the beginning

Duplicates WILL happen

Best for:

Engagement farming

Repeating actions on purpose

Evergreen campaigns

❌ When DISABLED (Recommended)

Completed targets are remembered

Scheduler skips already-processed users

Campaign continues naturally

Duplicates are PREVENTED

Facebook friend requests

DM campaigns

Lead-based workflows

Sequential target lists (A → B → C)

To prevent duplicates, this option must remain UNCHECKED

Correct Scheduler Setup to Prevent Duplicate Actions

Step-by-Step Configuration

Open

Campaign → Scheduler

Select:

Schedule Type:

Loop Run

DO NOT check

❌ Clean up completed task records when starting a task

Set your interval (hours or minutes)

Enable Scheduler

That’s it.

JarveePro will now

remember completed actions

and avoid duplicates.

Important Clarification: Scheduler vs Content Explorer

⚠️ The scheduler

only applies to campaigns

, not Content Explorer searches.

Content Explorer:

Uses platform rules

May re-scan content

Has separate duplicate controls

Scheduler:

Controls campaign execution

Relies on task records

Trying to apply scheduler logic to Content Explorer will

not work

Common Use Cases & Best Practices

Facebook Friend Requests

Upload target profile URLs once

Disable task record cleanup

Scheduler continues target-by-target without repeats

Instagram Comment Campaigns

Works best with

Content Aware Comment

Avoid aggressive loop intervals

Use delays

High-Volume Campaigns

Use VPS with sufficient RAM/CPU

Avoid excessive browser instances

Scheduler logic remains consistent regardless of scale

Summary

Duplicate actions are caused by task record cleanup

JarveePro Scheduler relies on task history

Disable cleanup to prevent duplicates

Scheduler applies only to campaigns, not Content Explorer

Proper configuration ensures smooth, sequential execution

, SMM panel orders are processed automatically — JarveePro assigns accounts, performs actions, and reports back results.

, you need to manually track which accounts executed which actions. This is where the

JarveePro Records feature

becomes essential.

Tracking SMM Panel Orders Without API

Open Records

in JarveePro.

– Select the social platform (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, etc.).

– Match the customer’s order date range.

JarveePro will display:

Which

The

exact time

campaign name

linked to the activity.

Why This Matters for SMM Panel Agencies

A customer orders

100 Instagram followers today

One week later, they order

another 100 followers

With JarveePro Records, you can review which accounts were used in the first order to decide whether to re-use them or select new accounts.

with every order.

By combining your SMM Panel services with JarveePro’s

How to Use the Task Scheduler in JarveePro

2025-09-08

The Task Scheduler allows you to control

when

and

how often

your automation runs. Different types of tasks may require different scheduling approaches.

Below, we’ll explain each option and give you examples for common scenarios like posting/broadcasts vs. following/unfollowing.

Scheduler Options Explained

Enable Schedule

Activates the scheduler and lets you set the start time.

Stop the task after [X hours]

Defines how long the task will run before stopping automatically.

Loop execution and task starts again every [X days/hours]

Sets how often the task restarts. For example, “1 Day” means it will restart every 24 hours.

Loop times (Current/Max)

Controls how many times the task repeats.

= unlimited (the task runs daily without stopping).

Any number = the task will stop after reaching that count.

Automatically reset completed tasks when starting a task

Resets the task to start from the beginning each time. Only use this when you want a

fresh cycle

(e.g., reposting content daily).

Practical Examples

Example 1: Posting or Broadcast Campaigns

For posting videos, images, or broadcast messages, you usually want the task to

start fresh every day

Recommended Settings:

Enable Schedule

Stop task after = 2 Hours

Loop execution = 1 Day

Loop times = 0 (unlimited)

Automatically reset completed tasks

Result:

Each day the campaign will start from the beginning, run for 2 hours, then stop. The next day it will restart with new content.

Example 2: Following / Unfollowing Tasks

For sequential actions like following or unfollowing, you usually want the task to

pick up where it left off

, not restart.

Stop task after = 3 Hours

Do not select “Automatically reset completed tasks”

The task runs for 3 hours daily, pauses, and the next day continues from where it left off in the list.

Notice:

Use

Reset = ON

for campaigns that should restart daily (posting, broadcasts).

Reset = OFF

for campaigns that should continue sequentially (follows, unfollows).

This ensures your tasks run exactly as intended—whether you want daily fresh campaigns or ongoing actions that pick up from yesterday.

Independent device fingerprints

Separated action schedules

text:
Instagram Repost Settings & Troubleshooting

2026-02-13

Overview

The Instagram Repost tool allows you to automate content curation by scraping and resharing high-performing posts. To maintain account safety and system stability in 2026, specific limits and timing logics must be followed.

Technical Troubleshooting (FAQ)

Q1: Why am I receiving the "【Repost】failed to execute... (408) Request Timeout" error?

Answer:

The

408 Request Timeout

is a signal that the connection between JarveePro and Instagram’s servers was severed before the task could finish. This is almost always caused by

Batch Overload

The Cause:

Attempting to scrape more than 100 posts (especially heavy Reels or high-res carousels) in a single operation. The high network demand causes the remote server to time out to protect itself from perceived "scraping attacks."

The Fix:

Limit your

Scrape Quantity to 50 posts or fewer

. Smaller batches complete faster, reduce resource competition in the background, and prevent your IP from being flagged for suspicious activity.

Q2: How does the "Timer" logic work when Restarting vs. Continuing a campaign?

Understanding how JarveePro calculates the 1,440-minute (24-hour) cycle is key to consistent posting:

Continue:

The tool checks the timestamp of the

last successful action

. It will wait for the remainder of your set interval (e.g., 24 hours) to pass before it attempts to post again.

Restart:

This clears the execution "memory" for that cycle.

Note:

To make the tool run

immediately

after a restart, ensure your "Start Time" includes the current hour and that you haven't already hit your "Daily Max" limit.

Pro Tip:

If you need to force a post for testing, temporarily lower the "Wait Time" to 1 minute, let it execute, and then change it back to 1,440 minutes.

Developer Best Practices for SMM Providers

To avoid "Running" campaigns from hanging and draining system resources (VPS/PC), follow these optimization rules:

Limit Batch Sizes:

Keep target scraping under 50 items.

Monitor Concurrent Tasks:

Avoid running too many "Heavy Scrape" campaigns simultaneously on the same IP.

Interval Gaps:

Ensure your posting intervals are long enough to simulate human behavior, but your scraping batch is small enough to finish in under 3 minutes.

Summary

Fix JarveePro 408 Request Timeout errors by limiting scraping to 50 posts. Learn the difference between Restarting and Continuing campaigns to manage 24-hour posting cycles efficiently.

Many users planning large Instagram campaigns ask similar questions:

Is automation safe?

Can I manage 100+ accounts without bans?

Can I safely schedule posts and reels?

This article answers those questions clearly and applies to

Q1: Is JarveePro safe for managing multiple Instagram accounts?

Answer:

Yes, when used correctly. JarveePro is designed for multi-account automation using controlled behavior, persistent cookies, and proxy separation. Safety depends more on configuration and pacing than the software itself.

Q2: Can JarveePro handle 100+ Instagram accounts?

Yes. JarveePro can manage 100+ accounts when run on a device with proper proxy allocation and conservative daily limits. Large-scale users typically separate accounts across VPS environments for stability.

Q3: Does JarveePro use fingerprints like anti-detect browsers?

Yes. JarveePro was built on a browser-based fingerprint tool. Moreover, it focuses on account behavior consistency, cookie persistence, and proxy isolation. It is built more

Q4: Is JarveePro safer or less safe than anti-detect browsers?

Yes it is way better. For most users, they serve different purposes. Anti-detect browsers are better for manual account handling. JarveePro is better for long-term automated campaigns.

Q5: Can JarveePro auto-post Instagram posts and reels?

Yes. JarveePro supports scheduling Instagram posts and reels across multiple accounts. Posting frequency and timing should remain realistic to avoid detection.

Q6: Is scheduling Instagram content safe at scale?

Answer:

Scheduling is safe when content is rotated, timing is randomized, and accounts are not pushed beyond natural behavior. JarveePro includes tools to manage these factors.

Q7: Do I need a VPS to run large Instagram campaigns?

For more than 1000 accounts, a VPS is strongly recommended. It provides a stable environment and prevents local IP conflicts when managing many accounts.

Q8: What causes most Instagram bans when using automation tools?

Most bans are caused by aggressive settings, poor-quality proxies, or skipping account warm-up. The tool itself is rarely the direct cause.

Q9: Is JarveePro suitable for Instagram-only campaigns?

Yes. JarveePro can be used exclusively for Instagram without enabling other platforms. Many users run Instagram-only campaigns focused on posting, stories, and controlled engagement.

Summary

JarveePro is safe for managing 100+ Instagram accounts when used with proper infrastructure, realistic pacing, and account warm-up. It is an automation tool designed for scalable campaigns, not shortcuts. Safety depends on how it is used.

real-time monitoring & trigger system

that watches for activity you care about across social media, then

continuous engagement engine

Introduction

AI Templates under

JarveePro Content Explorer

are one of the most powerful — and most misunderstood — features in the entire system.

Many users assume AI Templates are just for “generating posts.” In reality, they are the

core engine behind content intelligence

, enabling:

Context-aware posting

Search-driven engagement

RSS-based trend posting

Auto-generated comments and replies

Multilingual, categorized content at scale

This article explains

what AI Templates are

when to use them

how they interact with Search, RSS, and variables

, and

why some options (Generate Post / Generate JSON) exist at all

If you’ve ever wondered

“When should I use AI Templates vs normal campaign content?”

— this guide answers that clearly.

What Are AI Templates in Content Explorer?

AI Templates are

reusable AI instructions

that tell JarveePro:

What type of content to generate

What context to use

Which platform the content is for

How the output should behave

They are not tied to a single platform or campaign.

Instead, they act as a

universal content brain

for JarveePro.

AI Templates can be used for:

Posts

Comments

Replies

Descriptions

Engagement text

Structured content (JSON)

Why AI Templates Need a Separate Knowledge Base Article

AI Templates are often confused with:

Campaign “Generate Content”

One-click AI posting

Simple caption generators

That confusion leads to:

Wrong setup

Overcomplicated workflows

Misuse of JSON output

Underutilization of Search + Generate

This article separates

auto-posting

content loading

, and

engagement automation

into clear use cases.

Core Use Cases of AI Templates

AI Templates can be grouped into

three main use cases

Use Case 1: Content Loading & Structured Generation (Advanced Users)

This use case is for users who want to

prepare content in advance

and load it into campaigns.

When to Use This

Bulk content preparation

Multilingual content packs

Structured content libraries

Loading posts into campaigns manually

Relevant Options

Generate Post 1 / Generate Post 2

Generate as JSON Format

Important Clarification

These options are

not designed for casual auto-posting

They exist for:

Advanced workflows

Content importing

Users who need structured output

If you just want to auto-post daily content,

this is usually unnecessary

Use Case 2A: Auto Posting with AI Only (Broadcasting)

Goal:

Post branded or promotional content without relying on external data.

When to use:

SaaS promotion (e.g., JarveePro updates)

Evergreen marketing

Affiliate offers

Motivational or educational content

Key Point:

RSS is NOT required

Why:

You already know what you want to say. AI is just helping generate variations.

Use Case 2B: Auto Posting with RSS + AI (News & Trend-Aware Content)

Generate content that reacts to

latest news, trends, or market movements

Trading

Crypto

Finance

Breaking news

Industry updates

Workflow:

RSS monitors trusted sources

New articles are detected

RSS title + description passed into AI Template

AI generates timely, relevant posts

Key Difference:

RSS adds

fresh context

— AI transforms it into

platform-ready content

Use Case 3: Search + Generate (Engagement Automation)

This is the

most powerful and most misunderstood

use case.

Search + Generate allows JarveePro to:

Search real posts, videos, or discussions

Extract context

Generate

relevant comments or replies

This is

not random AI output

— it’s context-driven.

Why Variables Are Required for Search + Generate

Variables tell the AI

what role it is playing

Without variables:

Output is generic

Comments feel disconnected

Engagement looks artificial

With variables:

AI understands the platform

Content matches the context

Engagement feels human

Examples of Variables

Instagram post

Instagram comment

TikTok video

YouTube comment

Facebook post

Variables define

how the AI interprets the content it sees

Two Ways to Use AI Templates for Engagement

This distinction should be very clear.

Method 1: Search + Generate Task (Manual & Reviewable)

Location:

JarveePro → Content Explorer → Search + Generate

How It Works

You define search conditions (hashtags, keywords, users)

JarveePro fetches real posts

AI Template uses variables

Content is generated for review

Best For

Testing templates

Reviewing AI output

High-precision engagement

Learning how variables affect results

This method gives

maximum control

Method 2: AI Templates Only (Fully Automated & Context-Aware)

In this mode:

No manual search task is required

JarveePro automatically feeds context

AI generates

content-aware comments and replies

Best For

24/7 engagement

Auto comment replies

Large-scale automation

Hands-off workflows

This is where JarveePro feels truly

intelligent and autonomous

Categorizing AI Templates (Highly Recommended)

AI Templates are most powerful when

organized properly

You can categorize them by:

Use Case

Posting

Commenting

Replying

Direct messages

Review replies

Language

English

Spanish

Arabic

Mixed-language

Localized variants

Content Group

Promotional

Educational

Conversational

News-based

Trend-driven

This turns Content Explorer into a

content management and intelligence system

, not just a generator.

What AI Templates Are NOT

It’s important to clarify expectations.

AI Templates are not:

Mandatory for simple scheduled posts

Required for basic automation

A replacement for campaign content fields

They are designed for

context, scale, and intelligence

Best Practices

Use

simple campaign content

for basic posting

RSS + AI Templates

for trend-aware automation

Search + Generate

for engagement

JSON output

only when loading content manually

Always define variables for engagement workflows

Organize templates by use case and language

Conclusion

AI Templates under JarveePro Content Explorer are not just a content generator — they are the

foundation of smart automation

When used correctly, they allow you to:

Generate context-aware posts

Engage intelligently at scale

React to real-time content

Automate without sounding automated

The key is understanding

when to use them

and

which mode fits your goal

Once mastered, AI Templates become one of the most powerful tools in JarveePro’s ecosystem.

text:
JarveePro API Guide: TaskUnit Creation, URL Allocation & Common Execution Errors

2026-04-20

Introduction

When using the JarveePro API for Instagram automation, many users assume that:

More accounts = more parallel execution units.”

That’s not always true.

Recent cases show confusion around:

Tasks collapsing into a single TaskUnit

“Value cannot be null” errors

“Open Browser Error” and “Browser closed” issues

Incorrect parameter distribution across accounts

This guide breaks down exactly how

TaskUnits are generated

, how

URL allocation works

, and why tasks may fail even when the API request is technically valid.

1. Why Your Task Creates Only 1 TaskUnit (Even with 50–100 Accounts)

This is

not a bug

JarveePro builds TaskUnits based on

parameter distribution rules

, not simply the number of accounts.

Key Rule

TaskUnits are primarily determined by the

MainKey parameter

(for Instagram, usually

Url

).

So:

10 accounts + 1 URL → 1 TaskUnit

1 account + 10 URLs → 1 TaskUnit

10 accounts + 10 URLs → multiple TaskUnits (depending on allocation settings)

Why This Happens

The system groups execution by

parameter units

, not accounts.

If your task only has:

"Url": ["single_url"]

Then all accounts are grouped into

one execution unit

, even if 100 accounts are provided.

2. The Real Control: URL Allocation Parameters

Inside your request:

"Parameter": {

"Url": {

"Parameters": [...],

"UseNoData": false,

"AccountUseNum": 1,

"UseNum": 100

These fields control everything:

UseNoData (Highest Priority)

true

→ URL can be reused infinitely

Every account can use the same URL

Overrides all other allocation rules

AccountUseNum

How many times a single URL can be used

Default =

(this is where many setups break)

If you have:

1 URL

50 accounts

AccountUseNum = 1

→ Only

1 account can use that URL

, others fail or collapse

UseNum

Total allowed usage count across the task

Does NOT control TaskUnit splitting directly

3. Fix for “Only 1 TaskUnit” Problem

If your goal is:

“1 URL → many accounts → multiple executions”

You must use:

Option A (Recommended)

"UseNoData": true

This allows:

Unlimited reuse of URL

Proper distribution across all accounts

Option B

"AccountUseNum": 50

Manually match it to account count.

4. Understanding the “Value cannot be null” Error

Error:

Instagram EX: Value cannot be null. Parameter name: value

This is

not random

. It means:

A required parameter defined by the TaskType is missing or null.

Example: LikePost

Requires ONLY:

Url

(MainKey)

If:

URL is empty

URL allocation fails

URL not assigned to a TaskUnit

→ This error appears

Hidden Cause

When allocation rules block URLs from being assigned (e.g.,

AccountUseNum=1

with many accounts), some TaskUnits end up with

no usable parameter

, triggering this exception.

5. TaskSettingJson: When It’s Required (and When It’s Not)

LikePost

Does

NOT

require

TaskSettingJson

ViewStoriesReels

❌ DOES require settings

Correct format:

"TaskSettingJson": {

"WatchTimeMin": 10,

"WatchTimeMax": 20,

"WatchTimeFull": true

If missing → task may fail or behave unpredictably.

6. Is ViewStoriesReels the Correct TaskType for Reels?

Yes—but incomplete usage is the problem.

You must include:

Url

InstagramViewStoriesReelsSetting

Without settings → execution is invalid.

7. Why You See “Open Browser Error” or “Browser Closed”

This is

separate from API structure

It happens at runtime due to:

Common Causes

VPS Mode disabled (required for browser execution in many setups)

Browser environment not initialized

Fingerprint/session issues

Resource limits (trying to open 50 browsers at once)

Only 1 thread allowed → only 1 browser opens

Important Insight

API success ≠ runtime success

Your logs already confirm:

API layer working

Task creation working

Failure happens during execution

8. Why Only 1 Browser Opens for 50 Accounts

This usually means:

Thread/concurrency limits are set to 1

Or system resources restrict scaling

Or accounts are grouped into 1 TaskUnit (most likely in your case)

Remember:

TaskUnit = execution container

If you only have 1 TaskUnit → only 1 browser instance is needed.

9. Advanced Controls for Task Distribution

These fields influence execution behavior:

MainUseParam

Whether main parameter drives execution logic

Reallocation

"Reallocation": true

Forces redistribution of TaskUnits during execution

MainKey

Defines the parameter used for grouping (usually

Url

10. Key Takeaways (What Actually Matters)

JarveePro distributes tasks based on

parameters, not accounts

is the

core driver

for Instagram tasks

Wrong allocation settings → tasks collapse or fail

“Value cannot be null” = parameter assignment failure

“Open Browser Error” = runtime/environment issue, not API

ViewStoriesReels requires

extra settings

, unlike LikePost

Summary

Most API issues are not caused by incorrect request formats—but by

misunderstanding how JarveePro builds execution units internally

If you remember just one thing:

Accounts don’t create TaskUnits—parameters do.

Once you fix parameter allocation (especially

UseNoData

and

AccountUseNum

), most “mysterious” failures disappear.

text:
JarveePro API: How to Check Task Results & Find Logs Easily

2026-04-13

Not seeing clear logs from your JarveePro API tasks? This guide explains how

CheckTask

really works, where logs are stored, and how to quickly find the information you need to debug tasks with confidence.

Introduction

If you’ve ever created a task using the JarveePro API and thought:

“It failed… but where are the logs?”

You’re not alone.

This is one of the most common questions from developers—and the good news is:

the logs are there.

They’re just not where most people expect them to be.

Once you understand how JarveePro structures tasks and execution data, debugging becomes much easier—and much faster.

Understanding How JarveePro Tasks Work

JarveePro uses a

task-based execution system

You send a task (e.g., post, like, campaign)

The system processes it asynchronously

You check the result using the API

At first glance, this feels straightforward. But there’s an important detail:

A “task” is not a single action — it’s a

collection of sub-tasks

Each sub-task represents a step in the execution process.

What

CheckTask

Actually Returns

The

API does more than just return a status.

It returns:

The main task

All related

sub-tasks

Execution status for each step

Associated messages (logs)

So instead of a simple response, you get a

task execution tree

Why Logs Seem “Missing”

Here’s where most confusion comes from.

Many developers expect something like:

"status": "failed",

"log": "error details here"

But JarveePro actually returns logs inside sub-tasks, like this:

"task": {

"children": [

"log": "Account is not logged in"

Key:

Logs are

not at the top level

Logs are stored

inside sub-tasks

You must

iterate through them

Common Reasons You Don’t See Logs

1. Not checking sub-tasks

If you only look at the main task response, you’ll miss the actual logs.

2. Task still running

If you call

CheckTask

too early:

logs may not exist yet

results may be incomplete

3. Some steps don’t produce logs

Not every sub-task generates detailed output.

How to Correctly Retrieve Logs via API

Step 1: Call

Type = CommandType.CheckTask

Data = task

Step 2: Traverse the response

Look for structures like:

Children

SubTasks

Items

Step 3: Extract logs

For each sub-task:

check

status

read

log

or

message

Step 4: Retry if needed

If the task is:

running → wait and retry

queued → wait and retry

Advanced Method: View Logs Directly from the Database

If you’re comfortable working with databases, there’s an even faster way to debug tasks.

JarveePro stores all task data locally in a SQLite database:

/Data/TaskDb.db

Where to Find the Logs

Inside the database, navigate to:

main → TaskUnit

This table contains the actual execution records.

Important fields:

TaskType

→ type of task

TaskDataJson

→ task payload

TaskResult

→ success (1) or failure (0)

Message

actual execution log

StartTime

EndTime

→ timing

Example Logs You’ll See

From real task records:

Account is not logged in

Open Browser Error

network error

platform-related failures

This is the exact information developers are usually trying to get from the API.

How to Query Logs

You can use any SQLite tool (such as DB Browser, DBeaver, or Navicat).

Example query:

SELECT TaskType, TaskResult, Message, StartTime, EndTime

FROM TaskUnit

ORDER BY StartTime DESC

LIMIT 100;

Why This Method Is So Useful

Compared to the API:

API (

CheckTask

structured

requires parsing

logs are nested

Database

direct

complete

immediate

When to Use Database Debugging

This method is especially helpful when:

API responses are unclear

logs seem missing

tasks fail without explanation

you need faster troubleshooting

Best Practices for Reliable Debugging

To get the most out of JarveePro API:

1. Always check sub-tasks

That’s where the real information lives.

2. Add retry logic

Don’t assume results are instant.

3. Store API responses

Useful for tracking patterns and debugging issues.

4. Use database logs when needed

Especially for deeper troubleshooting.

Conclusion

JarveePro doesn’t hide logs—it just organizes them differently.

Instead of returning a simple message, it gives you the full execution process.

Once you understand that:

CheckTask

= task tree

logs = inside sub-tasks

database = source of truth

Debugging becomes straightforward.

If

were named:

“GetTaskExecutionTree”

Most of this confusion wouldn’t exist.

But now that you know how it works, you can navigate it with confidence—and solve issues much faster.

text:
JarveePro Campaign Settings Explained: Account Delay, Action Delay and Scheduler

2026-02-26

Overview

JarveePro provides multiple delay control mechanisms to ensure safe, realistic, and properly spaced automation execution. These delay systems allow you to control how frequently actions run between accounts, between campaigns, and across scheduled intervals.

There are three main delay types:

Account Delay (Account Interval Delay)

Campaign Action Delay

Scheduler (Planned Execution Delay)

Understanding the difference between these is essential for proper automation behavior.

1. Account Interval Delay (Delay Between Accounts)

What it does

This setting controls the delay between the same account executing the same campaign.

If multiple accounts are selected in a campaign, JarveePro will execute the campaign sequentially based on this delay for every accounts.

Example

If Account Interval Delay is set to

2 hours (7200 seconds)

Execution sequence:

Account 1 executes campaign

Wait 2 hours

And so on

This applies only between accounts within the same campaign.

Important Notes

Maximum value: 10,000 seconds

Only applies for the same accounts that are selected

Does not affect actions for multiple accounts

Helps prevent too many actions for the same account

When to use

Recommended when:

Managing multiple accounts

Avoiding simultaneous actions with the same accounts

Creating more natural execution patterns

2. Campaign Action Delay (Delay Between Campaign Executions)

What it does

This controls the delay between each campaign execution cycle.

This delay applies even when only one account is used.

Example

If Campaign Action Delay is set to

24 hours (86400 seconds)

Execution sequence:

Campaign executes once

Wait 24 hours

Campaign executes again

Repeat continuously

Important Notes

Maximum value: 10,000 seconds (Available on JarveePro Version

4.0.0.2

Applies per campaign

Controls campaign repetition timing

Works independently of account delay

When to use

Recommended when:

Running recurring campaigns

Automating daily actions

Preventing excessive action frequency

3. JarveePro Scheduler (Planned Execution System)

What it does

The Scheduler provides advanced control over campaign execution timing using structured schedules instead of simple delays.

Unlike Action Delay, the Scheduler can start, stop, and repeat campaigns based on defined timing rules.

How Scheduler works

Example configuration:

Schedule Type: Number of Runs

Start Time: Set specific time

Interval: Every 1 day

Total Runs: 3 times

Execution sequence:

Campaign starts at defined time

Executes 3 Times

Stops automatically after run once and waits 1 day , then start the second time.

Repeats until

Total Runs (

3 times)

is reached

Major Advantages of Scheduler

Scheduler allows:

Automatic stopping after execution

Resource optimization

Precise execution timing

Loop execution control

Fully automated operation cycles

This is more advanced and efficient than Action Delay alone.

Important Scheduler Behavior Notes

Scheduler does NOT automatically stop when running loop campaigns.

If a campaign is running and Scheduler is applied:

Scheduler controls future executions

Existing running campaigns must be manually stopped if needed

Scheduler state is managed through:

Campaign Manager → JarveePro Scheduler

Difference Between Action Delay and Scheduler

Best Practice Recommendations

For beginners:

Use Campaign Action Delay only

For advanced users:

Use Scheduler for full automation control

For large-scale automation:

Combine:

Account Interval Delay

Scheduler

Proper account limits

This creates safe and scalable automation.

Example Recommended Configuration

Safe daily automation setup:

Account Interval Delay: 300–900 seconds

Campaign Action Delay: 600

–1500

seconds

Scheduler: Every 24 hours

Execution Count: Unlimited (loop)

Common Mistakes

Most common user errors include:

Setting delay too low

Not using Scheduler

Running too many actions simultaneously

Not spacing account execution

Proper delay configuration prevents account restrictions.

Summary

JarveePro provides powerful delay control through:

Account Interval Delay

Campaign Action Delay

Scheduler

Scheduler is the most advanced and recommended method for controlling campaign timing.

text:
JarveePro Content Explorer – Template & Comment Generation Guide

2025-09-26

What is JarveePro Content Explorer?

JarveePro Content Explorer helps you manage and generate posts, comments for your social media automation campaigns. It supports both

manual import

and

AI auto-generate

modes, allowing flexibility for different use cases. You can also update template configurations to ensure your latest settings are always applied.

What are the available comment generation modes in JarveePro?

JarveePro offers two modes:

Manual Import (TXT / CSV / Excel)

Upload a TXT, CSV, or Excel file, and each line will be imported as one comment.

Auto-AI-Generate (No manual import required)

In Auto-Generate Comment mode, comments are generated dynamically during task execution, based on the content of the target post. This means you don’t need to prepare or upload comments in advance.

How does Auto-AI-Generate mode work?

When you select Auto-AI-Generate mode, the system waits until the task starts running. At that time, JarveePro automatically analyzes the target post and creates relevant comments.

Tip:

If you see no comments before the task runs, this is normal. The system will generate them dynamically once execution begins.

How do I know if JarveePro is generating comments?

JarveePro only generates comments during

task execution

. When the task runs, the system opens a browser, analyzes the target post, and then creates comments dynamically.

You won’t see comments in advance — they are generated in real time while the post is being processed.

How do I update templates in JarveePro Content Explorer?

You can easily refresh your templates to apply the latest configuration.

Click

Update JarveePro Content Explorer

to sync your templates.

If successful, you will see the message:

“Template updated successfully. The latest configuration has been synced.”

Why is there no data when I try to preview comments?

If no post content is available at the time, JarveePro will not display generated comments. Instead, the system will generate them automatically once the task runs. This prevents errors and ensures comments are always relevant to the live post.

Can I switch between manual import and auto-generate modes?

Yes. When entering Content Explorer, you can choose which mode to use:

Manual Import

→ Upload your own prepared comments.

Auto-AI-Generate

→ Let JarveePro generate comments automatically.

This flexibility ensures both businesses that prefer predefined comments and those relying on AI automation can use the system effectively.

Key Takeaways

Manual Import Mode

→ Upload TXT/CSV/Excel with comments.

Auto-AI-Generate Mode

→ AI creates comments during task execution, no manual input needed.

Update Templates

→ Always click refresh to sync latest configurations.

Status Messages

→ Know whether the system is waiting, generating, or synced.

By understanding these functions, you can fully leverage JarveePro Content Explorer to streamline comment generation and keep your campaigns running efficiently.

Q1: I set up company monitoring and reposting successfully, but commenting stays in “Waiting” mode. Why doesn’t it start?

Answer:

In JarveePro, commenting tasks depend on

eligible triggers

, not just previously found posts. Even though monitoring and reposting are running, commenting may remain in “Waiting” because:

The commenting task is configured to wait for

newly discovered posts

, not cached results

Monitoring, posting, and commenting share the same execution timing or threads

Campaign or global thread limits are already occupied

The workflow is sequential by design (monitor → collect → comment)

“Waiting” does not indicate an error. It means there are currently no qualifying items for the commenting task to process.

Q2: The tutorial video shows an example for Facebook, but not for Twitter. What should I enter for Twitter?

The same format applies.

JarveePro uses a

platform-agnostic structure

for monitoring, AI templates, and task configuration. If a format works for Facebook, it works for Twitter/X as well. The only difference is the platform selection—not the input structure.

Q3: When using AI Templates, should I generate 100 posts in one prompt and return them in JSON format?

Answer:

No. Each AI Template execution in JarveePro is designed to generate

one post per run

Generating multiple posts in a single prompt can cause:

Parsing errors

Execution delays

Task failures

Best practice:

Configure the AI Template to generate

one post

, and allow JarveePro to loop or schedule repeated executions automatically.

Q4: If I want to generate crypto-related posts instead of JarveePro posts, do I just modify the prompt content?

Yes.

You only need to modify the

topic and style instructions

in the prompt. The structure remains the same. JarveePro does not restrict content categories—the AI Template output depends entirely on the prompt you provide.

Q5: How can I grow and collect followers from a Twitter (X) Community?

Answer:

This feature will need custom development with extra fee.

Most issues arise from misunderstood task dependencies, AI template execution logic, or platform limitations—not from software errors. Understanding how monitoring, commenting, threads, and AI templates work together is essential for smooth and scalable automation.

Q1: Why is my Instagram account getting flagged for bot activity?

Answer:

Getting flagged is usually not about your account being “bad,” but about how your actions are perceived by Instagram.

Common triggers include:

Following too many accounts daily

Reaching action limits too frequently

Performing actions too quickly or consistently

When Instagram detects patterns that resemble automation, it escalates responses:

First: Captchas

Then: Identity verification (e.g., photo submission)

Eventually: Temporary or permanent blocks

Q2: Has Instagram changed its policy recently?

In recent periods, the platform has become:

More sensitive to repetitive behavior

Faster at triggering captchas

Stricter with follow/unfollow activity

So even if your setup worked before, it may now be considered too aggressive.

Q3: What settings should I change in JarveePro to avoid getting flagged?

Answer:

The most effective adjustment is to

lower your daily follow limits

Recommended actions:

Reduce daily follow count

Increase delay between actions

Avoid hitting maximum limits every day

Add more randomness to activity

The key idea:

Don’t operate at the edge of limits—stay comfortably below them.

Q4: What is a safe follow strategy?

A safe strategy focuses on consistency over volume:

Gradually increase activity instead of jumping to high limits

Keep daily actions moderate and stable

Allow “rest days” or lower activity periods

Monitor warnings and adjust immediately

Think of it as long-term account health, not short-term growth spikes.

Q5: Can I continue using automation safely?

Answer:

Yes, but only if used carefully.

Automation tools like JarveePro are effective when:

Limits are conservative

Behavior mimics real users

You respond quickly to warnings

Aggressive automation leads to flags. Controlled automation leads to sustainable growth.

Summary

Instagram flags are usually caused by

over-aggressive activity

, not account issues.

To stay safe:

Lower your daily follow limits

Add delays and randomness

Avoid hitting limits consistently

Adapt to Instagram’s evolving detection

Smart scaling always beats maximum pushing.

Sequential

No repetition happens

2026-04-05

Introduction

Social media trends are shifting fast—what worked a few months ago already feels outdated. Right now, platforms are pushing raw, short-form, personality-driven content, while quietly tightening detection on automation patterns.

In today’s Q&A, we’re focusing on real questions users are asking while trying to adapt JarveePro to these new trends—especially around AI content, “fake live” formats, and staying under the radar while scaling.

Q1: Can I automate “fake live / POV comment” style content with JarveePro?

Answer:

Yes—but not fully in the way most people expect.

JarveePro can handle the posting and scheduling side, but the

content itself

needs to feel spontaneous. If every post follows the same structure or timing, it kills the illusion.

Best approach:

Pre-create multiple variations of POV-style videos

Randomize captions using spintax

Schedule posts at irregular intervals

The automation should deliver the content—not expose the pattern behind it.

Q2: Is AI-generated content still safe to use at scale?

Yes, but raw AI content is getting easier to detect—especially when reused across accounts.

Platforms aren’t banning “AI,” they’re flagging repetition and unnatural consistency.

What works now:

Mix AI-generated drafts with human edits

Avoid posting identical scripts across accounts

Add imperfections (typos, pauses, varied tone)

Think of AI as a starting point, not the final product.

Q3: Why do my short-form videos get low reach even with consistent posting?

Answer:

Because consistency alone isn’t enough anymore—

hook quality

matters more.

Most low-reach issues come from:

Weak first 1–2 seconds

Repetitive formats

Overused templates

Fix:

Test multiple hooks for the same content

Rotate formats (don’t post the same style daily)

Space out similar posts to avoid pattern detection

Automation keeps you consistent—but creativity drives reach.

Q4: Can I repost the same viral content across multiple accounts safely?

Answer:

Not directly. That strategy used to work—it doesn’t anymore.

Platforms now compare content across accounts more aggressively.

Identical posts = higher risk of suppression or flags.

Safer method:

Slightly edit each video (zoom, crop, overlays)

Change captions using spintax

Stagger posting times across accounts

You’re not duplicating—you’re

distributing variations

Q5: How do I make automated activity look more “human” in 2026?

By breaking patterns, not just slowing things down.

Most users already add delays—but still get flagged because their behavior is too predictable.

What actually works:

Randomize action sequences (not just timing)

Avoid doing the same actions daily

Mix active days with low-activity days

Real users are inconsistent. Your automation should be too.

Q6: Should I still automate engagement (likes, follows, comments), or focus only on content?

Answer:

Content is now the primary growth driver—but engagement still plays a role if used carefully.

Aggressive engagement automation is one of the fastest ways to get flagged today.

Balanced strategy:

Keep engagement actions light and randomized

Focus more on posting high-performing content

Add manual interaction when possible

In 2026, content gets you reach—engagement supports credibility.

Q7: Why do some accounts grow fast while others stagnate with the same setup?

Because platforms now evaluate accounts individually, not just based on activity.

Two accounts using identical settings can perform completely differently due to:

Content quality

Account history

Audience response signals

Key insight:

Automation scales actions—but growth depends on how people react to your content.

Summary

The biggest shift right now is clear: automation alone isn’t enough.

Trends favor raw, unpredictable content

Platforms detect patterns faster than ever

Content quality now outweighs action volume

JarveePro is still a powerful tool—but the edge comes from how you combine automation with creativity and variation.

If you adapt to trends while keeping your setup flexible, you won’t just avoid problems—you’ll stay ahead of most users still relying on outdated strategies.

Moving to a new VPS doesn’t mean starting from scratch.

Scheduler Manager

Valid

The campaign dashboard will display a countdown

Important:

The system works on a

default 40-minute interval cycle

Q2: How do I check and manage scheduled campaigns?
