Scheduled (In 60m)

→ Campaign will run in approximately 60 minutes

Scheduled (Over 60m)

→ The campaign will run

in more than 60 minutes

This is normal behavior due to the scheduler’s 40-minute processing interval.

It does not mean the campaign failed.

“Over 60m” means:

The campaign will run

not

So:

In 60m

→ Campaign will run within the next 60 minutes

Over 60m

→ Campaign is scheduled, but execution is more than 60 minutes away

As long as the status in

Scheduler Manager shows “Valid”

, everything is working correctly.

No action is required.

Schedule status is

Valid

Enable Schedule is checked

2026-02-21

Introduction

Today’s Q&A covers three important operational topics for power users and agencies:

Filtering disabled accounts inside Content Explorer

Understanding how comment limits per run actually work

Clarifying the meaning of “Max Uses Per Item” in repost campaigns

If you’re running multiple VPS + Monitor setups, these settings matter more than you think.

Q1: Can you add a filter in Content Explorer to filter accounts by status (active, disabled, etc.) so we can remove disabled accounts from scraper results?

Answer:

Yes.

The requested filter for account status (Active / Disabled) has been added to Content Explorer.

This allows users to quickly filter and remove disabled accounts from scraped lists, improving data quality and reducing campaign waste.

Q2: Is “Max Uses Per Item” the number of times the repost source account can be used? If so, should it be set higher than 1? How does the program know to run just one post per run?

“Max Uses Per Item” refers to how many times a specific source item (such as a repost source post/account) can be used by the campaign.

If you set it to 1, the source will only be used once.

If you want it reused multiple times, you should increase that number.

As for how the program determines what to execute per run:

Execution behavior is automatic and based on campaign settings, limits, and available eligible items. The system processes what is allowed within the configured limits during each run cycle.

For more details about campaign settings:

http://blog.jarveepro.com/knowledge/JarveePro-Campaign-Settings/Shared-Campaign-Settings-Explained/5451

Q3: Is “Comments Allowed Per Post” a total lifetime limit or per-run limit?

Answer:

It functions per run, not as a permanent lifetime cap.

This means if you leave the tool running, it can provide that amount during each execution cycle unless additional limits are configured.

Q4: Why did one post receive all 9 comments in a single run? There is no limit per run setting.

The number of comments per run is calculated as:

Total Posts × Comments Per Post

If no stricter rate limits are applied, the system will execute everything allowed within the configured parameters in a single run.

There is no separate “comments per run” toggle — the output volume is determined by:

Number of target posts

Comments allowed per post

Account rate limits

Q5: How can I control comment volume more precisely?

Use the

Smart rate-limiting:

The system dynamically adjusts action frequency based on account age, trust score, and platform tolerance.

Behavior simulation:

Platform feedback signals:

If the platform shows early warning signs (such as reduced action acceptance or temporary limits), JarveePro automatically slows down execution to protect the account.

Concurrent module coordination:

When multiple automation modules run simultaneously, JarveePro intelligently distributes actions to maintain balance and safety.

This adaptive execution ensures long-term sustainability, which is far more valuable than short bursts of aggressive automation.

Q2: How to optimize campaign scheduling for maximum efficiency and safety?

Gradual warm-up:

New accounts should start with lower action limits and gradually increase activity over several days or weeks.

Peak activity targeting:

Module diversification:

Instead of relying on a single action type (such as follows), combine follows, likes, views, and engagement actions to create a balanced profile.

AI Monitor integration:

JarveePro’s AI Monitor can detect performance trends and automatically adjust campaign parameters for optimal results.

Consistent execution over bursts:

Steady, predictable activity produces stronger long-term growth compared to aggressive spikes.

This approach improves both performance efficiency and account safety, ensuring sustainable automation scaling.

Q1: Why are comments posting instantly without pauses between them?

Answer:

posting account level

, not at the

receiving post level

The

Wait Time setting applies to each posting account individually

If multiple accounts are assigned to the same campaign, each account can comment independently

This means several accounts can comment on the same receiving post almost simultaneously

The system does not currently enforce delays between comments on the same target post

As a result, even though individual accounts respect their own delay rules, the receiving post may still receive multiple comments in rapid succession.

Delay between actions performed by the

same account

Protection against excessive activity from a single account

Simulation of realistic user pacing at the account level

However, it does not control timing between actions targeting the same receiving post.

To address this limitation, JarveePro will introduce a new feature:

Wait Time Between Actions (Receiving-Level Delay)

This improvement will:

Apply delay between comments on the same receiving post

Prevent multiple comments from appearing instantly in sequence

Ensure comments are distributed over time more realistically

Improve behavioral simulation across AI Monitor and comment campaigns

Strengthen account safety by reducing detectable automation patterns

This feature adds a second timing control layer:

Account-level delay

→ protects posting accounts

Receiving-level delay

→ protects target posts and improves realism

Together, these layers create much more natural execution patterns.

2026-02-27

Introduction

Proxies are a foundational component of safe and scalable automation. However, proxy connectivity issues can sometimes occur even when proxies appear functional in external tools. These discrepancies are usually caused by protocol mismatches, authentication handling differences, or proxy type configuration errors.

JarveePro supports multiple proxy protocols, but correct configuration is essential for proper connectivity. Today’s Q&A addresses a common issue where residential proxies work in external testers but fail inside JarveePro.

Q1: Why does my proxy work in proxy testers but shows “This site can’t be reached” inside JarveePro?

Answer:

This issue is most commonly caused by selecting the wrong proxy protocol inside JarveePro.

In this case, the residential proxy from IPRoyal was initially configured using the wrong proxy type. While many proxy testers automatically detect or support multiple protocols, JarveePro requires the correct protocol to be selected manually.

The proxy was configured with:

Host: 193.228.193.86

Port: 12321

Residential session-based authentication

Username/password authorization

These types of residential proxies typically require

SOCKS5 protocol

, not HTTP or HTTPS.

When the proxy type is incorrectly set (for example, HTTP instead of SOCKS5), JarveePro cannot establish a connection, even though external proxy testers may still work.

This results in errors such as:

“This site can’t be reached”

Proxy unavailable

Connection timeout inside JarveePro

The proxy itself is functional — the issue is purely configuration-related.

Q2: How do I fix residential proxy connection issues in JarveePro?

Answer:

To resolve this issue, configure the proxy using the correct protocol and authentication settings.

Follow these steps:

Open Proxy Manager in JarveePro

Click Add Proxy

Enter the proxy details:

Host: 193.228.193.86

Port: 12321

Username: your proxy username

Password: your proxy password

Select Proxy Type: SOCKS5

Click OK

Click Verify Proxy Availability

Once SOCKS5 is selected, the proxy will connect successfully and show as Available.

SOCKS5 proxies provide:

Better compatibility with residential proxy providers

Improved connection stability

Proper authentication handling

Full support for session-based residential routing

This ensures JarveePro can properly route automation traffic through the proxy.

Summary

If a proxy works in external testers but fails in JarveePro, the most likely cause is an incorrect proxy type selection. Residential proxies, especially session-based ones from providers like IPRoyal, typically require SOCKS5 protocol.

By simply changing the proxy type to SOCKS5 in JarveePro’s Proxy Manager, the connection issue can be resolved immediately. Proper proxy configuration ensures stable connectivity, safer automation, and reliable campaign execution.

text:
JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary – March 17, 2026 | Why JarveePro Shows “Invalid Serial Number” and Why Campaigns May Disappear

2026-03-17

Introduction

Running automation software like

JarveePro

usually works smoothly once everything is set up correctly. However, occasional server changes, license synchronization issues, or local file problems can trigger confusing errors such as

“Invalid Serial Number”

or even make campaigns appear to disappear.

This Q&A diary from a real support interaction highlights some common causes behind these issues—such as server restarts, license expiration timing, disk space limitations, and accidental deletion of local files. Understanding these factors can help users quickly troubleshoot and prevent future disruptions in their automation workflow.

Q1: Why does JarveePro show an “Invalid Serial Number” error after restarting the server?

Answer:

This error often appears when the

device ID associated with the license changes

. A server restart, VM reset, or hardware change can trigger JarveePro to detect the machine as a different device. When that happens, the system temporarily treats the license as invalid until the device ID is reset on the licensing server.

In most cases, support simply needs to

reset the device ID linked to the serial number

, allowing the same license to work again on the restarted server.

Q2: Will resetting the device ID delete accounts or campaigns in JarveePro?

No. Resetting the device ID only affects the

license authentication

, not the local automation data.

Accounts, campaigns, and settings are stored in the

local JarveePro data files on your pc

, not in the license system. As long as those files remain intact, all campaigns should remain available after the license is reset.

Q3: Why did the license appear expired even though the user upgraded earlier?

Answer:

When a license is upgraded, the

billing cycle usually continues from the original subscription date

, not the upgrade date.

For example:

Original subscription date: March 13

Upgrade on: March 17

The system still calculates the expiration based on

March 13

, because the upgrade simply adjusts the plan level rather than resetting the billing cycle.

Q4: After renewing the license, can users log in immediately with the same serial number?

Yes. Once payment is successfully processed, the

same serial number can normally be used right away

The system automatically updates the license status, allowing users to log in without waiting for a new serial number—provided the device ID remains the same.

Q5: Why did the campaigns disappear after the system started working again?

Answer:

If campaigns disappear, the most common causes include:

Local file deletion

– Campaign data is stored in local directories. Removing those folders can erase the campaign configuration.

Server disk cleanup

– When a server runs out of space, users sometimes delete files to free storage and accidentally remove JarveePro data folders.

Corrupted or missing data files

– If critical files inside the JarveePro installation directory are removed or overwritten, campaigns may no longer load.

In this situation, the system showed that

the server had no remaining disk space

, and files had been deleted. That likely removed some campaign data files.

Q6: Where are JarveePro campaigns stored?

Campaigns are saved

locally within the JarveePro installation data folders

This means:

The campaigns are

not stored in the license system

If files are deleted or the server is reset without backup, campaigns may disappear

Regular

backups of the JarveePro data folder

are highly recommended

Summary

The issues in this case were caused by a combination of

server restart, license expiration timing, and local file deletion due to storage limitations

The key lessons for JarveePro users are:

Server restarts can change device IDs and trigger license validation errors

License upgrades do not reset billing cycles

Campaigns are stored locally, so deleting files or clearing disk space can remove them

Regular backups and adequate server storage help prevent data loss

By keeping these best practices in mind, users can ensure their

JarveePro automation campaigns remain stable and protected

even when server changes occur.

Q1: I set “Posts Allowed per Account” to 7 to 7, but all 7 posts upload at once. How do I post one per day?

The “7 to 7” setting is designed for bulk execution and will post all selected content immediately.

To post one item per day, use scheduler to stop it after 1 time, which ensures only one post is executed per scheduled run.

Q2: I use the “1 to 1” setting. The first post uploads fine, but subsequent scheduled runs don’t post anything. What am I missing?

This happens because the

scheduler is not correctly configured for repeated execution

Steps to fix:

Go to

Campaign Manager → Scheduler

Set the

Schedule Type

to

“Number of Runs”

Example for 7-day sequential posting:

Start Time: Today at 12:02 p'm

Interval: 1 day

Total Runs: 7

Make sure

“Remaining Number”

allows all 7 scheduled runs.

In

Content Selection

, choose

“Pick Next Post Automatically”

so each run selects a new item from your preloaded list.

Avoid manually starting or stopping the campaign outside the scheduler.

For testing, you can temporarily shorten the interval (e.g., 1 hour) to verify sequential posting, then restore it to 24 hours.

Q3: Can I combine multiple posts and have them post sequentially automatically?

Yes. Preload multiple images and texts, set Times

Allowed per Photo/Video

to

1 to 1

, and configure the scheduler as described above.

The scheduler will automatically pick the next queued post for each scheduled run.

Reference: Go to

JarveePro Campaign Settings Explained: Account Delay, Action Delay and Scheduler

Summary:

Use

“1 to 1” posts per account

for sequential posting.

Configure the

Scheduler → Number of Runs

to cover the full posting period.

JarveePro allows users to manage multiple Instagram accounts through its centralized dashboard. Each account can be configured with its own activity limits, proxy settings, and automation schedules.

Assign a dedicated proxy to each account

Set realistic activity limits for actions such as likes, follows, and comments

If your Instagram actions in JarveePro appear to be running slower than expected, it is usually related to the safety settings designed to protect accounts from triggering platform limits.

JarveePro allows users to configure delays between actions such as likes, follows, and comments. If the delay range is set too high, actions will naturally run more slowly.

3. Proxy Performance

Slow or unstable proxies can also affect automation speed. If proxies are overloaded or have high latency, actions may take longer to complete.

4. Account Warm-up

Newly added accounts may operate at lower speeds during the warm-up period to prevent triggering security checks from the platform.

To improve performance, users should review their delay settings, check proxy quality, and ensure their accounts have completed the warm-up phase.

Introduction

One thing I love about these daily Q&A conversations is they reveal what’s really on marketers’ minds — not theory, not hype, but the practical questions people are asking before they scale.

And lately, a pattern keeps showing up: users are less interested in “can automation do X?” and much more interested in

how to do it safely, at volume, and still get results.

Today’s question came from a Facebook marketer asking something a lot of people quietly wonder:

Does Facebook automation still work in 2026 — especially for actions like adding friends from ID lists at controlled daily limits?

Short answer: yes — but the strategy around it matters far more than the action itself.

Let’s break it down.

Q1: Is your Facebook automation still working?

Answer:

Yes — Facebook automation still works in 2026, but the old “blast actions at maximum speed” mindset is what stopped working.

That’s the big difference.

Modern Facebook automation is much more about

behavior simulation, pacing, and account trust management

than brute-force activity.

Inside JarveePro, Facebook automation is commonly used for:

Controlled friend requests

Audience expansion from targeted user IDs

Engagement workflows

Content distribution support

Account warm-up sequences

Multi-account management

The goal isn’t “do more actions.”

It’s

do believable actions consistently.

That’s why experienced users focus on:

1. Gradual action limits

Instead of aggressive volume, they use progressive limits.

Example:

Week 1: 5–10 requests daily

Week 2: 10–15 daily

Week 3: 15–20 daily

This warming approach often matters more than the automation itself.

2. Quality targeting over quantity

A list of IDs can work well — if those IDs are relevant.

A tight, responsive audience often outperforms large random targeting.

Good automation amplifies targeting.

Bad targeting just automates waste.

3. Account trust first

In 2026, account reputation is an asset.

Aged accounts, warmed profiles, healthy engagement signals — these matter.

Automation works better when it supports trust instead of pushing against it.

That’s why people using JarveePro successfully usually treat automation as infrastructure, not a shortcut.

Q2: I have a list of IDs and would like to request 20/day — is that reasonable?

Answer:

For many warmed accounts,

20 friend requests per day

can be a conservative and workable range.

And honestly, this question reflects something smart:

You’re talking about controlled volume, not reckless scale.

That’s usually the right mindset.

Why 20/day often makes sense

At that pace you can:

Stay moderate

Test acceptance rates

Adjust based on response

Avoid unnatural spikes

Scale methodically

It’s boring.

And boring is often what works.

Better approach than jumping straight to 20

Many advanced users would still phase into it:

Start 8–10/day

Move to 15/day

Then stabilize at 20/day

That gives the account time to build rhythm.

Think less “launch campaign.”

More “condition system.”

Huge difference.

Even better: watch acceptance ratio

This is underrated.

Don’t just track how many requests you send.

Track:

Accepted requests

Pending requests

Declines

Response rate by audience segment

Because if 10 targeted requests outperform 20 weak ones…

20 isn’t actually the win.

Precision is.

What This Question Really Tells Us About the Market

Interesting thing about questions like this:

People are no longer asking whether automation exists.

They’re asking whether it can be deployed safely and predictably.

That’s a maturity shift.

The market has moved from:

“Can tools automate actions?”

to

“How do I build scalable operating systems with automation?”

That’s a much bigger conversation.

And frankly, that’s where tools like JarveePro fit best.

Summary

Today’s takeaway is simple:

Yes, Facebook automation still works in 2026.

But what works now is structured automation:

gradual limits

trust-based account warming

quality targeting

measured scaling

behavior that looks natural

And for friend requests from ID lists,

20/day can be reasonable

, especially when phased in thoughtfully.

The old automation game was speed.

The new automation game is controlled systems.

That’s a better game.

Introduction

As more developers integrate directly with

JarveePro

“Why does API behavior feel different from the desktop interface?”

This question came up during a detailed technical discussion with a developer exploring how JarveePro handles browser concurrency, task execution, and runtime control across different API surfaces.

What started as a simple question about browser launch timing quickly evolved into a deeper conversation about something many advanced users have noticed:

JarveePro currently exposes two distinct operational task systems — one tightly connected to the desktop interface, and another designed specifically for standalone API automation.

If you are building custom automation systems, external dashboards, or multi-account orchestration tools on top of JarveePro, this Q&A will help clarify how these systems behave and why some API tasks do not follow interface-level execution rules.

Q1. Does the JarveePro API automatically follow dashboard settings like “Max Threads” or browser staggering?

Answer

Not always — and this depends on which API task system you are using.

The developer noticed that when sending API requests for Instagram commenting tasks across multiple accounts, JarveePro attempted to launch all browser instances simultaneously.

For example:

10 accounts → 10 browsers launched immediately

20 accounts → 20 browsers launched immediately

Settings such as:

Max Threads

Browser staggering

Browser overlap prevention

appeared to be ignored.

Initially, this seemed like a bug.

However, after clarification from the JarveePro team, the behavior was confirmed as expected for API-native task types.

The key distinction is:

Interface-linked tasks

These are coupled to the JarveePro desktop UI and generally respect interface runtime settings.

API-native tasks

These operate independently from the interface and must be controlled entirely through API logic.

This means developers are responsible for:

concurrency control

browser launch timing

batching

queue management

stagger logic

inside their own applications.

The only interface-related setting still observed affecting execution was:

max browser per row

which is tied to browser window rendering rather than task scheduling.

Q2. Why do the official API documentation and Instagram Comment example use completely different structures?

Answer

This was one of the most interesting discoveries in the discussion.

The developer identified that the official documentation and the Instagram Comment example appear to expose two parallel API architectures.

and more.

This architecture behaves much closer to how the desktop interface manages automation internally.

Q3. Which API system respects JarveePro desktop runtime settings?

Answer

MainTask / interface-linked systems

These generally inherit desktop runtime behavior, including:

concurrent browser limits

browser staggering

browser positioning

account pairing logic

API-native task systems

These are intentionally decoupled from the interface.

They do not inherit interface execution management automatically.

Instead, they are designed for external orchestration where developers fully manage execution behavior themselves.

This separation exists because JarveePro’s long-term API direction focuses on making platform functionality independently accessible outside the desktop environment.

Q4. Can API-native tasks be viewed or modified from the JarveePro interface?

Answer

No.

JarveePro clarified that API-native task types:

are not controlled through the desktop UI

cannot be edited from the interface

are managed entirely through API endpoints

Their parameters and runtime behavior exist independently from interface-managed tasks.

Meanwhile, interface-linked task types are specifically designed to bridge UI workflows with API control.

Summary

This discussion revealed something many advanced JarveePro developers suspected but had not fully confirmed:

JarveePro currently operates with two parallel automation architectures.

One is tightly connected to the desktop interface and inherits interface execution behavior.

The other is API-native and intentionally decoupled for independent orchestration.

For developers building scalable automation systems, understanding this distinction is critical because it directly affects:

runtime control

As JarveePro’s API ecosystem continues evolving, clearer examples and expanded documentation across platforms will likely become one of the most requested resources from advanced users.

Introduction

Modern social media automation is no longer just about posting content or managing accounts.

discovering active audiences

identifying high-performing content

analyzing engagement behavior

collecting creator and follower data

As platforms like Instagram and TikTok continue tightening API access and privacy protections, many users now ask an important question:

What type of data can automation platforms realistically collect today?

JarveePro

includes multiple built-in data collection systems designed to help users gather public engagement signals, creator information, audience activity, and content performance metrics across supported platforms.

This article explains how JarveePro handles data collection, audience scraping, filtering systems, and demographic limitations in modern social media environments.

Q1. Does JarveePro include built-in data collection features?

Answer

Yes.

JarveePro includes built-in data collection capabilities through several automation and discovery modules, including:

JarveePro Advanced Content Explorer

These systems are designed to help users collect publicly accessible social media data from supported platforms.

Depending on the platform and workflow, JarveePro can gather:

public audience data

hashtag-related content

interaction signals

Q2. Does JarveePro support data filtering?

Yes.

JarveePro supports multiple forms of filtering for collected social media data.

The filtering system is primarily focused on engagement and content intelligence rather than private demographic profiling.

Q3. Can JarveePro filter audiences by age or gender?

No.

JarveePro does not currently include native age or gender filtering as a standard platform feature.

API limitations

As a result, most modern automation systems now prioritize behavioral analysis rather than direct demographic extraction.

This means JarveePro focuses more heavily on:

engagement behavior

interaction patterns

content affinity

audience activity

rather than attempting to provide direct demographic profiling.

Q4. What types of filtering are most commonly used in modern automation systems?

Modern automation systems increasingly prioritize behavioral targeting over demographic targeting.

In practice, marketers often achieve stronger targeting results by analyzing:

what users engage with

which creators they follow

how frequently they interact

what type of content performs well

rather than relying solely on estimated age or gender categories.

JarveePro’s filtering systems are designed around these engagement-based workflows.

This style of filtering is especially useful for identifying:

age

Yes.

Custom feature development is possible for specialized workflows.

However, these systems are significantly more complex in 2026 than traditional scraping tools from previous years.

Modern demographic estimation often requires combinations of:

Because of this complexity, custom demographic-related systems typically require dedicated development resources and platform-specific adaptation.

Q7. Why is behavioral targeting becoming more important than demographic targeting?

Answer

This reflects one of the largest shifts currently happening in social media marketing.

Platforms are increasingly moving away from exposing direct user identity information.

At the same time, engagement behavior has become a stronger predictor of audience intent.

For example:

A user consistently engaging with fitness creators may provide more actionable marketing value than simply labeling the user by age or gender category.

As a result, modern automation and intelligence systems increasingly focus on:

engagement behavior

interaction frequency

content affinity

niche participation

instead of relying primarily on demographic assumptions.

This transition is reshaping how modern social media growth systems operate across platforms like Instagram and TikTok.

Summary

Filtering systems primarily focus on behavioral and engagement intelligence rather than direct demographic classification.

While native age and gender filtering are not currently included as standard features, custom development may be possible depending on the platform and project requirements.

As social platforms continue increasing privacy protections in 2026, engagement-based intelligence is becoming more valuable than traditional demographic scraping alone.

Introduction

One of the most common situations new users experience when starting TikTok automation is assuming the platform should instantly behave exactly like demo videos or older automation tools.

In reality, TikTok’s security system in 2026 has become far more aggressive toward automation activity, especially on fresh accounts, untrusted browser environments, unstable IP setups, or incorrectly configured campaigns.

Continuous captcha requests

Browsers not opening in parallel

Accounts randomly getting logged out

Follow campaigns not executing properly

Differences between demo environments and real-world setups

Most importantly, this article explains why proper configuration matters before evaluating automation performance.

Q1. Is It Normal That TikTok Shows Captcha Frequently During Campaigns?

Yes — especially on newer accounts or improperly configured setups.

TikTok now aggressively challenges automation behavior through:

Captcha verification

Device trust validation

Behavioral scoring

Session integrity checks

Browser fingerprint analysis

IP reputation monitoring

Captcha frequency usually increases when:

Accounts are newly created

Accounts are not warmed up properly

Proxy quality is poor

No captcha-solving API is configured

Action speed is too aggressive

Too many actions happen simultaneously

Fingerprints are unstable between sessions

JarveePro supports captcha-solving integrations, but users must manually configure captcha API keys inside the platform settings.

Without a configured captcha-solving provider, manual captcha interruptions are expected.

Q2. Why Do Browsers Open One by One Instead of In Parallel?

This is usually related to thread settings.

Many users expect all browser profiles to launch simultaneously immediately after importing accounts, but JarveePro uses controlled threading to improve stability and reduce detection risk.

If browsers open sequentially, users should review:

Thread configuration

Campaign concurrency settings

Device resource limitations

CPU/RAM availability

Browser launch delay settings

Running too many browsers in parallel without proper hardware resources can cause:

Session corruption

Account instability

Increased captcha frequency

Browser crashes

Failed actions

Parallel launching shown in demonstration videos may differ depending on:

Hardware performance

Campaign configuration

Proxy quality

Number of accounts

Fingerprint complexity

Q3. Why Are Accounts Getting Logged Out Randomly?

Unexpected logout behavior is usually caused by trust-related issues rather than software malfunction.

Common causes include:

Low-quality proxies

Rotating residential IP instability

Shared datacenter proxies

Frequent IP switching

Browser fingerprint inconsistency

Login from multiple environments

Aggressive automation behavior

Fresh accounts without warm-up history

TikTok constantly evaluates whether an account session appears trustworthy.

If the platform detects unusual behavior patterns, it may:

Force re-login

Trigger security verification

Show captchas

Temporarily restrict actions

Invalidate sessions

This behavior is now common across most automation environments, not only JarveePro.

Q4. Why Is the Follow Campaign Not Following Properly?

In most cases, follow campaign issues are caused by campaign configuration mistakes rather than campaign failure.

Users should verify:

Source accounts are valid

Enough targets are added

Daily limits are realistic

Delays are configured properly

Accounts are warmed up

Follow limits are not exceeded

Campaign execution logic is understood correctly

A common beginner misunderstanding is expecting continuous nonstop actions immediately after starting campaigns.

JarveePro campaigns operate using:

Execution intervals

Delay scheduling

Safe pacing logic

Internal queue systems

Account protection logic

Improper expectations often lead users to believe campaigns are “not working” when the system is actually waiting for the next safe execution cycle.

Q5. Why Does TikTok Behave Differently Compared to Other Browsers Like Multilogin?

TikTok’s detection systems continuously evolve.

Different browsers, fingerprints, proxies, account histories, and automation patterns can produce different results across environments.

Even if another browser environment previously showed fewer captcha requests, results may change over time because TikTok updates:

Device fingerprint detection

Browser telemetry analysis

Behavioral AI systems

Session trust scoring

Proxy intelligence systems

Automation stability depends heavily on the complete environment, not only the browser itself.

This includes:

Proxy quality

Account age

Warm-up strategy

Session consistency

Action speed

Device stability

Browser configuration

Q6. Why Does JarveePro Recommend Reading Campaign Settings Documentation First?

Because most beginner issues are configuration-related.

Many reported “platform problems” are actually caused by:

Incorrect delay settings

Unrealistic action limits

Missing captcha integrations

Weak proxies

The campaign settings documentation explains:

Users who skip these concepts often misinterpret normal automation behavior as malfunction.

Q7. What Is the Best Way to Stabilize TikTok Automation in JarveePro?

Recommended best practices include:

Use high-quality stable proxies

Warm accounts slowly

Avoid aggressive action limits

Configure captcha-solving APIs

Use realistic delays

Avoid running too many accounts simultaneously

TikTok automation in 2026 is no longer about “maximum speed.”

It is about maintaining long-term account trust.

Summary

Most TikTok automation issues reported by new users are related to setup quality, account trust, proxy stability, and misunderstanding of campaign execution behavior.

Captcha requests, sequential browser launches, temporary follow delays, and account logouts are usually symptoms of environmental configuration issues rather than platform failure.

JarveePro is designed for scalable long-term automation, but success depends heavily on:

JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary – May 16, 2026 | JarveePro Facebook Message Campaign

2026-05-16

Introduction

One of the most common questions from new JarveePro users involves message campaign limits and account behavior during automation runs. Users often expect a single account to continuously message dozens of profile links without interruption, but campaign settings and account allocation rules can affect how many messages are actually sent.

In today’s JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary, we explain why a campaign stopped after only sending 3 messages and how the “Times Allowed Per Message By Account” setting works.

Q1: Why Did JarveePro Only Send 3 Messages Out of 35 Profile Links?

A user reported that their campaign successfully started, but only 3 messages were sent before the task completed.

Answer

This usually happens because of campaign configuration limits rather than a software error.

In this case:

The user had only:

1 account

1 message text

A list of 35–50 profile links

JarveePro distributes messages based on the settings configured inside the campaign. If the limits are too restrictive, the task may complete early after only a few successful sends.

The first thing users should check is:

Daily sending limits

Account allocation settings

Message rotation rules

“Times Allowed Per Message By Account”

Once the settings were adjusted, the campaign behavior changed correctly.

Q2: What Does “Times Allowed Per Message By Account” Mean?

The user mentioned that this section was not clearly explained in the knowledge base.

Answer

“Times Allowed Per Message By Account” controls how many times a specific message variation can be used by a single account.

For example:

If set too low, JarveePro may stop after sending only a few messages

If using:

1 account

1 message variation

50 profile links

then the limit should generally allow the message to be reused enough times to cover the target list.

In this support conversation, the recommendation was:

Set the value higher

Or configure it as 50–50 for the single account/message setup

This allows the same message template to be reused across the full profile list.

Q3: Should Users Upgrade Plans for Larger Messaging Campaigns?

The user was operating on the Individual Plan with only one account connected.

Answer

While the Individual Plan can handle smaller campaigns, larger outreach operations benefit from additional account capacity.

For users planning to:

Scale outreach

Rotate multiple message templates

Reduce account limitations

Increase campaign flexibility

JarveePro recommends:

Business Version (30 accounts)

Enterprise Version (Unlimited accounts)

Having multiple accounts provides:

Better distribution

Higher sending flexibility

Reduced limitation bottlenecks

More scalable automation workflows

Summary

If JarveePro only sends a few messages before completing a task, the issue is often related to campaign configuration rather than a system malfunction. Settings such as “Times Allowed Per Message By Account” directly affect how many times a message can be reused by an account.

For users running larger campaigns with only one account and one message variation, increasing the allowed usage value is essential for completing the full target list successfully.

As campaigns grow larger, upgrading to Business or Enterprise plans can significantly improve scalability and workflow efficiency.

2026-05-29

Introduction

When running JarveePro in advanced VPS or virtual machine (VM) environments, users may encounter situations where tasks are executed successfully, but the dashboard shows zero results or failed logs. This is usually not a task execution issue, but a configuration and environment visibility issue related to how virtual machines handle session rendering, tracking, and cache storage.

This guide explains the most common causes and solutions for VPS/VM deployment issues, including rendering mode, task logging discrepancies, and cache accumulation management.

Q 1: Why are tasks (such as story views) showing “0 success” even though they are actually running on VPS/VM?

Answer:

This issue typically occurs when the virtual machine is running in a

non-rendered or background (silent) session mode

In this mode:

The VM executes automation tasks in the background

However, there is no active graphical session (no visible browser rendering layer)

JarveePro cannot fully confirm UI-level completion events (such as story views being registered)

As a result:

Tasks may still be executed correctly

But the system cannot record or validate them as successful actions

This leads to “0 success” or missing analytics data in the dashboard

Recommended Fix:

Ensure each VM session is running in an

active connected desktop session

Avoid fully headless or silent execution modes for engagement-based actions

Verify that the VM has an active graphical environment (not background-only execution)

Q 2: Do VPS/VM deployments require manual cache management, and why is cache growing so large?

Answer:

Yes. In long-running VPS or VM deployments, cache accumulation is expected and must be actively managed.

JarveePro generates cache data such as:

Session data

Browser rendering cache

Temporary automation files

Profile and login state storage

Over time, this data can accumulate significantly (e.g., 40GB+), which may cause:

Reduced system performance

Disk space exhaustion

Task instability or intermittent logging issues

File locking conflicts during runtime cleanup

Recommended Fix:

Implement a

regular cache cleanup schedule

Do not clear cache while tasks are actively running

Pause automation before performing cleanup operations

Summary

JarveePro VPS/VM deployments are fully capable of running large-scale automation, but proper environment configuration is essential for accurate tracking and stable performance.

Two key factors must be addressed:

Rendering session visibility

— ensures task success is properly recorded

Cache lifecycle management

— prevents performance degradation over time

When both are correctly configured, JarveePro can reliably execute and log automation tasks across multi-VM infrastructures without discrepancies.

JarveePro engages users on social platforms

Developer API sends structured lead data to the CRM

CRM stores the lead and triggers follow-up automation

Engagement behavior

Without the Developer API:

External CRM integration is not available

API-level activation and configuration

JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary – Nov. 3rd, 2025(Instagram vs. Facebook – Which Gets Banned Faster and Why?)

2025-11-03

Introduction

Many JarveePro users often ask which platform is stricter when it comes to automation safety — Instagram or Facebook. Both are owned by Meta, but their detection systems, action limits, and verification methods work very differently.

This article breaks down that comparison in a simple Q&A format, showing which platform reacts faster to aggressive automation and how you can keep your accounts safe while scaling your activity.

Q1: Which platform gets banned faster — Instagram or Facebook?

Answer:

Instagram generally bans or limits accounts faster than Facebook when users perform high-frequency actions such as mass follows, direct messages, or likes. Its detection system is highly sensitive to repetitive behavior patterns.

Facebook, on the other hand, focuses more on content moderation than speed-based activity detection. It still enforces limits, but you can usually perform moderate automation tasks like scheduled posting, page management, or joining groups with fewer restrictions.

Q2: Why does Instagram ban accounts faster?

Instagram’s infrastructure was designed around fast, repetitive engagement — which means it has more advanced spam detection built in.

Here are the main reasons:

Stricter rate limits:

Instagram monitors per-hour and per-day actions closely. Performing too many similar actions quickly (like follows or messages) easily triggers blocks.

Pattern tracking:

Repeating identical actions — same messages, same timing, or same type of engagement — sends clear bot signals.

Identity verification:

Instagram relies heavily on selfie or video verification when it suspects non-human behavior.

Device sensitivity:

As a mobile-first app, Instagram checks device IDs, IPs, and geolocation data constantly to detect suspicious activity.

Because of these systems, even experienced marketers notice that Instagram reacts faster to automation compared to Facebook.

Q3: What actions are most likely to trigger bans?

Answer:

On Instagram, mass-following, unfollowing, or sending a large number of direct messages in a short time can quickly lead to action blocks.

Facebook’s most sensitive areas include posting to too many groups too quickly or leaving repetitive comments that look automated.

The more identical and frequent your actions appear, the faster the system identifies them as unnatural. Always focus on variation and timing control — this is exactly what JarveePro’s scheduling system was designed to manage intelligently.

Q4: How can I reduce the risk of getting banned while using JarveePro?

Start slowly. If you are using new or recently warmed-up accounts, limit daily actions and build up gradually. Avoid large spikes or sudden activity bursts.

Here are a few key principles to follow:

Keep your daily follows and unfollows moderate.

Send fewer direct messages and always use

Spintax

to make your messages unique.

Space out your actions naturally using

JarveePro’s random delay options

Focus on realistic timing that mimics real human behavior.

When used properly, the JarveePro Scheduler helps you balance productivity and safety by managing all timing loops, pauses, and randomized delays automatically.

Q5: Can I use cracked or brute accounts to reduce the risk?

Answer:

No — and it’s important to be clear on this. Using or purchasing “cracked” or “brute” accounts is illegal, unsafe, and against Meta’s policies. Those accounts are often already flagged, and connecting them to your main network can lead to instant bans or even IP/device blacklisting.

JarveePro is built for legal, ethical automation that helps users scale real marketing operations safely. Always use verified and legitimate accounts for automation.

Q6: What’s the safest way to automate across multiple platforms?

Always warm up accounts first, use strong IP or proxy separation, and never rush high-volume actions on fresh profiles.

Enable

Safe Mode

for sensitive actions like following, messaging, or commenting. Add random delays between actions.

And most importantly, monitor your performance logs — when you see a warning or temporary block, pause the automation for that account before continuing.

2025-10-13

Every day, JarveePro users send in questions about automation logic, AI integration, and account behavior. Below are some of the top discussions from today’s support team exchange and expert responses.

Question 1:

Can a dedicated residential IP be used for 1 Facebook account, 1 Instagram account, and one X (Twitter) account?

Answer:

Yes, you

can

technically use one dedicated residential IP for one Facebook, one Instagram, and one X account —

if they all belong to the same person or brand entity

However, here’s what you should keep in mind:

Consistency:

Facebook and Instagram are both Meta products. Using the same IP for both is normal and safe if they represent the same identity or business.

Cross-platform behavior:

X (Twitter) has a different ownership and detection system. If too many login patterns overlap (e.g., identical device fingerprint + same IP used for unrelated accounts), it may trigger a flag on one of the platforms.

Best Practice:

Assign

1 residential IP per entity (brand or person)

rather than per platform.

Keep

consistent time zones and device types

across logins.

Use

JarveePro Account Manager

to isolate browser fingerprints for each account group.

Question 2:

Explain to me about the AI Agent and what difference it has with the Monitor?

Answer:

This is one of the most common confusions — both

AI Agent

and

Monitor

are automation layers, but they serve different roles:

Feature

Purpose

Executes intelligent actions such as replying, commenting, or posting with natural language understanding.

Observes user activity, post feeds, or inboxes to detect changes, new messages, or mentions.

Core Function

Acts like an

AI virtual assistant

— it can think, generate, and respond.

Acts like a

watchdog

— it only detects and triggers conditions.

Technology

Built on ChatGPT + JarveePro AI logic to understand context and sentiment.

Uses rule-based scanning and triggers (no NLP involved).

Example Use

AI Agent replies to comments using spintax and GPT-generated responses.

Monitor detects when a new comment appears and triggers the AI Agent.

Automation Chain

Monitor → AI Agent → Execution

Monitor only detects

In short:

The

Monitor

is your “sensor,” while the

AI Agent

is your “brain and hands.”

You can think of it as:

Monitor detects → AI Agent decides → JarveePro executes.

Question 3:

I'm trying to make a comment campaign with AI and ChatGPT but it doesn’t execute. This error comes out: “The content explorer doesn’t work well. I import a contact and it doesn’t create the account login box.”

Answer:

This problem usually means your

account hasn’t been logged in through the “Account Login” process

— so JarveePro can’t verify the account session for the AI to perform actions.

Here’s how to fix it

Correct Steps to Fix the Issue:

Step

Action

Description

Accounts

Account Login

button at the top right.

Normal

, rebind it to your campaign and re-run.

Always confirm the green “Normal” status before launching any AI-driven campaign (Comment, Like, or Message).

Q1: About the red circle setting

“I thought it was for specifying ranges like 1–400 in the list, but it seems different. What does it actually mean?”

A1:

This setting defines

how many total likes each account will execute

. For example, if it’s set to 4000, every account you run will attempt up to 4000 likes. It’s not a “list selector,” it’s an

action quota

Insight:

Many beginners confuse quotas with ranges. The difference matters: quotas help you control

account health & scaling strategy

, while ranges are more about

target segmentation

. Knowing this prevents account bans and helps you push accounts longer without hitting limits.

Q2: From Manila, PH – why does Facebook kill my accounts after registration?

“Even with PH proxies, antidetect browsers, and using GMX/Mail.com emails, Facebook always asks me to confirm captcha, then video selfie, and eventually disables the account.”

A2:

This isn’t just your setup — it’s part of

Facebook’s new defense layer in SEA regions

. Here’s the deeper issue:

IP Trust Score

– Facebook scores IP ranges, not just the fact that it’s “Philippines.” Datacenter proxies and reused IP pools are

already flagged

Email Trust Level

– GMX/Mail.com are public burner domains. Facebook has years of data linking them to automation. That’s why you get extra checks.

Biometric Enforcement

– In PH/India/Indonesia, Facebook increasingly demands video selfies. It’s their strongest anti-fake-account filter right now.

Behavioral Red Flags

– Fresh accounts that immediately try to log in through proxies or automation look like

bot farms

to FB.

The problem isn’t just the captcha. The real game is

building account credibility from Day 1

. If you can’t bypass the “newborn account trap,” no amount of proxies will save you.

JarveePro Tip:

Use

mobile 4G/5G residential proxies

tied to real carrier IPs.

Start with

domain-based or aged emails

instead of GMX/Mail.com.

Spend 2–3 days “warming up” accounts in JarveePro’s antidetect browser: watch reels, scroll, like random content — before attempting registration or linking to automation.

Diversify: don’t try to farm all accounts locally; mix in

aged/marketplace accounts

for scale.

Why This Matters:

If you’re building accounts in PH and they keep dying, you’re losing money and time. But with the

right setup + JarveePro warm-up workflow

, you can cut loss rates by 60–70% and actually scale campaigns without hitting the selfie wall every time.

Action Quotas vs. Ranges:

Learn that quota settings (e.g., 4000 likes per account) control activity limits to protect account health, unlike target ranges. Proper use prevents premature blocks and supports long-term scaling.

Facebook Account Trust in PH:

Public email domains, flagged datacenter IPs, and immediate automation trigger Facebook’s strongest verification steps, including captchas and video selfies.

Safe Scaling Practices:

Use mobile 4G/5G residential proxies, aged/domain-based emails, and a 2–3 day warm-up period in JarveePro’s antidetect browser. Diversify account sources and actions to maximize survival rates.

Effective quota management combined with trust-building workflows can reduce account losses by 60–70%, turning what would be a high-risk campaign into a sustainable operation.

Ecosystem-level integrations

interfaces

Instagram automation sounds simple on the surface — add an account, turn on follow, watch the numbers grow. In reality, most problems users face with Instagram automation in 2025 are not software issues, but configuration mistakes, skipped steps, or unrealistic expectations. This Daily Q&A Diary addresses the most common questions we receive about connecting Instagram accounts to JarveePro, running automation on private profiles, setting safe daily limits, and understanding why actions sometimes don’t start. Q1: I logged in, added my Instagram account, but I don’t know if it’s really connected. Did it work?

Answer:

Adding an account is

not the same as starting it

After adding your Instagram account:

Go to Accounts

→ Instagram

Select the account (checkbox on the left)

Click

Start

If the status changes from

Unknown

to

Running

, the account is connected correctly.

If you don’t click

, nothing will run.

JarveePro will not auto-start accounts for safety reasons.

Answer:

To connect safely and avoid blocks:

Use a

dedicated proxy

(1 proxy = 1 IG account)

Add your account under

Accounts

→ Instagram

Start

to initialize login

If Instagram challenges the login, JarveePro will show it clearly in the account status.

Short answer:

Yes — but

with limits

What works on private accounts:

Follow users (they receive follow requests)

Like posts (from public profiles)

Warm-up actions

What does NOT magically change:

Private accounts grow

slower

Users must manually approve follow requests

Expect lower acceptance rates than public accounts

This is an Instagram limitation, not a JarveePro limitation.

Answer:

This is already built into JarveePro — and yes, the format is shown directly in the UI.

Best-practice setup:

Enable

Follow

Unfollow after X days

Set

daily limits conservatively

Do

NOT

Follow too fast

Unfollow immediately

Stack too many actions on a fresh account

JarveePro gives you the tools. Safety comes from

how you configure them

Q5: What are the safest limits to avoid Instagram blocks?

Recommended starter limits (new or private account):

Follows: 20–40/day

Likes: 50–80/day

Unfollows: after 3–7 days

Actions spread across the day (no bursts)

🚫 Do not run automation immediately after login

🚫 Do not copy aggressive settings from old YouTube videos

Instagram in 2025 ≠ Instagram in 2019.

Check how to set your accounts rate limits here:

https://blog.jarveepro.com/knowledge/JarveePro-3-Update/JarveePro-Rate-Limits-Avoid-Bans-with-Safe-Daily-Activity/5521

Q6: I followed the steps, but nothing is happening

Checklist before opening a ticket:

Account is

Started

Status is

Running

Actions are enabled

Daily limits are set

Targets are added

No error message shown

If any of the above is missing — JarveePro will not act.

Automation does not guess your intent.

not a “click one button, get followers” tool

professional automation platform

Daily Q&A Diaries

UI labels

unclear in the UI

already explained

By following the steps and formats already provided in the JarveePro interface and Daily Q&A Diaries, users can automate safely, consistently, and with confidence. 2025-12-22

Introduction

Before starting Instagram automation, asking the right questions can save users from mistakes, confusion, and unnecessary support tickets. In this JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary for Dec. 22nd, 2025, we address some of the most frequently asked pre-sales and onboarding questions — including proxy requirements, Instagram photo and Reels posting, comment reply delays, and how JarveePro connects to Instagram. If you’re evaluating JarveePro or setting up your first Instagram account, this guide clarifies exactly what is supported, what is required, and how automation works behind the scenes.

Q1: Do I need a proxy for each Instagram account?

Answer:

Yes. Each Instagram account must use its own dedicated proxy. JarveePro does not include proxies in any plan, so users need to add their own.

Best practices:

Use 1 proxy per Instagram account

Avoid sharing proxies between accounts

Prefer residential or mobile proxies

Match the proxy country with the account’s registration location

Using shared or reused proxies significantly increases the risk of login challenges and temporary or permanent blocks.

Q2: Does JarveePro post directly to Instagram?

Yes. JarveePro posts directly to Instagram and does not require a Facebook Page, Meta Business Manager, or API-based connection.

This allows full control over posting, automation actions, and scheduling without Meta account dependencies.

Q3: Can JarveePro post photos to Instagram?

Yes. JarveePro fully supports direct photo posting to Instagram, including captions, hashtags, and scheduling.

Q4: Can JarveePro post Instagram Reels?

Answer:

Yes. JarveePro supports Instagram Reels posting, including:

Custom uploaded videos

Q5: Are there any music or copyright limitations when posting Reels?

JarveePro does not restrict music usage. However, Instagram may mute, limit, or remove content that violates its copyright or music policies. Users are responsible for ensuring compliance with Instagram’s rules.

Q6: Can I set delays for comment replies?

Yes. JarveePro allows custom delays for comment replies.

You can:

Set delays such as 5, 10, or 30 minutes

Apply hourly and daily rate limits

Enable randomized timing to better mimic human behavior

This helps reduce automation patterns and lowers detection risk.

Q7: What are the safest automation limits for Instagram?

Answer:

For new or private accounts, recommended starter limits are:

Follows: 20–40 per day

Likes: 50–80 per day

Unfollows: After 3–7 days

Spread actions evenly throughout the day

Avoid aggressive settings, especially during the first 7–14 days of automation.

Summary

JarveePro is a professional Instagram automation platform designed for scalability and control. Proper setup is essential: each account requires its own proxy, accounts must be manually started, posting works directly to Instagram, and delays and limits should be configured conservatively. By following this Q&A guide, users can automate Instagram safely, efficiently, and with confidence in 2025.

Introduction

Running a Facebook Like Post campaign can look confusing at first — especially when the number of accounts is higher than the number of successful likes.

Question

I ran a

Facebook Like Post

campaign with

112 accounts

The result shows

71 success

and

1 failed

Where are the other accounts? Why didn’t all 112 accounts like the post?

Answer

This behavior is

normal

and depends entirely on

how the Post URLs are set up

how likes are distributed across those posts

JarveePro does

not

force every account to like every post.

Instead, it works like this:

1. Likes Are Distributed Per Post URL

In your campaign settings, you defined:

Likes Allowed per Post:

20 → 34

This means:

Each post URL will receive

between 20 and 34 likes

Once a post reaches its allowed limit,

JarveePro stops assigning accounts to that post

If you add multiple post URLs, JarveePro spreads accounts across them —

not all accounts are used on every post

2. Total Accounts ≠ Total Likes

You had:

112 accounts

Multiple post URLs

A per-post like limit

So the math looks like this:

Some accounts are used until posts reach their limits

Remaining accounts are

not needed

, so they are skipped

Skipped accounts are

not failures

That’s why you see:

71 success

1 failed

The rest are simply

unused for this task

3. What Counts as “Failed”?

An account is marked as

Failed

only if:

It tried to like a post and couldn’t (login issue, checkpoint, restriction, etc.)

Check logs here to see why?

If an account was never assigned a post because limits were reached, it is

not counted as failed

4. What Is a “Post URL”? (Very Important)

Post URL

is the direct link to a specific Facebook post.

Correct examples:

https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=XXXXX&id=XXXXX

https://www.facebook.com/username/posts/XXXXXXXX

Incorrect examples:

Page URLs

Profile URLs

Group URLs without a specific post

Homepage links

Each

Post URL = one post that can receive likes

How to Use All Accounts

If you want

more accounts to be used

, you can:

Add

more post URLs

Increase

Likes Allowed per Post

Run multiple Like Post campaigns

JarveePro follows your limits strictly — it does not over-like posts.

Summary

JarveePro distributes likes

based on your settings

Not all accounts are required if post limits are reached

Unused accounts are

normal

, not errors

“Failed” only means an account actually tried and failed

JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary — Dec. 26th, 2025 | How to correctly set up JarveePro Scheduler for automatic, continuous runs.

2025-12-26

Introduction

Scheduling automation tasks sounds simple, but small configuration details can completely change how a campaign behaves.

In this JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary — Dec. 26th, 2025, we break down common scheduling misunderstandings, explain why campaigns may run only once instead of repeating, clarify how JarveePro handles already-followed users, and show the correct setup for running campaigns continuously without manual restarts.

This guide is based on real user questions and real-world usage scenarios.

Question 1

Where scheduled runs can be viewed in JarveePro

Answer

Scheduled campaigns do not create new campaign records every time they run. Scheduling works inside the same campaign instance.

When configured correctly, the campaign:

Runs at the scheduled time

Stops based on stop conditions

Waits until the next scheduled cycle

Not seeing a new campaign entry is expected behavior. Just need to enable scheduler in settings

Question 2

Why a campaign runs only once even when repeat is enabled

This happens when Auto Stop conditions are enabled.

If options like:

Auto Stop After X Hours are active, the campaign will stop after the first run and will not repeat, even if a repeat interval is set.

Repeat scheduling only works when stop conditions do not conflict.

Question 3

Why repeated campaigns act on the same users again

Answer

JarveePro checks historical actions before performing tasks.

If a user was already followed or liked in a previous run:

The system confirms the action state

Marks it as successful

Does not Check Reset Completed Campaigns Before Restart

This behavior protects account safety and keeps statistics accurate.

Question 4

Why already-followed users are counted as successful actions

JarveePro measures campaign success based on the final state, not repeated execution.

If the required condition is already met:

The action is considered successful

The system avoids unnecessary retries

Campaign data remains consistent and reliable

This design prevents false failures.

Question 5

Correct setup for running a campaign automatically every 8 hours

Answer

To allow continuous automation without manual restarts, use the following setup:

Enable Schedule

Set Repeat Every to 8 Hours

Disable Auto Stop options

Avoid limiting repeat counts unless intentional

This configuration allows campaigns to run, pause, and restart automatically throughout the day.

Summary

Most scheduling issues in JarveePro are caused by conflicting settings rather than software errors.

Key points to remember:

Scheduled campaigns reuse the same campaign instance

Auto Stop settings override repeat schedules

Repeated campaigns may encounter the same users

Already-followed users are logged as successful actions

Continuous automation requires Auto Stop to be disabled

Understanding how scheduling and stop conditions interact helps users build stable, hands-free automation workflows.

JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary — Dec. 27th, 2025 | Real Questions. Real Limits. Real Automation Logic.

2025-12-27

Every day, JarveePro users ask questions that reveal the same core truth:

automation success isn’t about pushing harder — it’s about pushing smarter.

Below are the

most representative and practical questions

we received on Dec. 27th, along with detailed explanations based on real platform behavior and long-term automation experience.

Q1: After warm-up, what are the REAL daily limits for posting, liking, and following?

Short answer:

There are

no universal fixed limits

— and anyone claiming otherwise is oversimplifying.

Detailed explanation:

Daily limits depend on multiple factors:

Account age

Previous manual activity

Warm-up history

IP consistency

Platform tolerance (X, Facebook, Instagram, etc.)

For example:

newly warmed account

might safely handle:

5–8 posts/day

30–50 likes/day

20–30 follows/day

An

aged, well-maintained account

may handle:

10–15 posts/day

100+ likes/day

50–80 follows/day

JarveePro

does not force limits

— it executes

what you configure

. The platform’s job is control; your job is strategy.

Golden rule:

Increase actions gradually, never suddenly.

Q2: Why do some accounts succeed while others fail with the SAME settings?

This is one of the most misunderstood aspects of automation.

Because accounts are not equal.

Even if:

Same proxy provider

Same delays

Same action limits

Accounts differ in:

Creation source

Historical trust score

Past violations

Platform-side flags (invisible to users)

JarveePro treats all accounts equally —

platforms don’t

That’s why professional users always:

Test with small batches

Monitor error patterns

Separate risky accounts from stable ones

Automation is probability management, not certainty.

Q3: I have 100+ accounts, but only some performed actions. Where are the rest?

This is usually

not a bug

, but expected behavior.

Common reasons:

Action distribution logic

JarveePro spreads actions across available targets

Target limitations

Not enough valid URLs, posts, or users

Account health filters

Some accounts temporarily paused due to errors or limits

Platform throttling

Platforms silently restrict certain accounts

Important:

JarveePro will

skip unsafe actions

rather than force execution — this protects accounts.

Check:

Logs

Error messages

Target volume

Per-account daily caps

Q4: Should I run all features at once (posting + liking + following)?

Strong opinion here:

No — especially not early.

Recommended rollout:

Posting only (first 5–7 days)

Add light engagement (likes, views)

Then follows / comments

Increase volume slowly

Running everything at once:

Increases risk signals

Makes troubleshooting harder

Causes mixed performance data

Automation works best when actions are

layered

, not stacked.

Q5: Why does JarveePro sometimes stop actions even when limits aren’t reached?

Because

safety overrides volume

JarveePro monitors:

Platform response codes

Temporary blocks

Suspicious patterns

Repetitive behavior signals

If a platform starts pushing back, JarveePro slows or pauses actions to prevent permanent damage.

Think of it as:

“Live risk adjustment,” not failure.

Q6: Is aggressive automation worth it for fast growth?

Blunt answer:

Short-term gain, long-term loss.

Aggressive automation may:

Spike numbers temporarily

Trigger silent shadow limits

Reduce long-term account lifespan

Professional users prioritize:

Account survival

Stable growth

Predictable performance

Sustainable automation always beats aggressive bursts.

Q7: What’s the biggest mistake new users make?

Easy:

Copying someone else’s limits blindly.

What worked for:

A 5-year-old account

A different niche

A different country

…may kill a new account in days.

JarveePro is a

control system

, not a growth guarantee. Strategy still matters.

Q8: Best practices summary

Warm up slowly

Increase actions gradually

Use enough targets

Monitor logs daily

Separate strong vs weak accounts

Don’t chase “max limits”

Prioritize consistency over volume

Automation isn’t magic.

It’s discipline, data, and patience.

JarveePro gives you

powerful control

, but long-term success comes from understanding how platforms

actually behave

— not how we wish they did.

Tomorrow’s growth depends on today’s restraint.

JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary — Dec. 28th, 2025 | Automation Reality Check: Stability, Signals, and Smart Scaling

2025-12-28

Introduction

Automation only looks simple on the surface. Once you start scaling across multiple accounts and platforms, small details begin to matter—a lot. In the December 28th edition of the JarveePro Daily Q&A Diary, we address real questions from users dealing with slowdowns, platform differences, verification checks, and long-term stability. These insights are based on real automation behavior, not theory, and are designed to help users operate JarveePro more safely, consistently, and effectively.

Q1: Why does automation performance slow down after several days, even without errors?

This is a

platform-side behavior

, not a JarveePro issue.

Most social platforms use

progressive trust evaluation

, meaning:

Early actions are tolerated

Continued patterns are observed

Repetitive signals trigger

soft throttling

Soft throttling looks like:

Actions execute but engagement drops

Some actions silently skip

Reach decreases without warnings

JarveePro executes commands correctly, but platforms may

lower visibility or priority

What to do:

Rotate content (don’t reuse identical text)

Reduce repetitive timing patterns

Add rest days (yes, rest matters)

Mix automation with manual-like behavior

Automation should breathe — not run nonstop.

Q2: Is it normal that different platforms behave very differently under the same setup?

Absolutely.

And expecting consistency across platforms is a mistake.

Examples:

X (Twitter):

Sensitive to timing patterns and following velocity

Instagram:

Focuses heavily on interaction quality and repetition

Facebook:

Account history and relationship graphs matter more than raw actions

TikTok:

Content behavior matters more than engagement actions

JarveePro provides unified control —

but

each platform interprets actions differently

That’s why:

One “universal setup” rarely works long-term.

Q3: Some accounts suddenly require verification or login checks — why?

This is usually triggered by

behavioral inconsistency

, not volume.

Common triggers:

IP changes too frequently

Different action patterns day to day

Sudden feature activation (new actions enabled)

Proxy reputation degradation

JarveePro doesn’t cause verifications —

it only

reveals

when platforms start questioning trust.

Best practice:

Keep IPs stable

Avoid enabling new features abruptly

Change limits gradually, not overnight

Think

predictable

, not

random

Q4: Can I run automation 24/7 if limits are low?

Strong answer:

No — and you shouldn’t try.

Platforms measure:

Active hours

Sleep cycles

Behavioral rhythms

Accounts that operate:

16–20 hours/day

Every single day

Without variation

…don’t look human, even at low limits.

Recommended approach:

8–12 active hours/day

Randomized start/end times

Occasional no-action days

JarveePro supports scheduling for a reason — use it.

Q5: Why do comment or DM features feel “riskier” than likes or follows?

Because they are.

From a platform perspective:

Likes = passive signal

Follows = semi-active

Comments & DMs =

high-intent actions

High-intent actions:

Are inspected more deeply

Trigger spam detection faster

Carry higher penalty weight

Rules for comments/DMs:

Use spintax properly

Avoid URLs early

Lower volume than likes/follows

Delay activation until account is stable

If engagement is the fire, comments are gasoline.

Q6: How many accounts should I test before scaling?

Professional answer:

Never scale from a single account.

Minimum recommended testing:

5–10 accounts per platform

Different creation times

Same setup, observed separately

Why?

One account ≠ pattern

Platforms behave probabilistically

You need averages, not anecdotes

Scale only when:

Error rate is stable

Engagement doesn’t decay quickly

No repeated verification loops

Q7: Is it better to maximize limits slowly or stay conservative forever?

Neither extreme works.

The correct mindset is

adaptive scaling

Increase when signals are positive

Pull back when friction appears

Accept plateaus as healthy states

Automation is not about:

“maximum allowed”

It’s about:

“maximum sustainable”

Long-living accounts outperform aggressive ones every time.

Q8: Daily Best Practices Snapshot (Dec. 28)

Don’t expect identical behavior across platforms

Slowdowns without errors = soft throttling

Schedule downtime intentionally

Treat comments & DMs as high risk

Test in batches, not singles

Stability > speed

Summary

Automation doesn’t fail loudly anymore.

It fails

quietly

The users who succeed with JarveePro are not the ones chasing limits —

they’re the ones

reading signals and adjusting early

Control gives you power.

Awareness keeps that power alive.

Q1: I can’t follow more than “Suggested accounts.” Why is this happening?

This occurs because your campaign is set to follow only one account or one profile URL. Instagram limits the number of follows per account per day, and using a single account for hundreds of follows can trigger bans or restrictions.

Use multiple accounts to distribute follow actions.

Avoid overloading a single profile; doing so can result in temporary blocks or permanent bans.

Q3: Can I follow hundreds of users with a single profile URL?

Answer:

No — following hundreds of users from a single profile URL is unsafe. Instagram monitors follow patterns closely, and excessive activity from one account may trigger restrictions or a ban.

Tip:

Use multiple profiles to distribute the workload.

Pace follow actions realistically to mimic natural human behavior.

Use JarveePro campaigns to automate safely while staying within limits.

Q4: What is the safest way to scale follow campaigns using JarveePro?

Scaling safely requires distributing actions, monitoring performance, and respecting Instagram limits.

Add multiple accounts to your campaign.

Set realistic daily follow limits per account.

Schedule actions over several days rather than all at once.

Monitor account health and adjust volume accordingly.

Automating gradually ensures all accounts remain healthy and avoids triggering Instagram’s anti-spam algorithms.

safe follow automation

on Instagram.

Distribute follow operations across multiple accounts.

Avoid using a single profile URL for high-volume follows.

Pace follow actions to mimic natural behavior and prevent bans.

Use JarveePro’s knowledge base and campaign settings to monitor limits and optimize automation.

By combining these practices with JarveePro’s automation tools, marketers can

scale Instagram engagement safely and effectively

, maximizing visibility and growth without compromising account health.

Platforms monitor unusual spikes or repetitive actions.

New accounts warm up slowly and naturally.

Mature accounts stay under detection thresholds.

Automated behavior blends with human-style patterns.

Higher trust, fewer bans, fewer checkpoints, and long-term stability.

Never jump from zero to high activity levels

Q1: What is the correct port setup when running multiple VPS with JarveePro?

Answer:

All VPS instances must use the

same port: 9999

JarveePro’s VPS version is designed to communicate with each server through a unified fixed port. Every VPS should listen on port

9999

, regardless of how many VPS you deploy.

Q2: Why should all VPS share the same port instead of using different ports?

JarveePro handles communication using a standardized port protocol.

Using

one universal port

avoids routing conflicts and ensures that:

JarveePro detects all VPS correctly

Campaigns sync normally

Tasks and status updates flow back to the main controller without interruption

You do

not

need separate ports for separate servers.

Q3: What issue caused confusion during the setup process?

Answer:

There was a misunderstanding about “port routing,” which normally applies when multiple services run on one IP.

However — this does

apply to JarveePro.

✔ Every VPS = Port 9999

❌ No port mapping

❌ No unique ports per VPS

Q4: What should future users do when setting up JarveePro with multiple VPS?

Follow this checklist:

Set

port 9999

on every VPS.

Ensure each VPS has its own unique IP address (required).

Keep firewall inbound/outbound rules allowing port 9999.

Start JarveePro VPS Program on each VPS and verify connection status from the controller.

This setup guarantees stable multi-server performance.

Summary

Today’s key takeaway is the correct multi-VPS setup for JarveePro:

All VPS must use port 9999 — the same port for every instance.

This standardized communication method ensures reliable task management across all servers and avoids the confusion caused by typical port routing practices.

Q1: Is my setup correct when using Content Explorer with Facebook comment campaigns?

Q2: Why does JarveePro comment multiple times on the same Facebook post when using a 1-hour scheduler?

This happens because the scheduler option

“Clean up completed task records when starting a task”

is enabled. When the scheduler restarts every hour, JarveePro clears its history and no longer remembers which post URLs were already processed.

As a result, previously commented posts are treated as new targets.

Q3: How can I ensure one comment per Facebook post URL only?

Answer:

To enforce one comment per post URL:

Open the scheduler settings

Uncheck “Clean up completed task records when starting a task”

Keep the scheduler running in loop mode

This allows JarveePro to retain task history and prevents duplicate comments on the same post.

Q4: Does AI-generated content cause duplicate comments?

No. AI-generated comments can be different or identical, but they do

not control deduplication

. Deduplication is handled entirely by task records and scheduler logic.

AI only affects

comment content

, not

posting behavior

Q5: When should I use AI Monitor instead of Content Explorer?

Answer:

AI Monitor is recommended when you need:

Real-time monitoring of

new Facebook group posts

Keyword-based detection without manual refreshing

Faster reaction to newly published content

For service businesses targeting local Facebook groups, AI Monitor is the most efficient and scalable solution.

Q6: Is AI Monitor a lifetime upgrade and is it worth it for single businesses (not agencies)?

Yes. AI Monitor is a

lifetime license

For single businesses that rely on Facebook group monitoring and lead engagement, it often replaces multiple tools and manual workflows, making it cost-efficient long-term.

Summary

Duplicate Facebook comments in JarveePro are not caused by AI-generated content but by scheduler settings that reset completed task records. Disabling the cleanup option ensures proper deduplication. For users who need real-time Facebook group monitoring based on keywords, AI Monitor is the recommended long-term solution.
