Introduction

As the JarveePro community grows, questions are increasingly focused on operational stability, pricing models, and sustainable automation rather than raw volume. This Daily Q&A addresses several common points of confusion around JarveePro Content Explorer verification, proxy setup, Facebook reputation defense, and the difference between moderation tools and automation-based responses.

Understanding these distinctions is essential for running long-term campaigns safely in 2026.

Q1: Why does Content Explorer sometimes get stuck on “Logging account…” when verifying new accounts?

Answer:

This behavior is usually caused by incomplete or incorrect proxy setup rather than a software malfunction. Content Explorer requires a working proxy to complete the login and verification process. If no proxy is assigned, the proxy fails authentication, or the connection is unstable, the Chromium window may remain open indefinitely instead of returning an error.

To avoid this, ensure proxies are loaded, tested successfully, and correctly assigned before starting account verification.

Q2: What proxy requirements are recommended for verifying accounts in Content Explorer?

Proxies should be active, tested, and aligned with the account’s expected region. Using untested, expired, or mismatched proxies can prevent the login process from completing. Running multiple account verifications simultaneously may also increase the chance of hangs or timeouts.

Verifying one account at a time with stable proxies significantly improves success rates.

Q3: How much can someone realistically charge for managing 100 Facebook accounts used for commenting and profile defense?

Managing 100 Facebook accounts for controlled liking, commenting, and reputation defense is typically priced between

$699 and $3,000 per month

, depending on account age, proxy quality, activity pacing, monitoring effort, and reporting expectations.

Higher pricing reflects risk management and infrastructure costs rather than the volume of actions performed.

Q4: How should large numbers of Facebook accounts be managed to reduce ban risk in 2026?

Accounts should be aged, warmed up gradually, and operated with strict rate limits. A conservative baseline is 3–5 comments per account per day, with likes and passive activity occurring more frequently than comments. Scrolling feeds and idle time help maintain normal behavioral patterns.

Static or consistent proxies are recommended, but behavioral pacing is more important than proxy type alone.

Q5: What is “Comment Guard,” and is it part of JarveePro?

Answer:

Comment Guard refers to Facebook’s native page-level moderation features or similar third-party tools that automatically hide or filter comments containing specific keywords. It is not a JarveePro feature and operates independently at the page or profile moderation level.

Comment Guard only works on assets owned or managed by the account holder.

Q6: Can Comment Guard be used to manage negative comments on other pages or posts tagging a client?

No. Comment Guard cannot affect content on external pages, groups, or profiles, even when a client is tagged. In such cases, moderation tools are ineffective.

The appropriate approach is monitoring mentions and responding with aged accounts using controlled, human-like interaction rather than attempting to hide comments.

Summary

Content Explorer verification issues are most often related to proxy configuration rather than software errors. Large-scale Facebook commenting and defense services require conservative rate limits, aged accounts, and realistic behavior to remain stable. Comment Guard is a moderation tool for owned assets and cannot replace automation when dealing with third-party posts. Separating moderation from engagement strategy is key to effective and sustainable use of JarveePro.

fresh content after the campaign starts

Filters (keywords, engagement thresholds, content type) must actually match the post.

AI Monitor waits patiently for content that meets its logic rules.

Start AI Monitor campaigns

expected posting activity.

Keep filters simple during testing.

. This diary breaks down why blindly reacting can backfire, and how to design a smarter, lower-risk reputation defense strategy using JarveePro and human judgment together.

Q1: My client wants me to comment with multiple accounts on posts attacking her. Is this a good idea?

Answer:

In most cases,

no

— mass commenting on hostile posts can

increase

damage instead of reducing it.

On Facebook, comments signal engagement. When many accounts comment on an attacking post (especially on another page), the algorithm often interprets this as “high interest,” which can:

Increase the post’s reach

Push it into more feeds

Extend its lifespan

Instead of burying the attack, you may unintentionally

amplify it

Q2: Doesn’t using real employee accounts make this safer?

not

change platform mechanics.

Comment in a short time window

coordinated behavior (brigading)

Q1: Can JarveePro remove Facebook’s 24-hour message limit on a single ID?

Answer:

The 24-hour messaging restriction is enforced

JarveePro operates

within

Facebook’s rules. It does not hack, crack, spoof, or bypass platform-level restrictions.

Q2: Why do some accounts get blocked after sending only 1–2 messages?

This is an

account-level trust issue

, not a software issue.

Common reasons include:

New or low-trust Facebook accounts

Accounts with poor activity history

Messaging people you have no prior interaction with

Accounts previously flagged or restricted

Region/IP/account behavior mismatch

When Facebook’s system detects “high-risk behavior,” it may apply a

24-hour limit immediately

, even after a single message.

Q3: Can JarveePro guarantee sending 20 messages per day from one Facebook ID?

Answer:

No — and anyone who claims they can is

lying

Facebook does not provide a fixed, guaranteed daily message quota. Some accounts can send 20+, some can’t send 2. It depends on:

Account age

Trust score

Past violations

Recipient relationship

Message context

JarveePro can help you

test, manage, and scale safer workflows

, but it cannot force Facebook to allow actions your account isn’t trusted to perform.

Q4: Why are friend requests failing or blocked even when sending just one?

Answer:

Friend request limits are also

Facebook-controlled

Common causes:

Sending requests to users with high privacy settings

“You don’t know this user” restrictions

Accounts with low social graph activity

Accounts that previously sent too many requests

If Facebook blocks the action, JarveePro will reflect that result — it will not mask or bypass it.

Q5: Can JarveePro help manage these risks at all?

Yes —

but with realistic expectations

JarveePro helps by:

Testing account limits safely

Controlling daily action volume

Reducing risky behavior patterns

Scaling across

multiple warmed accounts

instead of burning one

What it

does not

do:

Remove Facebook limits

Override account restrictions

“Unlock” blocked IDs

Q6: Is there a free trial to test message limits?

Answer:

No free trial is available for this purpose.

Facebook limits are

account-specific

, not software-specific. A short trial cannot “prove” whether an account will be unrestricted long-term.

Users are advised to start with a

monthly plan

and upgrade later if needed.

Summary

Facebook’s message and friend request limits are

non-negotiable platform rules

. JarveePro does not bypass them — and that’s a good thing.

If your account is limited after minimal actions, the solution is

account quality, warming, and scaling strategy

, not a magic button.

Software manages behavior. Facebook decides permissions.

Understanding that difference saves you time, money, and burned accounts.

Using multiple AI prompts offers better flexibility and safety:

No complex syntax to manage

Less repetition in comments and replies

More natural, human-like engagement

Better compatibility with AI-generated content

Ideal for scraper-based engagement and short-form posts

This approach significantly improves content diversity without increasing operational complexity.

JarveePro improves AI comment diversity by enabling users to select multiple AI prompts that act as variables. Instead of relying on traditional spintax, the system randomly applies different prompts to generate more human-like, varied, and platform-safe content—perfect for large-scale automation and scraper-based engagement.

2026-01-25

Introduction

Many users expect real-time monitoring to instantly return results without understanding how baseline scraping works. JarveePro’s “Search All New Results” feature is designed to establish a content baseline first, then shift into future-only monitoring—ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and zero duplication.

Q1: Why is Real-Time Monitoring not finding new Twitter posts immediately?

Answer:

In most cases, this is caused by

time range and filter settings

, not a system issue.

If

“Search for results published within the last X hours”

is enabled and

no posts exist within that window

, JarveePro will correctly return no results.

This is expected behavior and indicates the monitor is working as designed.

Q2: What does “Recent Posts” or “Last 24 Hours” mean in JarveePro?

“Recent posts” refers strictly to

content published within the selected time window

(e.g. last 1, 12, or 24 hours).

JarveePro does

not

fetch older posts outside this range unless the setting is changed.

If there are no qualifying posts during that period, no URLs will be collected.

Q3: Why does “Search Posts by Keywords” return zero results even when the keyword exists?

Answer:

All filter conditions must be met for a post to be collected. Common blockers include:

Minimum likes set too high

Word count filters excluding short tweets

Language filters

Time window too narrow

If any condition fails, the post is skipped.

Q4: Can I monitor every future post from a specific Twitter account?

Yes.

This is exactly how

“Search All New Results”

works.

Here’s the logic:

First run:

JarveePro scrapes existing posts to establish a baseline

Subsequent runs:

JarveePro

only collects newly published posts

This ensures:

No duplicate scraping

Continuous future monitoring

Only fresh content is captured after the initial run

In short:

First scrape = old posts

Next scrapes = new posts only

Q5: What is the best setup for continuous Twitter monitoring?

Answer:

For ongoing monitoring:

Enable

Search All New Results

Avoid strict filters at the beginning

Set a reasonable monitoring interval

Let the first run complete fully

After that, JarveePro will keep collecting

only new posts automatically

Summary

JarveePro supports continuous monitoring of Twitter accounts using “Search All New Results.” The first run collects existing posts, while all subsequent runs fetch only newly published content. This design ensures reliable real-time tracking without reprocessing old posts.

2026-01-30

Introduction

AI-powered replies are one of JarveePro’s most powerful features—but only when users understand how context, templates, and API connections actually work.

This Q&A diary documents a real Enterprise user case involving AI Templates, ChatGPT API limits, and automated content recognition. The goal is simple: clarify confusion, prevent repeat questions, and help users get AI replies working smoothly without overcomplicating the setup.

Q1: Is there a video showing how to create AI templates for reply tasks?

Answer:

Yes. JarveePro provides official video demos showing how to create and use AI templates for reply and comment tasks. These videos demonstrate both custom AI templates and built-in templates that already handle content context automatically.

Q2: Do I need to use the exact same AI prompt shown in the demo video?

No. The demo prompt is only an example. You can modify the wording freely as long as the prompt instructs the AI to generate a reply based on the post content. JarveePro automatically supplies the context—there is no requirement to copy the prompt word-for-word.

Q3: Are the templates shown in the video default templates?

No. The templates shown in demos are custom examples. JarveePro also provides built-in AI templates that work out of the box without requiring any variables or manual context mapping.

Q4: Why does the AI template work for others but not for me?

In most cases, this issue is related to the API key, not the AI template. Common causes include:

Using a free or exhausted API key

Missing API billing or token limits

Incorrectly saved API credentials

Once a valid, paid API key is added and saved, AI templates function normally.

Q5: Does ChatGPT Plus include API access?

Answer:

No. A ChatGPT Plus subscription does

not

include API usage. API access requires a separate OpenAI API key with active billing and available tokens.

Q6: Why do I see a “Too many requests” or connection error?

This error usually indicates that the API key has:

Reached its token limit

No billing attached

Been overused within a short timeframe

Adding billing or generating a new API key resolves the issue.

Q7: What should I enter for the variable “content” in Search & Generate tasks?

Nothing. In fact, it is

not necessary to use a “Search & Generate” task at all

if your goal is content-aware comments or replies.

When you set up an

AI Template directly

(for AI Comment or AI Reply tasks),

JarveePro automatically analyzes the post content and injects the context internally

. The system generates content-aware comments or replies without requiring any variables, placeholders, or manual input.

Q8: Can JarveePro automatically recognize the post topic and reply accordingly?

Answer:

Yes. When you select a built-in AI template, JarveePro passes the post’s thematic content directly to the AI engine. The reply is generated based on the scraped content without any custom prompt setup.

Q9: Why does my task stay on “Waiting”?

“Waiting” means the task is functioning correctly. The system is waiting for new content from the Advanced Content Explorer. Once new posts are detected, the reply task resumes automatically.

Q10: How do I run campaigns endlessly with scheduling enabled?

Endless campaigns require:

A scheduler with repeating intervals

Enough accounts to handle ongoing replies

Each account can perform limited actions per run. To scale continuously, additional accounts must be added.

Q11: Where do I set the number of loops and replies per run?

Loops & timing:

Scheduler settings

Replies per run:

Campaign link/task settings

These controls work together to regulate campaign behavior safely.

Check our knowledge base for basic campaign settings

Summary

This case highlights the most common AI-related misunderstandings in JarveePro:

AI context is passed automatically

API access is separate from ChatGPT Plus

Variables are usually unnecessary

“Waiting” status is normal

1st account → Link 1

Post URL

tab and

Text

The Correct Setup: Sequential Rotation (The Fix)

JarveePro will rotate correctly only if all four settings are aligned:

Add all your links under “Post URL”

Example:

5 links × 10 comments = 50 total

10 links × 10 comments = 100 total

Enable “Sequential” Mode

This is the MOST important setting.

It tells JarveePro:

Use Link 1 first, then Link 2, then Link 3… in order.

Set your Max Uses correctly

For 100 accounts and 10 links:

Setting

Value

Why

Max uses per account

1 → 1

Each account leaves ONE comment

Max uses per item (URL)

10 → 10

Each URL gets 10 comments before cycling

Max uses per target

20 → 20 (optional)

Works as a safety cap for rotation

These numbers MUST match your plan.

If you want 5 links × 20 comments each → set Max uses per item to 20.

Apply the same logic to the “Text” tab

If you want:

Account 1 → Text 1

Account 2 → Text 2

Account 3 → Text 3

…then you must:

Enable Sequential

Set Max Uses Per Item = same number as URL rotation

Set Max Uses Per Account = 1 → 1

Most users miss this part — the text rotates independently from the URL list.

Why jarveePro was repeating the same URL before

Three common reasons:

Max Uses per Item was set too high (like 100 → 100)

Only one URL was imported

Summary

Add all URLs into Post URL

Use

Sequential

mode

Max Uses Per Item

to the correct distribution

JarveePro Daily Report – Sept 20th, 2025 (Licensing, VPS Setup, Proxies & Bandwidth Insights)

2025-09-20

Welcome to the

JarveePro Daily Report – Sept 20th, 2025

. Today’s update addresses common client questions about

license upgrades, running JarveePro on dedicated servers, proxy requirements, and bandwidth usage

. We also cover the latest software improvements, ensuring smoother account management and more efficient automation across platforms.

Q1: Is it possible to buy a month or year license first and then later upgrade to lifetime by paying the difference?

A1:

Yes. You can start with a Monthly or Yearly license, and later upgrade to Lifetime by paying only the difference. This way, you don’t need to pay the full price again.

Q2: We will use a dedicated server to run this software. Is it ok if we access it via remote desktop?

A2:

Yes, that works perfectly. Many clients use JarveePro on VPS or dedicated servers with remote desktop access. It will not affect the performance of the software as long as the server has stable internet and enough resources (RAM, CPU).

Q3: Do we need proxies from IPfarming as well?

A3:

If you plan to manage multiple accounts (for example, 50–500 IDs), then yes, proxies are highly recommended. Proxies help keep each account safe by separating their login IPs, making them look more natural. Without proxies, using too many accounts under the same IP may lead to restrictions.

Q4: If we use 500 IDs just for liking posts or commenting, what kind of bandwidth are we expecting to use each day?

A4:

JarveePro itself does not use heavy bandwidth. Each action (like, comment, post) sends only small requests to the platform.

For 500 accounts:

If each account does

10–15 comments per day

, and

20–25 likes per day

, the total data use is still very small (only a few hundred MB daily).

To give you an idea: streaming a short YouTube video uses more bandwidth than all 500 accounts liking and commenting for a whole day. So a basic internet line is more than enough.

JarveePro Update Log (Latest Release)

Optimized the Dashboard interface.

YouTube:

Now supports importing passwords and email protocols from recovery email accounts.

Fixed an issue where the

"Use your security key with TikTok.com"

pop-up appeared during login.

Account Management:

Added ability to copy text in the account table by double-clicking it.

Added a setting to prevent overlapping browser windows.

Added a setting to select fingerprint browser versions

138, 127, and 118

Notes for Clients:

Always start slowly when running multiple accounts. Increase actions gradually to avoid platform restrictions.

Use quality proxies and dedicated servers for smoother operation.

If you’re unsure about technical terms (like bandwidth), think of it this way: JarveePro’s actions are like sending text messages, not streaming videos. Very light on internet usage.

Summary

Key insights from today’s Q&A and updates include:

License Flexibility:

Start with monthly or yearly plans and upgrade to lifetime licenses later by paying only the difference.

Server & RDP Usage:

JarveePro works seamlessly on VPS or dedicated servers via remote desktop, provided the server has stable internet and sufficient RAM/CPU.

Proxies for Multi-Account Management:

Using 50–500 accounts? Proxies help separate logins, improve account safety, and reduce risk of restrictions.

Bandwidth Considerations:

Even hundreds of accounts performing likes and comments daily consume minimal data—much less than streaming a short video.

Latest Software Updates:

Improved dashboard interface, YouTube import support, fixes for login pop-ups, and new settings for fingerprint browser versions and window management

text:
JarveePro Error: “Profile Error Occurred – Your Preferences Cannot Be Read”

2026-03-17

Introduction

While using

JarveePro

, some users may encounter a message that says:

“Profile error occurred. Your preferences cannot be read. Some features may be unavailable and changes to preferences won’t be saved.”

This error can look alarming at first, but in most cases it is related to

insufficient disk space on the server

, not a permanent system failure. Understanding why this happens—and how to prevent it—can help keep your automation running smoothly without interruptions.

Q1: What does the “Profile Error Occurred – Your Preferences Cannot Be Read” message mean?

Answer:

This error usually indicates that the system

cannot access or write the browser profile configuration files

used by JarveePro.

JarveePro relies on browser profiles to store automation settings, cookies, and account preferences. If the system cannot read or update these files, the application may temporarily disable some features and show this warning.

Q2: Is this error directly responsible for campaigns disappearing?

In most cases,

no

This error itself

does not directly delete campaigns or automation tasks

. Campaign configurations are stored separately in JarveePro’s internal data files.

However, the issue can have

indirect effects

if the root cause is a

server storage problem

, especially when the disk becomes completely full.

Q3: What is the most common cause of this error?

Answer:

The most common cause is

insufficient disk space on the server

, particularly on the

C drive

When the operating system runs out of available disk space:

The system cannot create or update profile files

Browser sessions fail to initialize

Temporary cache files cannot be written

Automation processes may behave unpredictably

For stable performance, it is recommended to

always keep at least 10GB of free space on the C drive

for system memory buffering and temporary file operations.

Q4: What types of files can consume disk space during automation?

Answer:

Several types of files may gradually occupy disk space during automation:

1. Browser Cache

Each automated account generates browser cache files.

These may include:

Cookies

Website resources

Media files

Session data

A single account may generate

hundreds of megabytes of cache

, and multiple accounts can quickly accumulate several gigabytes.

2. Automation Logs

JarveePro stores operational logs for troubleshooting and activity tracking.

3. Profile Data

Each account uses a browser profile that stores preferences and session data.

4. Other Software on the Server

Many servers run multiple applications simultaneously, which may also consume disk space over time.

Q5: How much space do JarveePro accounts typically use?

Answer:

The exact storage usage depends on activity levels, but generally:

1000 accounts

may use around

2–3GB

of profile and automation data.

Browser cache

can grow faster, especially when accounts browse media-heavy platforms.

If each account generates large cache files, even

a few hundred accounts can consume several gigabytes

of disk space.

Q6: How can users prevent this error?

1. Keep Disk Space Available

Minimum:

10GB free

Prevents write failures

2. Control Thread Count

Match threads to

real CPU capability

, not advertised specs:

Safe baseline:

4 cores → 1–2 threads

8 cores → 3–5 threads

16+ cores → scale higher

If errors appear → reduce threads immediately

3. Avoid Task Spikes

Running multiple heavy actions at the same time = instant overload

Better approach:

Stagger tasks

Add delays

Spread activity across time

4. Upgrade Infrastructure

If you're serious about volume:

Move from VPS →

VDS / Dedicated CPU server

This alone can eliminate:

Profile errors

Random instability

Task failures

5. Monitor CPU, Not Just Disk

Most users only check storage — mistake.

Watch:

CPU usage %

Load spikes

System lag when tasks start

Q7: Can this error be caused by CPU or server load issues?

Answer: Yes — and this is more common than many users realize.

Even if your server has plenty of disk space, this error can appear when the system is under

heavy CPU or thread load

When running multiple tasks or threads simultaneously:

Browser profiles may fail to initialize in time

Profile files cannot be accessed fast enough

Read/write operations get delayed or interrupted

JarveePro throws the same “Profile Error” message

In this case, the issue is

performance-related, not storage-related

What’s Actually Happening Behind the Scenes

JarveePro relies heavily on:

Browser instances

Real-time profile access

Concurrent automation actions

When you increase threads:

You’re not just adding tasks — you’re multiplying:

CPU usage

Memory pressure

Disk I/O operations

If the server

can’t keep up

, profile access fails → error appears.

Real Example (From Users)

VPS:

4 cores / 8GB RAM

Threads:

Result:

✅ 1 thread → works fine

❌ 2–3 threads → error appears

Why?

Shared VPS environments often

don’t deliver full CPU power consistently

“4 cores” ≠ guaranteed 4 cores under load

Summary

The “Profile Error Occurred – Your Preferences Cannot Be Read” message in JarveePro is

not limited to disk space issues

It is typically caused by:

Insufficient disk space

, OR

High CPU load / excessive threading

While disk-related problems prevent profile files from being written, CPU overload prevents them from being accessed in time.

Both scenarios lead to the same error message.

For stable automation at scale, users must:

Maintain sufficient disk space

Control thread usage

Avoid overloading VPS environments

Use higher-performance servers when scaling

My Take

If someone tells you this error is “just disk space”…

They’ve never scaled hard enough 😄

At small scale → yes, disk

At real scale →

CPU becomes the bottleneck FAST

JarveePro Licensing & VPS Explained: How One License Runs Multiple VPS and Hundreds of Accounts

2026-01-18

Introduction

Many users are confused about how JarveePro licensing works when VPS is involved.

Questions like

“Do I need 10 licenses for 10 VPS?”

“Is the VPS included?”

, or

“How many accounts can I really run?”

come up again and again.

This guide explains

JarveePro Standard License vs VPS License

, how

VPS Mode actually works

, and how users can scale from

10 to 500+ accounts

using

one single license

, even if they have zero technical background.

If you have a goal, a growth plan, and a lot of accounts — this will make everything click.

Q1: What is JarveePro Standard License?

Answer:

The JarveePro Standard License is designed to run JarveePro on

one local PC or one VPS only

When you launch JarveePro with a standard license, you will choose:

“I want to start the JarveePro main program”

This mode:

Runs on

one machine

Controls all accounts

locally

Is ideal for small to medium setups

Requires

one license per machine

If you want to run JarveePro on multiple VPS at the same time, the standard license is

not enough

Q2: What is JarveePro VPS License?

Answer:

JarveePro VPS License is a

special lifetime license

that enables

VPS Mode

When you launch JarveePro with this license, you choose:

“I want to start the JarveePro VPS program”

This unlocks:

VPS Mode inside JarveePro

The built-in

VPS Manager

Centralized control of

multiple VPS from one program

⚠️ Important:

This is

NOT

10 licenses.

ONE license that can control up to 10 VPS

Q3: Does the VPS license include the actual VPS server?

Answer:

No.

JarveePro

does not sell VPS hardware

You:

Buy your VPS from providers like AWS, Vultr, DigitalOcean, etc. or from

https://jarveepro.com/service.html

Install JarveePro on

one main machine

Add VPS IPs into JarveePro VPS Manager

JarveePro only provides the

software and control system

, not the servers.

Q4: How does one license control multiple VPS?

Answer:

In VPS Mode, JarveePro acts as a

central controller

Inside

VPS Manager

, you:

Add each VPS by IP and port

Set thread limits per VPS

Assign accounts to specific VPS

JarveePro then:

Sends tasks to each VPS

Executes actions remotely

Collects results back into one dashboard

All campaigns, settings, and logic stay in

one JarveePro interface

Q5: How many accounts can I run with one VPS license?

Answer:

There is

no fixed account limit

imposed by JarveePro.

The real limits are:

VPS hardware (CPU, RAM)

Proxy quality

Platform safety rules

Typical setups:

1 VPS → 30–60 accounts

10 VPS → 300–500+ accounts

All of this is done with

one VPS license

, not multiple licenses.

Q6: Is this the same as buying 10 standard licenses?

Answer:

No — and this is a critical difference.

If you bought 10 standard licenses:

You would pay

$2199 × 10

You would manage 10 separate installations

No centralized control

With the

VPS License ($3,979 one-time)

One license

One control panel

Up to 10 VPS

Centralized campaigns and monitoring

That’s why the VPS license exists.

Q7: What does “10 VPS Version” actually mean?

Answer:

It means:

One lifetime JarveePro license that allows JarveePro to connect to and manage up to

10 VPS simultaneously

It does

not

mean:

10 licenses

10 copies of JarveePro

10 separate activations

It is

one license, VPS-enabled

Q8: Do I still need proxies if I use VPS?

Answer:

Yes.

VPS ≠ proxy.

You still need:

Residential or mobile proxies

One proxy per account (recommended)

Proper IP rotation strategy

VPS handles

processing power

Proxies handle

account safety

Q9: Is VPS Mode required for Mother–Child (Slave) method?

For small setups, no.

For

large-scale setups (100+ accounts)

, yes.

VPS Mode allows:

Account distribution

Load balancing

Lower detection risk

Stable long-term automation

This is why agencies and growth teams use VPS Mode.

Q10: What is the total cost structure (simplified)?

Answer:

One-time costs:

JarveePro Standard License:

$2,199

OR JarveePro VPS License (10 VPS):

$3,979

Monthly costs:

VPS hosting (your provider)

Proxies (your provider)

JarveePro software itself has

no monthly fee

Summary

JarveePro VPS License is

not expensive — it is misunderstood

You are not buying servers.

You are not buying multiple licenses.

You are buying

one lifetime control system

that lets you scale automation across multiple VPS safely and efficiently.

If your goal is serious growth with hundreds of accounts, VPS Mode is not optional — it’s the foundation.

text:
JarveePro Rate Limits: Avoid Bans with Safe Daily Activity

2025-12-15

JarveePro’s

Rate Limit feature

is designed to keep your accounts safe while still allowing automation at scale. The goal is

human-like activity

, not maximum speed. Following these guidelines reduces the risk of bans or soft-bans.

General Principles

Start Slow:

Every new account needs a warm-up period to mimic natural activity.

Incremental Growth:

Increase posts, likes, follows, and messages gradually.

Respect Platform Limits:

Each social network has its own thresholds; exceeding them is the fastest way to trigger a ban.

Use Rate Limits:

Always configure JarveePro’s per-day and per-hour limits. Never disable them.

Suggested Safe Limits by Platform (Post-Warm-Up)

These are

general recommendations

, for normal personal/business accounts. Adjust carefully for aged or highly trusted accounts.

Platform

Posts / Day

Likes / Day

Follows / Day

Auto Replies / Day

Notes

Twitter

5–20 tweets (retweets counted separately)

50–200 likes

30–100 follows

20–50 replies

After warm-up, gradually increase by 10–20% weekly. Retweets and replies count separately.

Instagram

1–5 posts

100–300 likes

50–150 follows

30–50 comments

Stories don’t count toward limits. Adjust based on account age.

TikTok

1–3 posts

20–50 follows

10–30 comments

Warm-up phase: 1 post/day for first 7 days.

Facebook Pages

N/A

10–20 comments

Focus on page posts; avoid mass commenting too quickly.

LinkedIn

1–2 posts

20–50 likes

10–30 connections

10–20 messages

Connections should grow gradually; avoid bulk messaging.

YouTube

1–3 videos

50–200 likes

10–30 comments

Use DaisySMS for phone verification if prompted.

These numbers are

safe starting points

. Always monitor account health and adjust if you see warnings or soft bans.

Q: After the warm-up phase, what are the limits in terms of posts, retweets, replies, etc. per day for Twitter?

A:

After the warm-up phase, safe daily activity limits on Twitter depend on account age, trust, and past activity. The goal is to mimic human behavior to reduce the risk of bans or soft-bans.

Recommended safe limits per day (post-warm-up):

Action

Safe Daily Limit

Notes

Tweets (original)

5–20

Gradually increase from warm-up; space throughout the day

Retweets

20–50

Counted separately from tweets

Replies / Mentions

Avoid sending replies too quickly; randomize intervals

Likes

50–200

Spread activity to appear natural

Follows

30–100

Gradually increase; monitor follow/unfollow limits

Direct Messages / Auto Replies

Use with caution; never send bulk identical messages

Twitter-Specific Warm-Up Phase

For Twitter, the warm-up period is crucial:

Days 1–3:

1–3 tweets, 5–10 likes, 2–5 follows, 1–2 replies

Days 4–7:

3–5 tweets, 20–50 likes, 10–20 follows, 5–10 replies

After Week 1:

Gradually increase to the general safe limits table above

Tips:

Retweets are counted separately from original tweets. Spread activity throughout the day.

Slow and steady wins the safety game

. Rapid spikes = high risk of suspension.

Additional Tips for Safety

Use different actions per account:

Don’t do maximum posts, likes, follows, and messages all at once.

Randomize timing:

JarveePro’s scheduling tools can randomize intervals to mimic human behavior.

Monitor notifications:

If the platform flags an account, scale down immediately.

Check the Rate Limit logs:

JarveePro logs allow you to review hourly/daily activity to stay within safe limits.

Summary

Account limits are

not fixed

— they depend on:

Account age and trust

Platform type and activity history

Warm-up progression and scaling speed

JarveePro Rate Limits

let you configure all of this safely. Start conservative, monitor activity, and gradually scale to maximize automation without risking bans.

text:
JarveePro Scheduler — Advanced Use Cases & Deep Answers

2025-10-17

If you’ve already learned the basics from our

Task Scheduler beginner guide

, this article will take you a step further.

JarveePro’s Scheduler is not just a timer — it’s a

full automation controller

that can coordinate thousands of posts, reschedules, and campaign loops with precision. Here, we’ll dive into

real user cases and advanced behaviors

to help you get the most out of it.

While the

basic guide

explains how to create and run schedules, many power users have deeper questions once they start using it daily. This article answers the most common

real user cases

and

advanced scenarios

from our support channel.

Case 1: “If I tick ‘Automatically Reset Completed Tasks’ — will it repost old content?”

Short answer:

No, unless you also enable

“Clear Historical Usage Data When Resetting a Task.”

Detailed explanation:

The “Reset Completed Tasks” option clears the current session data and prepares the campaign for a new run.

JarveePro will

not repost

the same content if your campaign settings restrict reusing photos, captions, or videos.

Only if you also check “Clear Historical Usage Data” will JarveePro forget past posting records and allow the same content to be reused.

Tip:

Use both options together only when you intentionally want to recycle old posts.

Case 2: “What happens if I schedule the same campaign multiple times a day?”

When you set

Loop Execution

(e.g., every 4 hours), JarveePro will repeat the task based on your defined cycle.

Example:

Task starts at 00:00, repeats every 4 hours

It will run at 00:00, 04:00, 08:00, 12:00, 16:00, and 20:00.

Each time, it checks for new unposted content and posts accordingly.

Pro Tip:

Avoid scheduling overlapping times between multiple campaigns that use the same accounts to prevent rate-limit issues or flagged behavior.

Case 3: “If I change content while a task is paused — will it take effect when resumed?”

Yes.

When you pause a scheduled task, all campaign parameters (like source lists, captions, or new videos) are

re-read

once you resume.

This allows mid-cycle edits without restarting from scratch.

However:

If you had “Automatically Reset Completed Tasks” enabled, the campaign will start fresh, and completed items won’t be recognized as already posted.

Case 4: “How does JarveePro handle time zones when scheduling tasks?”

JarveePro always uses your

local computer time zone

, not UTC or the proxy’s region.

If you’re running accounts from multiple countries, plan your schedule using your system time.

Example:

If your PC is set to GMT+8 and you schedule 10:00, your post goes live at 10:00 local time — regardless of whether the account uses a U.S. or Brazil proxy.

Case 5: “Can I combine Task Scheduler with Auto Stop Conditions?”

Yes — they work beautifully together.

Example setup:

You schedule posting every 3 hours.

You also set “Stop task after" 1 Minute, 1 Hour, 1 Day or More.

JarveePro will check the stop condition each loop. Once triggered, the schedule pauses automatically, ensuring your actions stay within safety limits.

Case 6: “Why do my tasks keep starting and stopping instantly?”

This usually happens when:

The scheduled

start time

is in the past.

No valid items are left to process.

Or the system reached your

maximum loop count

Fix:

Double-check the

“Start Time”

, make sure the content queue is not empty, and either set loop count to

(unlimited) or increase it to your preferred number.

Case 7: “How can I schedule posting evenly across all accounts?”

Use the

Account Interval Delay

and

Loop Delay

together.

Example:

Post between 10:00 and 22:00

Every 4 hours

Add random delay of 10–30 minutes between accounts

JarveePro will spread actions smoothly throughout the day, avoiding pattern detection.

Advanced Power Tip: Combining Schedulers with JarveePro AI Monitor

If you run AI Monitor (auto-updating sources), the Scheduler can auto-reset and fetch new items each cycle.

This means every time the Scheduler restarts, JarveePro pulls a fresh list of videos, comments, or targets — ideal for viral posting loops.

2026-05-27

Overview

The

Watch Video

tool inside JarveePro TikTok Campaigns is designed to simulate natural TikTok video engagement by automatically watching videos and optionally performing engagement actions such as likes, favorites, and shares during playback.

Unlike simple “view bot” systems, JarveePro’s Watch Video campaign focuses on timed engagement behavior, helping actions appear more organic and human-like.

This tool is useful for:

Increasing account activity naturally

Warming up TikTok accounts

Supporting engagement campaigns

Creating realistic viewing behavior patterns

Combining passive and active engagement actions

How the TikTok Watch Video Tool Works

The campaign works by:

Selecting TikTok accounts

Loading video URLs

Watching videos for a configurable duration

Triggering optional engagement actions at specific playback times

This creates a more realistic engagement sequence compared to instant interactions.

Campaign Settings Explained

Select Accounts

Choose which TikTok accounts will run the Watch Video campaign.

JarveePro supports running the campaign across multiple accounts simultaneously while maintaining individual session behavior.

Best practice:

Rotate accounts naturally

Avoid aggressive simultaneous actions on fresh accounts

Video URLs

Add the TikTok video URLs you want the campaign to watch and engage with.

Supported use cases:

Your own TikTok videos

Client campaigns

Influencer promotion

Warm-up engagement targets

Niche content interaction

You can load:

Single URLs

Multiple URLs

Rotating engagement targets

Watch Video Settings

Limit Video Play Time (Seconds)

Defines how long JarveePro will watch the TikTok video before exiting.

Default:

30 seconds

This helps simulate natural watch duration instead of instantly leaving the video.

Why It Matters

TikTok heavily analyzes:

Watch duration

Retention signals

Interaction timing

Longer and more realistic watch sessions create safer behavioral patterns.

Best Practices

Use 15–45 seconds for standard campaigns

Randomize durations when scaling

Avoid extremely short watch times

Optional Engagement Actions

JarveePro can trigger engagement actions during playback at predefined timing points.

This creates more realistic interaction flow compared to immediate actions.

Like After +2 Seconds Playing

Automatically likes the video after 2 seconds of playback.

Why This Helps

Mimics quick positive engagement

Creates realistic “scroll and like” behavior

Helps diversify interaction timing

Recommended for:

Warm-up campaigns

Low-intensity engagement automation

Favorite After +10 Seconds Playing

Adds the video to Favorites after 10 seconds of playback.

Why This Matters

Favorites are considered a stronger engagement signal than likes because they indicate higher viewer interest.

This behavior:

Improves engagement diversity

Simulates deeper user interaction

Creates more natural activity patterns

Niche targeting

Content research accounts

Long-term engagement campaigns

Share After +22 Seconds Playing

Shares the video after 22 seconds of playback.

Why This Is Powerful

Shares are one of TikTok’s strongest engagement indicators.

Triggering shares later in the watch session:

Looks more human

Suggests genuine viewer interest

Avoids unnatural instant-share behavior

Best used carefully:

Lower daily limits recommended

Avoid excessive share activity on fresh accounts

Recommended Campaign Strategy

Safe Warm-Up Setup

20–30 second watch duration

Likes enabled

Favorites optional

Shares disabled initially

Best for:

New TikTok accounts

Account aging

Behavioral warm-up

Balanced Engagement Setup

30–45 second watch duration

Favorites enabled

Limited shares

Established accounts

Engagement diversification

Daily activity simulation

High-Engagement Campaigns

Longer playback sessions

Full engagement stack enabled

Rotating video targets

Delayed action intervals

Best for:

Influencer campaigns

Viral amplification workflows

Advanced automation systems

Best Practices

Avoid aggressive share limits

Rotate target videos frequently

Use realistic watch durations

Combine passive and active engagement

Scale slowly on new accounts

Keep interaction patterns varied

Conclusion

The TikTok Watch Video tool in JarveePro is more than a simple view automation feature. It is a timed engagement system designed to simulate realistic TikTok viewing behavior while adding optional interaction layers such as likes, favorites, and shares.

When configured properly, it helps:

Improve behavioral diversity

Create natural engagement patterns

Support account warm-up strategies

Enhance large-scale TikTok automation workflows

Used correctly, Watch Video campaigns become an important foundation layer for safer and more human-like TikTok automation inside JarveePro.

text:
JarveePro VPS Setup Guide: Fix Instagram Reels, Stories & Browser Limits

2026-01-20

Introduction

Running JarveePro on a VPS is essential for users managing multiple accounts, large-scale automation, or distributed infrastructures. However, VPS environments behave differently from local PCs, especially when it comes to browser rendering, media playback, and system performance settings.

This FAQ addresses

common VPS-related questions raised by JarveePro users

across Telegram, WhatsApp, and support channels, focusing specifically on

browser limits, Instagram Reels & Stories playback, and Windows VPS configuration

Q1: Why do Instagram Reels or Stories not load on my VPS?

Answer:

This is usually caused by

Windows VPS performance settings

, not JarveePro itself.

Most VPS providers deploy Windows with

“Adjust for best performance”

enabled by default. This disables visual components and media-related features required for Chromium-based browsers to play Instagram Reels and Stories correctly.

Solution

On each VPS:

Open

System → Advanced system settings

Go to

Performance → Settings

Select

Custom

Enable:

Animate controls and elements inside windows

Show window contents while dragging

Smooth edges of screen fonts

Apply changes and restart the browser

Once enabled, Chromium inside JarveePro can properly load Instagram media.

Q2: Why does Instagram work on my local PC but not on the VPS?

Answer:

Local PCs typically use

“Best appearance”

Windows settings by default, which allow media codecs and UI rendering to function normally.

VPS environments prioritize CPU efficiency over visuals, which:

Disables some rendering pipelines

Affects video playback inside embedded browsers

This is why the same JarveePro setup works locally but fails on a VPS until visual settings are adjusted.

Q3: How many browser instances can run simultaneously on one VPS?

There is

no fixed limit

set by JarveePro.

The real limit depends on:

CPU cores

Available RAM

Disk I/O

Proxy quality

What actions the browsers are performing (idle vs watching Reels vs posting)

Practical guidance:

Lightweight actions (likes, follows): dozens of browsers may run

Media-heavy actions (Reels, Stories): significantly fewer

Scaling to hundreds or thousands requires

multiple VPS machines

, not one system

JarveePro is designed to scale

horizontally

, not by forcing everything onto one VPS.

Q4: Can I run 1,000 Chrome browsers on a single PC or VPS?

Answer:

No — not realistically or safely.

Even enterprise servers cannot stably run 1,000 active Chromium instances with media playback. Doing so would cause:

CPU throttling

Memory exhaustion

Browser crashes

Account instability

Best practice:

Split workloads across multiple VPS

Assign accounts logically per VPS

Avoid media-heavy tasks on overloaded machines

Q5: Is this a JarveePro limitation or a VPS hardware issue?

In most cases, it is a

VPS configuration or hardware limitation

, not a JarveePro issue.

Common causes:

Disabled Windows visual effects

Low CPU/RAM allocation

Media codecs unavailable in VPS environment

Overloaded VPS running too many browsers

Once the VPS is configured correctly, JarveePro behaves the same as on a local machine.

Summary

Running JarveePro on a VPS requires proper system configuration to ensure stable automation and media playback.

Key takeaways:

Instagram Reels & Stories issues are usually

Windows VPS settings

Enable visual effects for Chromium-based browsers

Browser limits depend on VPS hardware, not JarveePro

Scale using

multiple VPS

, not a single overloaded machine

Correct VPS setup eliminates most playback and performance issues.

text:
JarveePro 导入账户中文教学｜Facebook 批量导入账号详细步骤

2025-10-11

下面是一份面向不会看英文客户的中文一步步教学，按截图（左侧是表格预览，右侧是

Please mark the columns to import

区）来讲，包含示例与常见问题解决办法。

（示例中“Column1/Column2/Column3/Column4”就是界面中表格最上方显示的列名）

一、导入前先准备好文件（CSV / TXT）

每行一条账号记录，列与列之间用同一种分隔符（常见：逗号

或 制表符

\t

）。

推荐用 Excel 保存为

CSV UTF-8

，或者保存为 TXT（行分隔

\r\n

，列分隔

文件示例（每一行为一个账号）：

[email protected]

,abc123456,

,socks5://1.2.3.4:1080

1378617182343,abc123456,

上面两行分别是：

账号或邮箱,密码,辅助邮箱,代理

二、界面操作（按顺序）

打开

Import Account

左侧：选择

Category Type = Facebook

，并选好 Category Name（或新建）。

点击

Open File

，选你准备好的 CSV/TXT。界面会在中间显示表格预览（Column1, Column2...）。

如果显示不正确，检查左侧的

Row Separator

（一般

\r\n

）和

Column Separator

\t

），修改后点击重新载入（Reload txt file）。

右侧的 “Please mark the columns to import” 就是关键：对照中间表格，把每个下拉框选择成对应的列（Column1/2/3...）。

全选、确认无误后点击

OK

完成导入。

三、右侧每一项怎么填（中文逐项解释）

I only have cookies（仅有 cookies）

如果你的文件里只有 cookie 字符串（没有账号/密码），勾选这个选项。只需要在 Cookies 下拉里选择对应的列，导入时会把该列当作 cookie 导入。

Account / Email（账号 / 邮箱）

选择包含账号名或邮箱的列（例如

[email protected]

1378617182343

）。看中间预览哪一列是邮箱/账号就选哪列。

Password（密码）

选择包含密码的列（例如

abc123456

）。

Cookies（Cookies 字符串）

如果你有 cookie，请选择包含完整 cookie 字符串的列。

常见格式

c_user=xxx; xs=xxx; datr=xxx;

（即

name=value; name2=value2; ...

，整段作为一个字符串）。

Proxy（代理）

选择包含代理信息的列。

常用格式

socks5://IP:端口

IP:端口

用户名:密码@IP:端口

（带账号密码的代理）

如果你的文件里只有 IP 或端口，需要在导入前批量拼好格式（见后面批量处理方法）。

2FA（两步验证 / 验证码）

如果账号需要填写 2 步验证码并且你有固定的验证码列（例如人工采集到的临时代码），在这里选择该列。

Token（访问令牌）

有些服务用长字符串 token 登录（不常见）。如果你有，将那列映射到 Token。没有可不选。

四、根据你截图的具体示例（直接对应的选择建议）

截图里中间表格示例显示：

Column1 = 是账号ID

Column2 = 密码（

abc123456...

Column3 = 辅助邮箱（hotmail 等）

Column4 = 代理（

socks5://...

在右侧下拉应该这样选（针对该截图）

Account / Email →

Column1

（如果这列是你登录用的账号/ID）

Password →

Column2

Cookies → （如果没有 cookie 列则不选）

Proxy →

Column4

其他（2FA/Token）如果没有就不选

五、常见问题与解决办法（排查流程）

导入后失败 / 登录不成功

检查密码是否正确（有无多余空格）。

检查代理是否有效（尝试手动用一个账号连接测试）。

检查 cookie 是否完整（部分 cookie 丢失会导致登录失败）。

是否需要 2FA（需要验证码或手动验证）。

表格列对不上 / 列内容乱码

用记事本或 Excel 打开，确认列分隔符（逗号 vs 制表符）。

保存为

CSV UTF-8

，避免中文或特殊字符乱码。

代理格式不被识别

统一格式为

IP:端口

IP:端口:用户名:密码

如果代理信息分两列（IP 与 端口），用 Excel 拼接成一列再导出：例如在新列输入公式

=A2 & ":" & B2

我只有 cookies 没有密码

勾选右侧的

I only have cookies

，并把 Cookies 下拉选择成对应列，导入后 JarveePro 会用 cookie 登录（成功率视 cookie 有效性）。

保存文件/编码提示

Windows 用户：Excel -> “另存为” -> 选择

CSV UTF-8

，或用记事本存

UTF-8

编码。

文本编辑器（Notepad++）也可用来替换分隔符、去除 BOM。

六、几个常用批量处理小技巧（Excel / 文本编辑）

在 Excel 中把代理列拼接成

socks5://IP:端口

在新列写公式（假设 IP 在 A 列，端口在 B 列）：

="socks5://" & A2 & ":" & B2

，下拉填充后复制为值再导出 CSV。

把 cookie 放在单列

如果 cookie 数据跨多列，用

=A2 & "; " & B2 & "; " & C2

拼接成一列。

去除多余空格

Excel 用

TRIM()

去空格：

=TRIM(A2)

七、快速对照表（常用映射）

你的文件里这一列示例

在界面右侧选哪个

[email protected]

或手机号/ID

Account / Email → 对应 ColumnX

abc123456

Password → 对应 ColumnX

（辅助邮箱）

Auxiliary / Secondary Email（若有此项）→ ColumnX

c_user=...; xs=...;

（cookies）

Cookies → ColumnX

socks5://1.2.3.4:1080

1.2.3.4:1080

Proxy → ColumnX

123456

（验证码）

2FA → ColumnX

长串访问令牌

Token → ColumnX

1.

Accounts: Do I Need to Buy Them Separately?

JarveePro allows you to manage multiple social media accounts, but

it does not come with pre-loaded accounts

. You will need to either create these accounts yourself or purchase them from third-party providers if you don’t want to set them up manually.

If you're just starting, here are a few options:

Create Accounts

: You can manually create these accounts yourself, giving you complete control over the details and security.

Buy Accounts

: To save time, many users opt to buy pre-set social media accounts. These accounts are usually sold by third-party vendors, but you should be cautious when selecting suppliers to ensure the accounts aren't flagged as spam. You can search

PVACreator.com

to buy accounts.

If you need to manage a large number of accounts and want to avoid the hassle of manual creation, purchasing accounts might be a more efficient option.

2.

Proxies: Do I Need to Buy Proxies Separately?

Proxies are essential for avoiding IP bans. When managing multiple accounts, social platforms can easily detect if you are operating several accounts from the same IP address, which will result in bans or restrictions.

Why Proxies Are Important?

Avoid Bans

: By rotating proxies, you can simulate accounts coming from different geographical locations, reducing the chances of getting flagged for using multiple accounts from the same IP.

Ensure Stability

: Using proxies ensures that your accounts remain safe from being blocked due to using a public IP address, especially during high-volume automation.

JarveePro

provide proxy services, you can contact them to buy proxy or purchase proxies from third-party providers.

It’s best to use

residential proxies

or

mobile proxies

, rather than regular datacenter proxies, as the latter are more likely to be blacklisted by social platforms.

3. CAPTCHA Solving Tools

When creating accounts, many platforms (like Gmail, TikTok, and Facebook) require CAPTCHA verification. Without the right CAPTCHA solving tools, your account creation process may fail or be delayed.

For example,

SadCaptcha

and

YesCaptcha

are popular CAPTCHA solving tools that can help bypass this verification process.

JarveePro

allows integration with these tools, ensuring that the automation process is not interrupted by CAPTCHA challenges.

4. Browser Fingerprint Management Tools

Browser fingerprints are a key mechanism used by platforms to identify users based on their device and behavior.

title: Post
summary: Step 1: Choose "Campaigns" and Facebook, and select posting task.
text:
Post

2025-05-17

Step 1: Choose "Campaigns" and Facebook, and select posting task.

Step 2: Select accounts and add post contents. You can import multiple pieces of content in CSV format or add them one by one.

Step 3: The account username or ID that is automatically @ed when posting.

Step 4: Select photos and videos that you want to post.

Step 5: Complete task settings and click "OK" to start.

What This Page Does:

This tab is to configure how many posts are made per Facebook account, how frequently the posts are scheduled, and whether data is reused or randomized.

If you Want Each Account to Post 500 Posts, what will you do?

Select “Number of post(s) per account”

Set it: 500 to 500

→ Each account will make exactly 500 posts.

In Select Accounts: Choose 500 Facebook accounts

In Post Content tab: Provide the post content (text, media, etc.)

In Task Settings:

Set “Account Use Interval(s)”: From 1 to 1

→ This means no delay between each account's posting action.

Explanation of Settings:

Number of post(s) per account:

Specifies how many posts each account will make.

Example: Set to 500 means each account will post 500 times.

Account Use Interval(s):

Sets the delay between actions for each account.

Example: Set to 1 to 1 means no delay between each account's posting action.

Post Story:

If checked, the post will be shared as a Facebook Story.

Post Public:

If checked, the post will be made public immediately.

Data is not reused:

Ensures that the post content is not reused across different accounts.

If unchecked, data could be reused in different accounts.

Random use of data:

If enabled, posts are shared randomly from the provided content. If unchecked, the posts will be used in the order they are provided.

Save post URL to file:

If enabled, the URLs of the posted content will be saved to a file for tracking purposes.

Real-World Example Setup for New Users:

Scenario: You want 500 accounts to each make 500 posts

In Select Accounts: Choose 500 Facebook accounts

In Post Content: Provide 500 different pieces of content (text, media)

In Task Settings:

Number of post(s) per account: 500–500

Account Use Interval(s): 1–1

Post Public: Checked

Data is not reused: Checked

Random use of data: Optional

(Optional) Enable Save post URL to file to track URLs of the posts

Post

2025-05-28

Step 1: Choose "Campaigns" and Instagram, and select posting task.

Step 2: Select account(s) and add text content(s). You can import multiple text contents in CVS format. Or you can add text content one by one.

Step 3: Add location(s) when you post the posts. You can choose import locations in CVS format or add location one by one.

Step 4: Select photo(es) or video(es).

Step 5: Complete task settings and click "OK" to start.

What This Page Does:

This section allows you to configure how many Instagram posts are made per user account, and how they are distributed across different accounts.

If You Want to Post the Same Content Multiple Times Using the Same Account, How Do You Set It Up?

Select "Number of post(s) per account":

Set it to 500. This means each account will perform 500 post tasks.

For Individual Version:

If you’re using a single TikTok account:

Set "Number of post(s) per account" from 500 to 500 (this ensures the same content is posted multiple times).

Not recommended for large-scale tasks. For scalability with multiple accounts, consider upgrading to Enterprise or Full Version.

For Full Version Users:

Uncheck "Random use of data" to ensure posts follow a specific order, which is important for structured tasks.

Check "Data is not reused" to prevent data from being reused in consecutive tasks.

If You Want to Post Using Multiple Accounts, How Should You Set It?

Keep "Number of post(s) per account" selected:

Set the range from 500 to 500(this controls the number of posts performed for each individual account).

Make Sure You Have the Following:

500 TikTok video/photo contents to post.

500 text contents and locations.

Check "Random use of data":

Enabling this ensures posts are randomized, avoiding repetitive actions and making the automation look more natural.

Check "Data is not reused" to ensure content is not reused across tasks.

Real-World Example Setup for New Users:

Scenario: Perform video posts for 10 different Instagram users using 10 separate accounts.

In Select Accounts:

Choose 10 Instagram account.

In the Select Video/photo Content Tab:

Select or import 10 video/photo contents you want to post.

In Task Settings:

Select "Number of post(s) per account": From 10 to 10 to ensure each account posts once.

Check "Random use of data" if you want to randomize the order of tasks, making the actions seem more natural and less repetitive.

Check "Data is not reused" to prevent the same content from being reused in multiple posts.

Post to Group & Page

2025-05-17

Step 1: Choose "Campaigns" and Facebook, and select "Post to Group" task.

Step 2: Select account(s) and add group URL in CVS format or one by one.

Step 3: You can import multiple pieces of content in CSV format or add them one by one.

Step 4: The account username or ID that is automatically @ed when posting.

Step 5: Select photos and videos that you want to post.

Step 6:Complete task settings and click "OK" to start.

What This Page Does:

This tab is to configure how many posts are made per Facebook account, how many posts are published on each page, and how the post data is used.

If you Want Each Account to Post 1 Post, what will you do?

Select “Number of Posts Per Account”

Set it: 1 to 1

→ Each account will post exactly one post

In Select Accounts: Choose the number of accounts you want to use

In Page URL tab: Provide your Page URL

In Post Content tab: provide your post content

Set “Number of Posts Per Page”

Set it: 500 to 500

→ This means 500 posts will be published on the page in total.

Explanation of Settings:

Number of Posts Per Account:

How many posts each account will make.

Example: Set to 1 means each account makes one post.

Number of Posts Per Page:

How many total posts will be published on the Facebook page.

Example: Set to 500 means the page will receive 500 posts.

Account Use Interval(s):

Determines the delay between actions of each account.

Example: Set to 1 to 1 means there is no delay between each account's posting action.

Data is not reused:

Ensures that the post content or data is not reused across different accounts or pages.

Random use of data:

If enabled, the post content is randomly selected. If unchecked, it is used in the order it's listed.

Save Post URL to File:

This option saves the URL of each post to a file, allowing you to track which posts have been made.

Real-World Example Setup for New Users:

Scenario: You want to make 500 posts on a page using 500 accounts

In Select Accounts: Choose 500 Facebook accounts

In Page URL tab: Provide your Page URL

In Post Content tab: provide your post content

In Task Settings:

Number of Posts Per Account: 1–1

Number of Posts Per Page: 500–500

Data is not reused: Checked

(Optional) Enable Random use of data

(Optional) Enable Save Post URL to File to keep track of the URLs of the posts

summary: Proxy Setup in JarveePro: Best Practices and Common Questions
text:
Proxy Setup in JarveePro: Best Practices and Common Questions

2025-09-16

When setting up multiple accounts in JarveePro, using the right proxy is essential. Below are the most common questions from users and their solutions.

Why can’t I log in to Instagram with free proxies?

Free proxies are often

public, unstable, or blacklisted

. Social platforms like Instagram quickly detect and block them.

Always use

dedicated or residential proxies

to ensure accounts stay safe.

How many proxies do I need for 100 accounts?

For the best safety:

1 account per proxy

→ safest option, ideal for long-term growth.

2–3 accounts per proxy

→ possible with high-quality residential proxies, but riskier.

If you’re adding

100 accounts

, plan for

100 proxies

(1:1 ratio).

Where can I buy proxies for JarveePro?

We recommend

IPFarming proxies

for account management:

Get IPFarming Proxies

They are optimized for automation and trusted by many JarveePro users.

How do I set up proxies in JarveePro?

Open

JarveePro → Accounts

Select the account you want to assign a proxy.

Enter the proxy details:

IP Address

Port

Username / Password (if required)

Click Bind

Proxy

Or got to Proxy Manager to Upload a list of proxy and auto bind to multiple accounts.

Do you have documentation/tutorial for proxy setup?

Yes A detailed step-by-step tutorial is available in iur YouTube Channel:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oUtkkv9j3Gw

Tips

Use

1 proxy per account

for maximum safety.

Avoid free proxies — they get blocked quickly.

Check proxy validity regularly inside JarveePro.

What This Page Does

This section lets you configure how many replies each tweet receives, or how many tweets each account will reply to. You can also define how data is used and whether it's reused across accounts.

If You Want One Tweet to Get 500 Replies

Select "Number of replies each tweet increases"

Set it: From 500 to 500

This means you need 500 accounts to send one reply each

Keep "Data is not reused" checked to avoid duplicate replies

Do not check "Random use of data" if you want replies to follow the input order

Ensure you have 500 reply texts ready in the "Text" tab

Make sure the tweet URL is added in the "Post URL" tab

If You Want Each Account to Reply to Different Tweets

Select "Number of tweets each account reply"

Set it: From 1 to 1

Uncheck "Data is not reused" to allow accounts to use tweet URLs or reply content more than once

Import tweet URLs in the "Post URL" tab

Enter reply content in the "Text" tab

Real-World Example

Goal: Use 500 Twitter accounts to reply once to the same tweet

In "Select Accounts": Choose 500 accounts

In "Post URL": Add the tweet URL you want to target

In "Text": Prepare 500 replies (or spintax variations)

In "Task Settings":

Select "Number of replies each tweet increases"

Set it: 500 to 500

Keep "Data is not reused" checked

Leave "Random use of data" unchecked

What This Page Does:

This tab is to configure how many reply comments are sent per Facebook comment link, from per account, and how the comment data is used.

If you Want to Reply the Same Comment to 500 Posts, what will you do?

Select “Number of Reply Comments”

Set it: From 500 to 500 (Each account will reply 500 times)

If you're using Individual Version, you may only have one Facebook account.

In this case, one account will reply 500 times — be cautious to avoid account limits or bans.

If you're a Full Version User, and you want to distribute replies across accounts:

In Select Accounts: Choose 500 Facebook accounts

In Comment Text tab: Write one reply or use spintax

In Comment Source tab: Provide 500 Facebook comment links

In Task Settings:

Select "Number of Reply Comments"

Set it: From 1 to 1 — each account replies only once

Uncheck "Data is not reused" — because you’re using the same comment for different targets

If you Want to Send Unique Replies to 500 Comments, what will you do?

Keep “Number of Reply Comments” selected

Set it: From 500 to 500

Make sure:

You have 500 different comment texts in the “Comment Text” tab

You have 500 different comment links in the “Comment Source” tab

Keep “Data is not reused” checked — to avoid duplicate replies

Real-World Example Setup for New Users:

In Select Accounts: Choose 500 Facebook accounts

In Comment Text tab: Write 1 reply or use spintax

In Comment Source tab: Add 500 Facebook comment links

Keep "Data is not reused" unchecked (since the same reply is reused)

What This Page Does:

This tab is used to configure how many Instagram accounts reply to comments on specific posts, or how many replies each account sends, based on the links you provide.

Task Execution Flow:

Number of Reply Comments Per Post

Set to: 500

Each post in your data list will receive 500 reply comments from different accounts.

✅ This option is selected in the current setup.

Account Use Interval(s)

Set to: 1 – 1

A delay of 1 second is applied between each time an account is used to perform reply actions. This helps simulate natural behavior.

✅ Currently enabled.

Random Use of Data

Unchecked

The tool will use the reply comment links in the exact order they appear in your list. This ensures structured processing.

❌ Random use of data is not selected.

Number of Post Reply Comments Per Account

Set to: 1

If this option is selected instead, each account would only reply to 1 post.

🔲 Not selected in current setup.

Example Use Case:

You want to boost engagement by making 500 accounts reply to a single comment on a post.

Provide your post links in the source tab.

Select “Number of reply comments per post”, and set it to 500.

Enable “Account Use Interval(s)” to slow down actions (1 second delay).

Leave “Random Use of Data” unchecked to ensure comments are processed in order.

title: Retry Failed Accounts in JarveePro
summary: The "Retry Failed Accounts" feature in JarveePro is designed to help users save time by not requiring them to restart a campaign from scratch when it encounters issues. This feature is especially helpful when certain accounts within a campaign fail due to errors, interruptions, or unexpected stops.
text:
Retry Failed Accounts in JarveePro

2025-10-30

The "Retry Failed Accounts" feature in JarveePro is designed to help users save time by not requiring them to restart a campaign from scratch when it encounters issues. This feature is especially helpful when certain accounts within a campaign fail due to errors, interruptions, or unexpected stops.

Here’s a breakdown of the options available when using "Retry Failed Accounts":

Duplicate Full Campaign

This option creates an exact copy of your campaign, including both the accounts that succeeded and those that failed. It’s essentially a fresh start for the entire campaign, ensuring that every aspect of the campaign is reset and retried, including successful accounts.

Copy Campaign Settings Only

This option allows you to create a brand-new campaign using the same settings (such as targets, filters, actions, etc.) as the original. It ignores the execution history, meaning the campaign starts as though it’s fresh. This is helpful if you just want to replicate the campaign's setup without the history.

Duplicate & Retry Failed Accounts

This is the most specific option. It allows the campaign to continue from where it left off, retrying only the accounts that failed. The accounts that have already succeeded will be skipped. This ensures that only the problematic accounts are retried without wasting time on those that already completed their tasks.

This feature is ideal for ongoing campaigns that might have interruptions or minor issues with specific accounts, allowing the campaign to continue smoothly without starting over.
headings: Retry Failed Accounts in JarveePro

Introduction

Keeping your social media accounts active and engaged is key to growing reach, visibility, and audience interaction. Manually tracking new posts, stories, Reels, or follower changes across multiple platforms is time-consuming and inefficient. JarveePro’s Content Explorer simplifies this process by allowing you to

scrape recent content, monitor new posts, and track new followers or followings automatically

. With this guide, you’ll learn a universal generate rule that works for

Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, YouTube

, and more — ensuring your accounts are always interacting with fresh and relevant content.

JarveePro Content Explorer

(e.g.,

Monitor_NewContent_JarveeProAdmin

).

Type

Search

→ Only track content or users.

→ Track content/users and produce posts or actions from results.

Search Source

Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, or others

→ Capture all existing content/followers/followings, then continue monitoring future updates.

→ Only capture recent posts/followers/followings to save resources.

Example:

Scrape the last 24 hours first, then continue tracking new results.

Set a range (e.g., 10–15 minutes).

Define when the task should run (e.g., 00:00–23:59).

content, followers, and followings

for your goal.

Step 3: Use Monitored Results

monitor task

as a source for campaigns, content generation, or automated engagement.

JarveePro will automatically find new posts or new followers/followings and execute the configured actions — no manual input required.

Track

only fresh content and new users

efficiently.

Keep accounts

active and relevant

across multiple platforms.

Automate content creation, engagement, or follow actions based on real-time data.

Works for

Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, YouTube

, and more.

JarveePro Content Explorer allows you to

scrape recent content and monitor new followers/followings automatically

, keeping your accounts active, engaged, and optimized for growth. By setting up a universal monitoring task, you can track Instagram, Twitter, YouTube, Facebook, and more — saving time while ensuring your accounts interact with the most relevant posts and users. With this generate rule, maintaining a consistent social media presence has never been easier.

title: Settings
summary: Click settings on the left, you can set up the Api Key, threads, size, and number of browsers on one interface.
text:
Settings

2025-05-07

Click settings on the left, you can set up the Api Key, threads, size, and number of browsers on one interface.

API Key Settings--Used to integrate various automation services, especially for CAPTCHA solving and SMS verification.

Yescaptcha Api Key--Use the YesCaptcha's service to automatically identify the verification code on the web page.

SadCaptcha Api Key--Use the SadCapcha

's service to automatically identify the verification code on the web page.

Open AI Api Key--Connects to OpenAI (like

ChatGPT

) for generating text like comments or answers.

Fingerprint Browser--(Recommended) Built-in anti-detect browser to help avoid bans and detection by social platforms. Simulates different software environments for each account.

Native Chrome--Uses your local Chrome browser, but fingerprint protection won’t work.

Number of Threads--Shows the number of browsers running simultaneously. For example, 5 means a maximum of 5 operation threads can be opened simultaneously.

Browser Size--Width × height of each simulated browser. Here is 1200 x 700 pixels.

Number of browsers in one lines--Number of browser windows. For example, 3 means that up to 3 browser windows are displayed in one row.

Data Backup Settings --Manage automatic and manual backups of your JarveePro data, including accounts, browser cache, and task settings.

Enable automatic data backup-check this box to enable automatic backups.

Backup every time the program starts: Automatically backs up once every time JarveePro is launched.

Backup every X hours: Allows interval-based backups (e.g., every 1 hour).

Accounts: Account configurations and login sessions.

Account Browser Caches: Browser cache and cookies.

Tasks: Task schedules and settings (recommended to enable).

Add Backup--Click to immediately create a snapshot of your current data.

Restore--Click the blue "Restore" button to load that specific backup (restores all selected content).

Delete--Click the red trash icon to permanently remove the selected backup file.

Yescaptcha APIKey:

Enter your SpinnerChief API key to enable automatic content spinning (rewriting text content).

Task threads (number of concurrent runs):

Sets how many automation tasks run at the same time. Example: Set to 1 means only one task will run at a time.

Account threads (Number of accounts running simultaneously):

Controls how many accounts can be active/running at once. Example: 1 = one account is active at a time.

summary: Step 1: Choose "Campaigns" and Facebook, and select task.
text:
Share Post

2025-05-17

Step 1: Choose "Campaigns" and Facebook, and select task.

Step 2: Select accounts and add URL of the post you want to share. You can import or add them one by one.

Step 3: Import your text in CSV format or add them one by one.

Step 4: Complete task settings and click "OK" to start.

What This Page Does:

This tab is to configure how many times a post is shared per account, how many times it is shared per post, and where the post is shared (feed, group, page, etc.).

If you Want Each Account to Share 1 Post, what will you do?

Select “Number Of Shares Per Account”

Set it: 1 to 1

→ Each account will share exactly one post.

In Select Accounts: Choose the number of accounts you want to use

In Share Url tab: Provide the URL of the post to be shared.

Set “Number Of Shares Per Post”

Set it: 500 to 500

→ This means 500 accounts will share the same post.

Explanation of Settings:

Number of Shares Per Account:

How many times each account will share the post.

Example: Set to 1 means each account shares the post once.

Number of Shares Per Post:

How many accounts will share the same post.

Example: Set to 500 means the post will be shared by 500 different accounts.

Account Use Interval(s):

Determines the delay between actions for each account.

Example: Set to 1 to 1 means there is no interval between each account's sharing action.

Share now(public):

If checked, the post will be shared immediately and publicly. If unchecked, the share will be scheduled.

Random use of data:

If checked, the posts to be shared will be selected randomly. If unchecked, posts will be shared in the order they are provided.

Data is not reused:

Ensures that each post or share data is used only once per task.

Share To Feed:

Select this option if you want to share the post on the Facebook feed.

Save to file:

If enabled, the URLs of the shared posts will be saved to a file, allowing you to track the posts that have been shared.

Real-World Example Setup for New Users:

Scenario: Share the same post to 500 accounts

In Select Accounts: Choose 500 Facebook accounts

In Share Url: Provide the URL of the post to be shared

In Task Settings:

Number of Shares Per Account: 1 to 1

Number of Shares Per Post: 500 to 500

Share To Feed: Selected

Data is not reused: Checked

(Optional) Enable Random use of data

(Optional) Enable Save to file to track shared posts
